The first issue: this verse is connected in meaning with what came before, the prohibition of harming the Prophet ﷺ, and he had been hurt by some of his wives. It is said that they asked him for some worldly goods. It is said that they asked for an increase in maintenance (nafaqah). It is said that they harmed him by jealousy of one another. It is said that he ﷺ was commanded to recite this verse to them and to give them the choice between the life of this world and the Hereafter. Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: whoever has a wife in his possession is not obliged to give her a choice. The Prophet ﷺ was commanded to give his wives a choice, and they chose him.

The sum of the matter is that Allah, glorified is He, gave the Prophet ﷺ a choice between being a prophet-king, to whom the keys to the treasuries of this world were offered, and being a prophet-servant living in poverty. He consulted Jibril, who advised him to choose poverty, and he chose it. When he chose it, which is the higher of the two ranks, Allah, mighty and majestic, commanded him to give his wives a choice, for some of them might dislike remaining with him under hardship. This was to keep him free from such (burdens). It is also said that the reason which made the giving of choice necessary was that one of his wives asked him to make her a ring of gold. He made her a ring of silver and coated it with gold (some say with saffron), but she refused except that it be of gold. Then the verse of choice was revealed, he gave them the choice, and they said: "We choose Allah and His Messenger." It is also said that one of them chose separation. And Allah knows best.

Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated, and the wording is Muslim's, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: Abu Bakr came asking permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he found people sitting at his door, none of whom had been given permission. He said: Abu Bakr was given permission and entered. Then 'Umar came and asked permission, and he was given permission. He found the Prophet ﷺ sitting around him with his wives, silent and downcast. He said: "By Allah, I will say something that will make the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laugh." So he said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you had seen the daughter of Kharijah, she asked me for maintenance, so I got up to her and struck her neck." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed and said: "They are around me as you see, asking me for maintenance." Then Abu Bakr got up to 'A'ishah and struck her neck, and 'Umar got up to Hafsah and struck her neck, both saying: "You ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for what he does not have!" They said: "By Allah, we will never ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for anything he does not have." Then he withdrew from them for a month, or twenty-nine days. Then this verse was revealed to him: "O Prophet, say to your wives..." until "...for those of you who do good, a great reward." He said: So he began with 'A'ishah and said: "O 'A'ishah, I want to present to you a matter, and I love that you not hasten in it until you consult your parents." She said: "What is it, O Messenger of Allah?" So he recited the verse to her. She said: "Am I to consult my parents about you, O Messenger of Allah? Rather I choose Allah, His Messenger, and the Hereafter. And I ask you not to tell any of your wives what I have said." He said: "None of them asks me but I tell her. Indeed Allah did not send me as one who causes difficulty, nor as one who seeks to cause difficulty, but He sent me as a teacher, one who makes things easy."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was commanded to give his wives a choice, and he began with me and said: "O 'A'ishah, I am going to mention to you a matter, and there is no harm if you do not hasten until you consult your parents." She said: He knew that my parents would never have commanded me to separate from him. She said: Then he said: "Indeed Allah says: 'O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you with a fair release... until...' 'for those of you who do good, a great reward.'" I said: "Am I to consult my parents about this? Indeed I desire Allah, His Messenger, and the Hereafter." The wives of the Prophet ﷺ did the same as I did. He said: This is a hadith that is hasan sahih (good and authentic). The scholars said: As for the Prophet ﷺ commanding 'A'ishah to consult her parents, it was because he loved her, and he feared that the excess of youth might lead her to choose separation from him, and he knew from her parents that they would not advise her to leave him.

The second issue: His saying, exalted is He, "Say to your wives" (qul li-azwajika). The Prophet ﷺ had wives. Some of them he had consummated the marriage with, some he had contracted marriage with but had not consummated it, and some he had proposed to but did not complete the marriage with. The first of them was Khadijah bint Khuwaylid ibn Asad ibn 'Abd al-'Uzza ibn Qusayy ibn Kilab. She had previously been married to Abu Halah [in the books of the Companions there are sayings about who came before], whose name was Zurarah ibn al-Nabbash al-Asadi, and before him she had been married to 'Atiq ibn 'A'idh, by whom she bore a boy named 'Abd Manaf. From Abu Halah she bore Hind ibn Abi Halah, who lived until the time of the plague and died in it. It is said that the one who lived until the time of the plague was Hind ibn Hind, and his mourner was heard, when he died, saying: "Oh Hind ibn Hind! Oh stepson of the Messenger of Allah!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not marry anyone else over Khadijah until she died. On the day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her, she was forty years old. She died after seven years of prophethood had passed, and it is said ten. It is also said that at her death she was sixty-five years old. She was the first woman to believe in him. All his children, except Ibrahim, were from her. Hakim ibn Hizam said: Khadijah died, and we carried her out from her house until we buried her at al-Hajun. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went down into her grave, and at that time the sunnah of the funeral prayer for her had not yet been established.

Among them was Sawdah bint Zam'ah ibn Qays ibn 'Abd Shams al-'Amiriyyah. She embraced Islam early and gave the pledge. She had been married to a paternal cousin of hers called al-Sakran ibn 'Amr, who also embraced Islam, and they both migrated together to the land of Abyssinia in the second migration. When they returned to Makkah, her husband died. It is said he died in Abyssinia. When her waiting period ended, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ proposed to her, married her, consummated the marriage with her in Makkah, and migrated with her to Madinah. When she grew old, he wished to divorce her, but she asked him not to do so and to keep her among his wives, and she gave her night to 'A'ishah, as is mentioned in the Sahih. So he kept her. She died in Madinah in Shawwal, in the year fifty-four.

Among them was 'A'ishah bint Abi Bakr al-Siddiq. She had been promised to Jubayr ibn Mut'im. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ proposed to her, and Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, leave it to me to withdraw her from Jubayr gently." He married her in Makkah two years before the Hijrah, and it is said three years. He consummated the marriage with her in Madinah when she was nine. She remained with him for nine years. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died when she was eighteen. He married no virgin other than her. She died in the year fifty-nine, and it is said fifty-eight.

Among them was Hafsah bint 'Umar ibn al-Khattab al-Qurashiyyah al-'Adawiyyah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her and then divorced her. Jibril came to him and said: "Indeed Allah commands you to take back Hafsah, for she is one who fasts much and stands in prayer much." So he took her back. Al-Waqidi said: She died in Sha'ban in the year forty-five, in the caliphate of Mu'awiyah, and she was sixty years old. It is said she died in the caliphate of 'Uthman in Madinah.

Among them was Umm Salamah, whose name was Hind bint Abi Umayyah al-Makhzumiyyah, and the name of Abu Umayyah was Suhayl. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her in the last nights of Shawwal in the year four. Her son Salamah gave her in marriage to him, according to the correct view, and her son was young. She died in the year fifty-nine. It is also said in the year sixty-two, and the first is more correct. Sa'id ibn Zayd led the funeral prayer over her, and it is said Abu Hurayrah did. She was buried in al-Baqi' at the age of eighty-four.

Among them was Umm Habibah, whose name was Ramlah bint Abi Sufyan. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent 'Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri to the Negus to propose to Umm Habibah on his behalf, and he married her to him. That was in the year seven after the Hijrah. The Negus paid the dowry on behalf of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, four hundred dinars, and sent her to him with Shurahbil ibn Hasanah. She died in the year forty-four. Al-Daraqutni said: Umm Habibah had been married to 'Ubayd Allah ibn Jahsh, and he died in the land of Abyssinia as a Christian. Then the Negus married her to the Prophet ﷺ and paid her dowry on his behalf, four thousand, and sent her to him with Shurahbil ibn Hasanah.

Among them was Zaynab bint Jahsh ibn Ri'ab al-Asadiyyah. Her name had been Barrah, and the Prophet ﷺ named her Zaynab. The name of her father was Barrah, so she said: "O Messenger of Allah, change my father's name, for Barrah is contemptible." The Prophet ﷺ said to her: "If your father had been a believer, we would have named him after a man from among us, the people of the household. But I have named him Jahsh, and the jahsh is from the barrah." Al-Daraqutni mentioned this hadith. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her in Madinah in the year five after the Hijrah, and she died in the year twenty, at the age of fifty-three.

Among them was Zaynab bint Khuzaymah ibn al-Harith [ibn 'Abd Allah] ibn 'Amr ibn 'Abd Manaf ibn Hilal ibn 'Amir ibn Sa'sa'ah al-Hilaliyyah. In the Jahiliyyah she was called Umm al-Masakin, because of her feeding the needy. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her in Ramadan, at the end of thirty-one months after the Hijrah. She remained with him eight months, and she died during his lifetime, at the end of Rabi' al-Awwal, at the end of thirty-nine months, and she was buried in al-Baqi'.

Among them was Juwayriyah bint al-Harith ibn Abi Dirar al-Khuza'iyyah al-Mustaliqiyyah. He took her in the expedition of Bani al-Mustaliq, and she fell to the lot of Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who made a contract of manumission (kitabah) with her. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ paid her manumission and married her, and that was in Sha'ban of the year six. Her name had been Barrah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ named her Juwayriyah. She died in Rabi' al-Awwal in the year fifty-six. It is said in the year fifty, at the age of sixty-five.

Among them was Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Harunivyah. The Prophet ﷺ took her captive on the day of Khaybar and chose her for himself. She embraced Islam, and he freed her and made her freedom her dowry. In the Sahih it is reported that she fell to the lot of Dihyah al-Kalbi, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bought her for seven heads. She died in the year fifty. It is also said in the year fifty-two, and she was buried in al-Baqi'.

Among them was Rayhanah bint Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Khunafah from Bani al-Nadir. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took her captive and freed her, and he married her in the year six. She died on his return from the Farewell Pilgrimage, and he buried her in al-Baqi'. Al-Waqidi said: She died in the year sixteen, and 'Umar prayed over her. Abu al-Faraj al-Jawzi said: I have heard someone say that he used to have intercourse with her by right of ownership (bi-milk al-yamin) and did not free her. I say: And for this reason, Allah knows best, Abu al-Qasim 'Abd al-Rahman al-Suhayli did not mention her among the wives of the Prophet ﷺ.

Among them was Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyyah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her at Sarif, ten miles from Makkah, in the year seven after the Hijrah, during the 'Umrat al-Qada'. She was the last woman the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married, and Allah, exalted is He, decreed that she would die in the place where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had built (a tent).

and was buried there, and that was in the year 61. It was also said: 63. And it was said: 68. These are the well-known wives of the Prophet ﷺ, those with whom he consummated marriage, may Allah be pleased with them all. As for those whom he married but did not consummate the marriage with, among them is al-Kilabiyya. They differed about her name: it was said Fatima, it was said Amra, and it was said al-'Aliya. Al-Zuhri said: He married Fatima bint al-Dahhak al-Kilabiyya, and she sought refuge from him, so he divorced her, and she used to say: "I am the wretched one." He married her in Dhu al-Qa'da in the eighth year after the Hijra, and she died in the year 60. Among them is Asma' bint al-Nu'man ibn al-Jawn ibn al-Harith al-Kindiyya, who is al-Jawniyya. Qatada said: When he entered upon her, he called her, and she said: "Come, you," so he divorced her. Others said: She is the one who sought refuge from him. In al-Bukhari it says: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Umayma bint Sharahil, and when she was brought in to him he extended his hand toward her, and it seemed she disliked that, so he commanded Abu Usayd to prepare her and clothe her in two garments. In another wording, Abu Usayd said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought al-Jawniyya, and when he entered upon her he said: "Give yourself to me." She said: "Does a queen give herself to a commoner?" He reached out his hand to place it on her to calm her, and she said: "I seek refuge in Allah from you!" He said: "You have sought refuge in One who grants refuge." Then he went out to us and said: "O Abu Usayd, clothe her in two garments of razqi [[The phrase (razqiyyayn) is in the dual, an adjective of an omitted noun, known from context. In another narration (razqiyyatayn). Al-raziqiyya: garments of white, long cloth.]] and return her to her people." Among them is Qutayla bint Qays, sister of al-Ash'ath ibn Qays; al-Ash'ath married her to him, then he departed to Hadramawt, and he took her with him there, when news of the death of the Prophet ﷺ reached him. He sent her back to her land, and he apostatized, and she apostatized with him. Then Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl married her, and Abu Bakr was greatly grieved over this. Umar said to him: "By Allah, she is not one of his wives; he did not give her a choice nor veil her." And Allah cleared her of him through apostasy [[As it appears in the manuscripts and Usd al-Ghaba, its wording is: (And Allah cleared her by apostasy). What is in Sharh al-Mawahib is: (... and she apostatized with her brother, so she was disavowed by Allah and His Messenger, etc.).]]. Urwa used to deny that he had married her. Among them is Umm Sharik al-Azdiyya, whose name is Ghuzayya bint Jabir ibn Hakim [[In al-Mawahib: (Jabir ibn Awf).]], and she had been before him with Abu Bakr ibn Abi Salma, and the Prophet ﷺ divorced her without consummating. She is the one who gave herself. It was also said: the one who gave herself to the Prophet ﷺ was Khawla bint Hakim. Among them: Khawla bint al-Hudhayl ibn Hubayra, whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married, but she died before reaching him. Among them: Sharaf bint Khalifa, sister of Dihya, whom he married but did not consummate. Among them Layla bint al-Khatim, sister of Qays; he married her, and she was very jealous, so she asked him to release her, and he released her. Among them: Amra bint Mu'awiya al-Kindiyya, whom the Prophet ﷺ married. Al-Sha'bi said: He married a woman from Kinda, and she was brought to him after he had died. Among them: the daughter of Jundub ibn Damra al-Jundaʿiyya. Some said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her, and some denied that this occurred. Among them: the Ghifariyya. Some said: He married a woman from Ghifar, and he commanded her, so she removed her garments, and he saw whiteness, so he said: "Go back to your people." It is said: he only saw the whiteness in the Kilabiyya. These are those whom he contracted with and did not consummate, ﷺ. As for those who proposed to them but the marriage was not completed with them, and those who gave themselves to him: among them is Umm Hani bint Abi Talib, whose name is Fakhita. The Prophet ﷺ proposed to her, and she said: "I am a woman with children [[i.e., having children.]]," and she excused herself to him, and he accepted her excuse. Among them: Dubaa'a bint 'Amir. Among them: Safiyya bint Bashama ibn Nadla, whom the Prophet ﷺ proposed to, and she had been taken as captive; the Prophet ﷺ gave her a choice, saying: "If you wish, I, and if you wish, your husband?" She said: "My husband." So he released her, and the Banu Tamim cursed her, as reported by Ibn Abbas. Among them: Umm Sharik, whose mention has already passed. Among them: Layla bint al-Khatim, whose mention has already passed. Among them: Khawla bint Hakim ibn Umayya, who gave herself to the Prophet ﷺ, and he deferred her, so Uthman ibn Maz'un married her. Among them: Jamra bint al-Harith ibn Awf al-Murri, whom the Prophet ﷺ proposed to, and her father said: "There is a defect in her," though there was none in her, so her father returned to her and she had become leprous; she is the mother of Shabib ibn al-Barsa' the poet. Among them: Sawda al-Qurashiyya, whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ proposed to, and she had children. She said: "I fear that my children will cry out near your head." So he praised her and supplicated for her. Among them: a woman whose name is not mentioned. Mujahid said: A woman proposed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and she said: "I will consult my father." Then she met her father, and he permitted her, so she met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "We have already wrapped ourselves in a blanket other than you." These are all the wives of the Prophet ﷺ. He had two concubines from among the slave-women: Mariya the Copt, and Rayhana, according to Qatada. Others said: He had four: Mariya, Rayhana, another beautiful one whom he took in captivity, and a slave-girl whom Zaynab bint Jahsh gave him.

**Third:** The words of Allah the Exalted, "If you desire the worldly life and its adornment" (33:28). "In" is a conditional particle, and its response is "then come" (*fa-ta'alayna*). Thus He made the choice contingent upon a condition. This shows that a conditional choice (*takhyir*) and a conditional divorce (*talaq*) are both valid, and both take effect and stand. This is contrary to the ignorant innovators who claim that if a man says to his wife, "You are divorced if you enter the house," the divorce does not take effect if she enters the house, because lawful divorce (*talaq shar'i*) is only that which is immediate, with no condition.

**Fourth:** The words "then come" (*fa-ta'alayna*) are the response to the condition. It is a verb addressed to the group of women, derived from your saying *ta'ala* ("come"). It is a summons to approach. It is said *ta'ala* meaning *aqbil* ("come forward"). It was originally used for one who has majesty and rank, and then in usage it came to be used for anyone who summons another to approach. In this place, however, it retains its original sense, since the one summoning is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). "I will provide for you" (*umatti'kunna*): the discussion of *mut'ah* (provision upon divorce) has already passed in *al-Baqarah* (see vol. 3, p. 200 ff.). It has also been read as *umat'ikunna* with a *damma* on the *ʿayn*. Likewise, "and release you" (*wa-usarrihkunna*) is read with a *damma* on the *ḥa'* as a new, independent sentence. "Fair release" (*sarah jamil*) is divorce in accordance with the Sunnah, without harm and without withholding what is due to her.

**Fifth:** The scholars differed over the manner in which the Prophet (ﷺ) gave his wives the choice, in two opinions.

The first: he gave them the choice, by the permission of Allah, between remaining married or being divorced, and they chose to remain. This was said by ʿĀʾishah, Mujahid, ʿIkrimah, al-Shaʿbi, Ibn Shihab, and Rabiʿah. Some of them said: he only gave them the choice between the world, in which case he would separate from them, and the Hereafter, in which case he would keep them, so that they would have the higher station that they had with their husband. He did not give them the choice of divorce. This was mentioned by al-Hasan and Qatadah. From among the Companions, ʿAli reported, through Ahmad ibn Hanbal, that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave his wives a choice only between this world and the Hereafter."

I say: The first opinion is more correct, based on the statement of ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), when she was asked about a man who gives his wife a choice: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave us a choice, so was that a divorce?" In another narration: "We chose him, and he did not count it as a divorce against us." Nothing has been established from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) except the choice commanded between remaining and divorce. For this reason he said: "O ʿĀʾishah, I am going to mention a matter to you, and there is no harm in your not hastening in it until you consult your two parents." This is the hadith. It is well known that he did not intend consultation in choosing the world and its adornment over the Hereafter. Thus it is established that consultation occurred only concerning separation or remaining married. And Allah knows best.

**Sixth:** The scholars differed concerning the woman given the choice who chooses her husband. The majority of scholars among the early generations and others, and the leading jurists of fatwa, said: no divorce is binding upon him, neither one nor more. This is the view of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, ʿAli, Ibn Masʿud, Zayd ibn Thabit, Ibn ʿAbbas, and ʿĀʾishah. Among the Successors are ʿAta', Masruq, Sulayman ibn Yasar, Rabiʿah, and Ibn Shihab. It was also reported from ʿAli and Zayd that if she chooses her husband, it is one irrevocable (*ba'in*) divorce. This is the view of al-Hasan al-Basri and al-Layth, and al-Khattabi and al-Naqqash related it from Malik. They relied on the argument that his saying "choose" (*ikhtari*) is an allusive expression (*kinayah*) for pronouncing divorce, so when he attributes it to her, it takes effect as one pronouncement, like his saying "You are irrevocably divorced."

The sound view is the first, based on the statement of ʿĀʾishah: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave us a choice, so we chose him, and he did not count it against us as a divorce." It was recorded by the two Sahihs. Ibn al-Mundhir said: The hadith of ʿĀʾishah indicates that if the woman given the choice chooses her husband, that is not a divorce. It also indicates that her choosing herself causes a divorce, and it indicates a third meaning: that if the woman given the choice chooses herself, it is a single pronouncement over which her husband retains the right of return (*raj'ah*), since it is impermissible for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to divorce contrary to what Allah commanded him. This was reported from ʿUmar, Ibn Masʿud, and Ibn ʿAbbas. Ibn Abi Layla, al-Thawri, and al-Shafiʿi also said so. It was reported from ʿAli that if she chooses herself, it is one irrevocable divorce. This is the view of Abu Hanifah and his companions. Ibn Khuwayz Mandad related it from Malik. It was reported from Zayd ibn Thabit that if she chooses herself, it is three divorces. This is the view of al-Hasan al-Basri, and Malik and al-Layth also said so, because ownership (*al-milk*) is only effected by that. It was reported from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, that if she chooses herself, it is nothing. It was also reported from him that if she chooses her husband, it is one revocable (*raj'i*) divorce.

**Seventh:** A group of Medinese scholars and others held that delegation of divorce (*tamlik*) and the choice (*takhyir*) are the same, and that the judgment is whatever she decides in both. This is the view of ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Abi Salamah. Ibn Shaʿban said: Many of our companions have chosen this, and it is the view of a group of the people of Medina. Abu ʿUmar (Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr) said: The majority of jurists hold this view.

The well-known position of the school of Malik is that there is a difference between them. The delegation (*tamlik*), according to Malik, is a man's saying to his wife, "I have delegated to you," meaning: I have delegated to you what Allah has given me of divorce, whether one, two, or three. Since it is permissible for him to delegate part of it to her and not all of it, and he claims that, the statement is her statement with her oath if he disputes it. A group of the people of Medina said: he has the right to dispute in both delegation and choice equally, in the case of a woman who has been consummated with. The first is the well-known view of Malik. Ibn Khuwayz Mandad related from Malik that the husband may dispute with the woman given the choice regarding three, and it would be one irrevocable divorce, as Abu Hanifah said. Abu al-Jahm also said so. Sahnun said: most of our companions hold this view.

The summary of the position of Malik is: if the woman given the choice chooses herself, and she has been consummated with, then it is the full divorce, and if her husband denies it, he has no right of denial. If she chooses one divorce, it is nothing; rather the choice is absolute: either she takes it or leaves it, because the meaning of the choice is release (*tasrih*). Allah the Exalted said in the verse of choice: "Then come, I will provide for you and release you with a fair release" (33:28). So the meaning of release is absolute separation. Allah the Exalted said: "Divorce is twice; then either retention in kindness or release with good treatment" (2:229). Release with good treatment is the third pronouncement, as was reported from the Prophet (ﷺ), as mentioned earlier. From the perspective of meaning: his saying "choose me" or "choose yourself" requires that he has no authority over her if she chooses herself, and he owns nothing of her, since he has made it up to her to remove from him what he owns or to remain with him if she chooses him. So if she chooses part of the divorce, she has not acted according to the implication of the wording, and she is in the position of one who was given a choice between two things and chose something other than them.

As for the woman who has not been consummated with, he has the right to dispute her in the choice and delegation if she claims more than one, because she is separated immediately.

**Eighth:** The narration from Malik has differed as to when she has the option. Once he said: she has the option as long as she is in the session, before rising or engaging in something that indicates turning away. If she does not choose and does not decide anything until they separate from their session, then what was in her hands is void. This is the view of most jurists. Another time he said: she has the option forever, as long as it is not known that she has abandoned it. That is known by her allowing him access to herself by intercourse or intimate contact. In that case, if she prevents him from herself and does not choose anything, he has the right to bring her before the judge so that she either decides or drops it. If she refuses, the judge cancels her delegation.

According to the first view, if she engages in something other than that, such as speech, action, walking, or anything that is not related to the choice, as we have mentioned, her choice lapses. Some of our companions argued for this view with the words of Allah the Exalted: "So do not sit with them until they engage in a different conversation" (4:140). Also, the husband spoke to her in general terms so that she would know the choice from her, so it became like a contract between them. If she accepts it, it stands; otherwise it lapses, like one who says, "I have given you as a gift" or "I have sold to you": if the other accepts, it stands; otherwise the ownership remains as it was. This is the view of al-Thawri, the Kufans, al-Awza'i, al-Layth, al-Shafiʿi, and Abu Thawr, and it is the preference of Ibn al-Qasim.

The reasoning of the second narration is that the matter has come into her hand, and she has come to own it over her husband through his delegating it to her. Since she owns it, it must remain in her hand just as it remains in the hand of her husband.

I say: This is the sound view, based on the statement of the Prophet (peace be upon him) to ʿĀʾishah: "I am going to mention a matter to you, and there is no harm in your not hastening until you consult your two parents." It was narrated by the Sahih, and al-Bukhari recorded it, and al-Tirmidhi authenticated it. It has been mentioned earlier at the beginning of the chapter. It is evidence for the one who says that if a man gives his wife a choice or delegates it to her, she may decide regarding it even if they separate from their session. This was reported from al-Hasan and al-Zuhri, and Malik said it in one of his two narrations.

Abu ʿUbayd said: What we hold in this matter is following the Sunnah concerning ʿĀʾishah in this hadith, when he gave her the choice until she consulted her parents, and he did not make her standing up from her session an exit from the matter. Al-Marwazi said: This is the most correct of the opinions in my view, and Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tahawi also said it.

The first issue: this verse is connected in meaning with what came before, the prohibition of harming the Prophet ﷺ, and he had been hurt by some of his wives. It is said that they asked him for some worldly goods. It is said that they asked for an increase in maintenance (nafaqah). It is said that they harmed him by jealousy of one another. It is said that he ﷺ was commanded to recite this verse to them and to give them the choice between the life of this world and the Hereafter. Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: whoever has a wife in his possession is not obliged to give her a choice. The Prophet ﷺ was commanded to give his wives a choice, and they chose him.

The sum of the matter is that Allah, glorified is He, gave the Prophet ﷺ a choice between being a prophet-king, to whom the keys to the treasuries of this world were offered, and being a prophet-servant living in poverty. He consulted Jibril, who advised him to choose poverty, and he chose it. When he chose it, which is the higher of the two ranks, Allah, mighty and majestic, commanded him to give his wives a choice, for some of them might dislike remaining with him under hardship. This was to keep him free from such (burdens). It is also said that the reason which made the giving of choice necessary was that one of his wives asked him to make her a ring of gold. He made her a ring of silver and coated it with gold (some say with saffron), but she refused except that it be of gold. Then the verse of choice was revealed, he gave them the choice, and they said: "We choose Allah and His Messenger." It is also said that one of them chose separation. And Allah knows best.

Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated, and the wording is Muslim's, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: Abu Bakr came asking permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he found people sitting at his door, none of whom had been given permission. He said: Abu Bakr was given permission and entered. Then 'Umar came and asked permission, and he was given permission. He found the Prophet ﷺ sitting around him with his wives, silent and downcast. He said: "By Allah, I will say something that will make the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laugh." So he said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you had seen the daughter of Kharijah, she asked me for maintenance, so I got up to her and struck her neck." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed and said: "They are around me as you see, asking me for maintenance." Then Abu Bakr got up to 'A'ishah and struck her neck, and 'Umar got up to Hafsah and struck her neck, both saying: "You ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for what he does not have!" They said: "By Allah, we will never ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for anything he does not have." Then he withdrew from them for a month, or twenty-nine days. Then this verse was revealed to him: "O Prophet, say to your wives..." until "...for those of you who do good, a great reward." He said: So he began with 'A'ishah and said: "O 'A'ishah, I want to present to you a matter, and I love that you not hasten in it until you consult your parents." She said: "What is it, O Messenger of Allah?" So he recited the verse to her. She said: "Am I to consult my parents about you, O Messenger of Allah? Rather I choose Allah, His Messenger, and the Hereafter. And I ask you not to tell any of your wives what I have said." He said: "None of them asks me but I tell her. Indeed Allah did not send me as one who causes difficulty, nor as one who seeks to cause difficulty, but He sent me as a teacher, one who makes things easy."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was commanded to give his wives a choice, and he began with me and said: "O 'A'ishah, I am going to mention to you a matter, and there is no harm if you do not hasten until you consult your parents." She said: He knew that my parents would never have commanded me to separate from him. She said: Then he said: "Indeed Allah says: 'O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you with a fair release... until...' 'for those of you who do good, a great reward.'" I said: "Am I to consult my parents about this? Indeed I desire Allah, His Messenger, and the Hereafter." The wives of the Prophet ﷺ did the same as I did. He said: This is a hadith that is hasan sahih (good and authentic). The scholars said: As for the Prophet ﷺ commanding 'A'ishah to consult her parents, it was because he loved her, and he feared that the excess of youth might lead her to choose separation from him, and he knew from her parents that they would not advise her to leave him.

The second issue: His saying, exalted is He, "Say to your wives" (qul li-azwajika). The Prophet ﷺ had wives. Some of them he had consummated the marriage with, some he had contracted marriage with but had not consummated it, and some he had proposed to but did not complete the marriage with. The first of them was Khadijah bint Khuwaylid ibn Asad ibn 'Abd al-'Uzza ibn Qusayy ibn Kilab. She had previously been married to Abu Halah [in the books of the Companions there are sayings about who came before], whose name was Zurarah ibn al-Nabbash al-Asadi, and before him she had been married to 'Atiq ibn 'A'idh, by whom she bore a boy named 'Abd Manaf. From Abu Halah she bore Hind ibn Abi Halah, who lived until the time of the plague and died in it. It is said that the one who lived until the time of the plague was Hind ibn Hind, and his mourner was heard, when he died, saying: "Oh Hind ibn Hind! Oh stepson of the Messenger of Allah!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not marry anyone else over Khadijah until she died. On the day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her, she was forty years old. She died after seven years of prophethood had passed, and it is said ten. It is also said that at her death she was sixty-five years old. She was the first woman to believe in him. All his children, except Ibrahim, were from her. Hakim ibn Hizam said: Khadijah died, and we carried her out from her house until we buried her at al-Hajun. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went down into her grave, and at that time the sunnah of the funeral prayer for her had not yet been established.

Among them was Sawdah bint Zam'ah ibn Qays ibn 'Abd Shams al-'Amiriyyah. She embraced Islam early and gave the pledge. She had been married to a paternal cousin of hers called al-Sakran ibn 'Amr, who also embraced Islam, and they both migrated together to the land of Abyssinia in the second migration. When they returned to Makkah, her husband died. It is said he died in Abyssinia. When her waiting period ended, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ proposed to her, married her, consummated the marriage with her in Makkah, and migrated with her to Madinah. When she grew old, he wished to divorce her, but she asked him not to do so and to keep her among his wives, and she gave her night to 'A'ishah, as is mentioned in the Sahih. So he kept her. She died in Madinah in Shawwal, in the year fifty-four.

Among them was 'A'ishah bint Abi Bakr al-Siddiq. She had been promised to Jubayr ibn Mut'im. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ proposed to her, and Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, leave it to me to withdraw her from Jubayr gently." He married her in Makkah two years before the Hijrah, and it is said three years. He consummated the marriage with her in Madinah when she was nine. She remained with him for nine years. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died when she was eighteen. He married no virgin other than her. She died in the year fifty-nine, and it is said fifty-eight.

Among them was Hafsah bint 'Umar ibn al-Khattab al-Qurashiyyah al-'Adawiyyah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her and then divorced her. Jibril came to him and said: "Indeed Allah commands you to take back Hafsah, for she is one who fasts much and stands in prayer much." So he took her back. Al-Waqidi said: She died in Sha'ban in the year forty-five, in the caliphate of Mu'awiyah, and she was sixty years old. It is said she died in the caliphate of 'Uthman in Madinah.

Among them was Umm Salamah, whose name was Hind bint Abi Umayyah al-Makhzumiyyah, and the name of Abu Umayyah was Suhayl. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her in the last nights of Shawwal in the year four. Her son Salamah gave her in marriage to him, according to the correct view, and her son was young. She died in the year fifty-nine. It is also said in the year sixty-two, and the first is more correct. Sa'id ibn Zayd led the funeral prayer over her, and it is said Abu Hurayrah did. She was buried in al-Baqi' at the age of eighty-four.

Among them was Umm Habibah, whose name was Ramlah bint Abi Sufyan. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent 'Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri to the Negus to propose to Umm Habibah on his behalf, and he married her to him. That was in the year seven after the Hijrah. The Negus paid the dowry on behalf of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, four hundred dinars, and sent her to him with Shurahbil ibn Hasanah. She died in the year forty-four. Al-Daraqutni said: Umm Habibah had been married to 'Ubayd Allah ibn Jahsh, and he died in the land of Abyssinia as a Christian. Then the Negus married her to the Prophet ﷺ and paid her dowry on his behalf, four thousand, and sent her to him with Shurahbil ibn Hasanah.

Among them was Zaynab bint Jahsh ibn Ri'ab al-Asadiyyah. Her name had been Barrah, and the Prophet ﷺ named her Zaynab. The name of her father was Barrah, so she said: "O Messenger of Allah, change my father's name, for Barrah is contemptible." The Prophet ﷺ said to her: "If your father had been a believer, we would have named him after a man from among us, the people of the household. But I have named him Jahsh, and the jahsh is from the barrah." Al-Daraqutni mentioned this hadith. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her in Madinah in the year five after the Hijrah, and she died in the year twenty, at the age of fifty-three.

Among them was Zaynab bint Khuzaymah ibn al-Harith [ibn 'Abd Allah] ibn 'Amr ibn 'Abd Manaf ibn Hilal ibn 'Amir ibn Sa'sa'ah al-Hilaliyyah. In the Jahiliyyah she was called Umm al-Masakin, because of her feeding the needy. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her in Ramadan, at the end of thirty-one months after the Hijrah. She remained with him eight months, and she died during his lifetime, at the end of Rabi' al-Awwal, at the end of thirty-nine months, and she was buried in al-Baqi'.

Among them was Juwayriyah bint al-Harith ibn Abi Dirar al-Khuza'iyyah al-Mustaliqiyyah. He took her in the expedition of Bani al-Mustaliq, and she fell to the lot of Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who made a contract of manumission (kitabah) with her. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ paid her manumission and married her, and that was in Sha'ban of the year six. Her name had been Barrah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ named her Juwayriyah. She died in Rabi' al-Awwal in the year fifty-six. It is said in the year fifty, at the age of sixty-five.

Among them was Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Harunivyah. The Prophet ﷺ took her captive on the day of Khaybar and chose her for himself. She embraced Islam, and he freed her and made her freedom her dowry. In the Sahih it is reported that she fell to the lot of Dihyah al-Kalbi, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bought her for seven heads. She died in the year fifty. It is also said in the year fifty-two, and she was buried in al-Baqi'.

Among them was Rayhanah bint Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Khunafah from Bani al-Nadir. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took her captive and freed her, and he married her in the year six. She died on his return from the Farewell Pilgrimage, and he buried her in al-Baqi'. Al-Waqidi said: She died in the year sixteen, and 'Umar prayed over her. Abu al-Faraj al-Jawzi said: I have heard someone say that he used to have intercourse with her by right of ownership (bi-milk al-yamin) and did not free her. I say: And for this reason, Allah knows best, Abu al-Qasim 'Abd al-Rahman al-Suhayli did not mention her among the wives of the Prophet ﷺ.

Among them was Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyyah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her at Sarif, ten miles from Makkah, in the year seven after the Hijrah, during the 'Umrat al-Qada'. She was the last woman the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married, and Allah, exalted is He, decreed that she would die in the place where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had built (a tent).

and was buried there, and that was in the year 61. It was also said: 63. And it was said: 68. These are the well-known wives of the Prophet ﷺ, those with whom he consummated marriage, may Allah be pleased with them all. As for those whom he married but did not consummate the marriage with, among them is al-Kilabiyya. They differed about her name: it was said Fatima, it was said Amra, and it was said al-'Aliya. Al-Zuhri said: He married Fatima bint al-Dahhak al-Kilabiyya, and she sought refuge from him, so he divorced her, and she used to say: "I am the wretched one." He married her in Dhu al-Qa'da in the eighth year after the Hijra, and she died in the year 60. Among them is Asma' bint al-Nu'man ibn al-Jawn ibn al-Harith al-Kindiyya, who is al-Jawniyya. Qatada said: When he entered upon her, he called her, and she said: "Come, you," so he divorced her. Others said: She is the one who sought refuge from him. In al-Bukhari it says: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Umayma bint Sharahil, and when she was brought in to him he extended his hand toward her, and it seemed she disliked that, so he commanded Abu Usayd to prepare her and clothe her in two garments. In another wording, Abu Usayd said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought al-Jawniyya, and when he entered upon her he said: "Give yourself to me." She said: "Does a queen give herself to a commoner?" He reached out his hand to place it on her to calm her, and she said: "I seek refuge in Allah from you!" He said: "You have sought refuge in One who grants refuge." Then he went out to us and said: "O Abu Usayd, clothe her in two garments of razqi [[The phrase (razqiyyayn) is in the dual, an adjective of an omitted noun, known from context. In another narration (razqiyyatayn). Al-raziqiyya: garments of white, long cloth.]] and return her to her people." Among them is Qutayla bint Qays, sister of al-Ash'ath ibn Qays; al-Ash'ath married her to him, then he departed to Hadramawt, and he took her with him there, when news of the death of the Prophet ﷺ reached him. He sent her back to her land, and he apostatized, and she apostatized with him. Then Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl married her, and Abu Bakr was greatly grieved over this. Umar said to him: "By Allah, she is not one of his wives; he did not give her a choice nor veil her." And Allah cleared her of him through apostasy [[As it appears in the manuscripts and Usd al-Ghaba, its wording is: (And Allah cleared her by apostasy). What is in Sharh al-Mawahib is: (... and she apostatized with her brother, so she was disavowed by Allah and His Messenger, etc.).]]. Urwa used to deny that he had married her. Among them is Umm Sharik al-Azdiyya, whose name is Ghuzayya bint Jabir ibn Hakim [[In al-Mawahib: (Jabir ibn Awf).]], and she had been before him with Abu Bakr ibn Abi Salma, and the Prophet ﷺ divorced her without consummating. She is the one who gave herself. It was also said: the one who gave herself to the Prophet ﷺ was Khawla bint Hakim. Among them: Khawla bint al-Hudhayl ibn Hubayra, whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married, but she died before reaching him. Among them: Sharaf bint Khalifa, sister of Dihya, whom he married but did not consummate. Among them Layla bint al-Khatim, sister of Qays; he married her, and she was very jealous, so she asked him to release her, and he released her. Among them: Amra bint Mu'awiya al-Kindiyya, whom the Prophet ﷺ married. Al-Sha'bi said: He married a woman from Kinda, and she was brought to him after he had died. Among them: the daughter of Jundub ibn Damra al-Jundaʿiyya. Some said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her, and some denied that this occurred. Among them: the Ghifariyya. Some said: He married a woman from Ghifar, and he commanded her, so she removed her garments, and he saw whiteness, so he said: "Go back to your people." It is said: he only saw the whiteness in the Kilabiyya. These are those whom he contracted with and did not consummate, ﷺ. As for those who proposed to them but the marriage was not completed with them, and those who gave themselves to him: among them is Umm Hani bint Abi Talib, whose name is Fakhita. The Prophet ﷺ proposed to her, and she said: "I am a woman with children [[i.e., having children.]]," and she excused herself to him, and he accepted her excuse. Among them: Dubaa'a bint 'Amir. Among them: Safiyya bint Bashama ibn Nadla, whom the Prophet ﷺ proposed to, and she had been taken as captive; the Prophet ﷺ gave her a choice, saying: "If you wish, I, and if you wish, your husband?" She said: "My husband." So he released her, and the Banu Tamim cursed her, as reported by Ibn Abbas. Among them: Umm Sharik, whose mention has already passed. Among them: Layla bint al-Khatim, whose mention has already passed. Among them: Khawla bint Hakim ibn Umayya, who gave herself to the Prophet ﷺ, and he deferred her, so Uthman ibn Maz'un married her. Among them: Jamra bint al-Harith ibn Awf al-Murri, whom the Prophet ﷺ proposed to, and her father said: "There is a defect in her," though there was none in her, so her father returned to her and she had become leprous; she is the mother of Shabib ibn al-Barsa' the poet. Among them: Sawda al-Qurashiyya, whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ proposed to, and she had children. She said: "I fear that my children will cry out near your head." So he praised her and supplicated for her. Among them: a woman whose name is not mentioned. Mujahid said: A woman proposed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and she said: "I will consult my father." Then she met her father, and he permitted her, so she met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "We have already wrapped ourselves in a blanket other than you." These are all the wives of the Prophet ﷺ. He had two concubines from among the slave-women: Mariya the Copt, and Rayhana, according to Qatada. Others said: He had four: Mariya, Rayhana, another beautiful one whom he took in captivity, and a slave-girl whom Zaynab bint Jahsh gave him.

**Third:** The words of Allah the Exalted, "If you desire the worldly life and its adornment" (33:28). "In" is a conditional particle, and its response is "then come" (*fa-ta'alayna*). Thus He made the choice contingent upon a condition. This shows that a conditional choice (*takhyir*) and a conditional divorce (*talaq*) are both valid, and both take effect and stand. This is contrary to the ignorant innovators who claim that if a man says to his wife, "You are divorced if you enter the house," the divorce does not take effect if she enters the house, because lawful divorce (*talaq shar'i*) is only that which is immediate, with no condition.

**Fourth:** The words "then come" (*fa-ta'alayna*) are the response to the condition. It is a verb addressed to the group of women, derived from your saying *ta'ala* ("come"). It is a summons to approach. It is said *ta'ala* meaning *aqbil* ("come forward"). It was originally used for one who has majesty and rank, and then in usage it came to be used for anyone who summons another to approach. In this place, however, it retains its original sense, since the one summoning is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). "I will provide for you" (*umatti'kunna*): the discussion of *mut'ah* (provision upon divorce) has already passed in *al-Baqarah* (see vol. 3, p. 200 ff.). It has also been read as *umat'ikunna* with a *damma* on the *ʿayn*. Likewise, "and release you" (*wa-usarrihkunna*) is read with a *damma* on the *ḥa'* as a new, independent sentence. "Fair release" (*sarah jamil*) is divorce in accordance with the Sunnah, without harm and without withholding what is due to her.

**Fifth:** The scholars differed over the manner in which the Prophet (ﷺ) gave his wives the choice, in two opinions.

The first: he gave them the choice, by the permission of Allah, between remaining married or being divorced, and they chose to remain. This was said by ʿĀʾishah, Mujahid, ʿIkrimah, al-Shaʿbi, Ibn Shihab, and Rabiʿah. Some of them said: he only gave them the choice between the world, in which case he would separate from them, and the Hereafter, in which case he would keep them, so that they would have the higher station that they had with their husband. He did not give them the choice of divorce. This was mentioned by al-Hasan and Qatadah. From among the Companions, ʿAli reported, through Ahmad ibn Hanbal, that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave his wives a choice only between this world and the Hereafter."

I say: The first opinion is more correct, based on the statement of ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), when she was asked about a man who gives his wife a choice: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave us a choice, so was that a divorce?" In another narration: "We chose him, and he did not count it as a divorce against us." Nothing has been established from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) except the choice commanded between remaining and divorce. For this reason he said: "O ʿĀʾishah, I am going to mention a matter to you, and there is no harm in your not hastening in it until you consult your two parents." This is the hadith. It is well known that he did not intend consultation in choosing the world and its adornment over the Hereafter. Thus it is established that consultation occurred only concerning separation or remaining married. And Allah knows best.

**Sixth:** The scholars differed concerning the woman given the choice who chooses her husband. The majority of scholars among the early generations and others, and the leading jurists of fatwa, said: no divorce is binding upon him, neither one nor more. This is the view of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, ʿAli, Ibn Masʿud, Zayd ibn Thabit, Ibn ʿAbbas, and ʿĀʾishah. Among the Successors are ʿAta', Masruq, Sulayman ibn Yasar, Rabiʿah, and Ibn Shihab. It was also reported from ʿAli and Zayd that if she chooses her husband, it is one irrevocable (*ba'in*) divorce. This is the view of al-Hasan al-Basri and al-Layth, and al-Khattabi and al-Naqqash related it from Malik. They relied on the argument that his saying "choose" (*ikhtari*) is an allusive expression (*kinayah*) for pronouncing divorce, so when he attributes it to her, it takes effect as one pronouncement, like his saying "You are irrevocably divorced."

The sound view is the first, based on the statement of ʿĀʾishah: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave us a choice, so we chose him, and he did not count it against us as a divorce." It was recorded by the two Sahihs. Ibn al-Mundhir said: The hadith of ʿĀʾishah indicates that if the woman given the choice chooses her husband, that is not a divorce. It also indicates that her choosing herself causes a divorce, and it indicates a third meaning: that if the woman given the choice chooses herself, it is a single pronouncement over which her husband retains the right of return (*raj'ah*), since it is impermissible for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to divorce contrary to what Allah commanded him. This was reported from ʿUmar, Ibn Masʿud, and Ibn ʿAbbas. Ibn Abi Layla, al-Thawri, and al-Shafiʿi also said so. It was reported from ʿAli that if she chooses herself, it is one irrevocable divorce. This is the view of Abu Hanifah and his companions. Ibn Khuwayz Mandad related it from Malik. It was reported from Zayd ibn Thabit that if she chooses herself, it is three divorces. This is the view of al-Hasan al-Basri, and Malik and al-Layth also said so, because ownership (*al-milk*) is only effected by that. It was reported from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, that if she chooses herself, it is nothing. It was also reported from him that if she chooses her husband, it is one revocable (*raj'i*) divorce.

**Seventh:** A group of Medinese scholars and others held that delegation of divorce (*tamlik*) and the choice (*takhyir*) are the same, and that the judgment is whatever she decides in both. This is the view of ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Abi Salamah. Ibn Shaʿban said: Many of our companions have chosen this, and it is the view of a group of the people of Medina. Abu ʿUmar (Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr) said: The majority of jurists hold this view.

The well-known position of the school of Malik is that there is a difference between them. The delegation (*tamlik*), according to Malik, is a man's saying to his wife, "I have delegated to you," meaning: I have delegated to you what Allah has given me of divorce, whether one, two, or three. Since it is permissible for him to delegate part of it to her and not all of it, and he claims that, the statement is her statement with her oath if he disputes it. A group of the people of Medina said: he has the right to dispute in both delegation and choice equally, in the case of a woman who has been consummated with. The first is the well-known view of Malik. Ibn Khuwayz Mandad related from Malik that the husband may dispute with the woman given the choice regarding three, and it would be one irrevocable divorce, as Abu Hanifah said. Abu al-Jahm also said so. Sahnun said: most of our companions hold this view.

The summary of the position of Malik is: if the woman given the choice chooses herself, and she has been consummated with, then it is the full divorce, and if her husband denies it, he has no right of denial. If she chooses one divorce, it is nothing; rather the choice is absolute: either she takes it or leaves it, because the meaning of the choice is release (*tasrih*). Allah the Exalted said in the verse of choice: "Then come, I will provide for you and release you with a fair release" (33:28). So the meaning of release is absolute separation. Allah the Exalted said: "Divorce is twice; then either retention in kindness or release with good treatment" (2:229). Release with good treatment is the third pronouncement, as was reported from the Prophet (ﷺ), as mentioned earlier. From the perspective of meaning: his saying "choose me" or "choose yourself" requires that he has no authority over her if she chooses herself, and he owns nothing of her, since he has made it up to her to remove from him what he owns or to remain with him if she chooses him. So if she chooses part of the divorce, she has not acted according to the implication of the wording, and she is in the position of one who was given a choice between two things and chose something other than them.

As for the woman who has not been consummated with, he has the right to dispute her in the choice and delegation if she claims more than one, because she is separated immediately.

**Eighth:** The narration from Malik has differed as to when she has the option. Once he said: she has the option as long as she is in the session, before rising or engaging in something that indicates turning away. If she does not choose and does not decide anything until they separate from their session, then what was in her hands is void. This is the view of most jurists. Another time he said: she has the option forever, as long as it is not known that she has abandoned it. That is known by her allowing him access to herself by intercourse or intimate contact. In that case, if she prevents him from herself and does not choose anything, he has the right to bring her before the judge so that she either decides or drops it. If she refuses, the judge cancels her delegation.

According to the first view, if she engages in something other than that, such as speech, action, walking, or anything that is not related to the choice, as we have mentioned, her choice lapses. Some of our companions argued for this view with the words of Allah the Exalted: "So do not sit with them until they engage in a different conversation" (4:140). Also, the husband spoke to her in general terms so that she would know the choice from her, so it became like a contract between them. If she accepts it, it stands; otherwise it lapses, like one who says, "I have given you as a gift" or "I have sold to you": if the other accepts, it stands; otherwise the ownership remains as it was. This is the view of al-Thawri, the Kufans, al-Awza'i, al-Layth, al-Shafiʿi, and Abu Thawr, and it is the preference of Ibn al-Qasim.

The reasoning of the second narration is that the matter has come into her hand, and she has come to own it over her husband through his delegating it to her. Since she owns it, it must remain in her hand just as it remains in the hand of her husband.

I say: This is the sound view, based on the statement of the Prophet (peace be upon him) to ʿĀʾishah: "I am going to mention a matter to you, and there is no harm in your not hastening until you consult your two parents." It was narrated by the Sahih, and al-Bukhari recorded it, and al-Tirmidhi authenticated it. It has been mentioned earlier at the beginning of the chapter. It is evidence for the one who says that if a man gives his wife a choice or delegates it to her, she may decide regarding it even if they separate from their session. This was reported from al-Hasan and al-Zuhri, and Malik said it in one of his two narrations.

Abu ʿUbayd said: What we hold in this matter is following the Sunnah concerning ʿĀʾishah in this hadith, when he gave her the choice until she consulted her parents, and he did not make her standing up from her session an exit from the matter. Al-Marwazi said: This is the most correct of the opinions in my view, and Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tahawi also said it.

**Qur'an 33:30–31**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear lewdness, her punishment will be doubled twofold﴾. On this there are three issues.

**The first issue:** The scholars said: When the wives of the Prophet ﷺ chose Allah and His Messenger ﷺ, Allah thanked them for that and said, as an honour to them: ﴿Women are not lawful for you after this, nor is it lawful that you exchange them for other wives﴾ [al-Ahzab: 52] [[See p. 219 of this part.]], and so on. He also made clear their ruling in contrast to others, saying: ﴿It is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah, nor to marry his wives after him, ever﴾ [al-Ahzab: 53] [[See p. 228 of this part.]]. He made the reward for their obedience and the punishment for their disobedience greater than that for others, saying: "O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear lewdness, her punishment will be doubled twofold." Thus He informed that whoever among the wives of the Prophet ﷺ commits a lewdness, and Allah protected His Messenger ﷺ from that as occurred in the hadith of the slander (ifk) [[See vol. 12, p. 197 onward.]], her punishment will be doubled twofold, because of the nobility of their station, the excellence of their rank, and their precedence over all other women. Likewise, the Sharia has explained in more than one place, as explained before more than once, that whenever sanctities are multiplied and then violated, the penalties are multiplied; for this reason the prescribed punishment (hadd) of a free person is doubled for a slave, and that of a married person for a virgin.

It has also been said: Since the wives of the Prophet ﷺ lived in the place of the descent of revelation and in the home of Allah's commands and prohibitions, the command applied to them more strongly and bound them, because of their status, more than it bound others; so their reward and their punishment were doubled. It has also been said: That is only because of the magnitude of the harm in their offences through harming the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so the punishment was in proportion to the magnitude of the crime of harming the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, those who harm Allah and His Messenger, Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter﴾ [al-Ahzab: 57] [[See p. 237 of this part.]]. This view was chosen by Ilkiya al-Tabari.

**The second issue:** Some people said: If fornication were supposed to have been committed by one of them, and Allah forbid it, she would be given two hadd punishments because of her great rank, just as the hadd of a free woman is increased over that of a slave woman. The "punishment" (adhab) here means the hadd, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾ [[See vol. 12, p. 166.]] [[See vol. 12, p. 162.]] [al-Nur: 2]. On this view, the meaning of "twofold" is the meaning of "twice" or "two times".

Abu Ubayda said: The double of a thing is two things until it becomes three. Abu 'Amr said the same, as al-Tabari reported from him, so that two punishments like it are added to it, making three punishments. Al-Tabari declared this weak. It is indeed not sound, though its wording allows the possibility. That the reward is twice contradicts this view, because the punishment for lewdness corresponds to the reward for obedience; this was said by Ibn 'Atiyya.

Al-Nahhas said: Abu 'Amr distinguished between "yudā'af" and "yudda'af". He said: "yudā'af" means many repeated times, and "yudda'af" means twice. He read "yudda'af" for this reason. Abu Ubayda said: "yudā'af lahā al-'adhāb" means it is made into three punishments. Al-Nahhas said: The distinction brought by Abu 'Amr and Abu Ubayda is not known to anyone among the people of language that I know of. The meaning of "yudā'af" and "yudda'af" is one and the same, namely it is made twofold, just as you say: If you give me a dirham, I will give you its double, that is, its two equivalents, meaning two dirhams. This is supported by ﴿We will give her reward twice﴾, and the punishment cannot be greater than the reward. In another place He said: ﴿Give them a double punishment﴾ [al-Ahzab: 68] [[See p. 250 of this part.]], meaning two equivalents. Ma'mar related from Qatada regarding "yudā'af lahā al-'adhāb ḍi'fayn" that he said: the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter.

Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: The apparent meaning is that by "two-fold" He meant two equivalents, because He said: "We will give her reward twice." As for bequests (wasiyya): if someone bequeaths to a person "twice the share of his child," it is a bequest that he be given the equivalent of his share three times. Bequests are interpreted according to customary usage among people, and Allah's speech is to be interpreted by the speech of the Arabs. In the speech of the Arabs, "ḍi'f" means an equivalent, and more than that, and it is not restricted to two equivalents. One says: "This is the ḍi'f of that," meaning its equivalent; "This is its ḍi'fān," meaning its two equivalents. So "ḍi'f" in its original sense is an unrestricted increase. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿For them is the recompense of the double﴾ [Saba': 37] [[See p. 306 of this part.]], and He did not intend one equivalent or two. All of this is the statement of al-Azhari. The disagreement regarding the hadd for one who slanders one of them has already been mentioned in al-Nur [[See vol. 12, p. 176.]], and praise be to Allah.

**The third issue:** Abu Rafi' said: Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, often recited Surat Yusuf and Surat al-Ahzab at dawn prayer, and when he reached "O wives of the Prophet" he raised his voice with it. He was asked about that, and he said: "I remind them of the covenant."

The majority read "man ya'ti" with the ya'. Likewise "man yaqnut", taking the wording of "man" into account. "Qunut" means obedience, and it has been discussed before [[See vol. 2, p. 86 and vol. 3, p. 213.]].

Ya'qub read "man ta'ti" and "taqnut" with a ta' at the beginning, taking the meaning into account.

Some people said: When "al-fahisha" (the lewdness) appears definite, it means fornication and sodomy; when it appears indefinite, it means all other sins; and when it is described by an adjective, it means disobedience of a husband and corruption of his companionship. Another group said: Rather, His saying "a clear lewdness" includes all sins, and likewise "al-fahisha" in whatever form it occurs.

Ibn Kathir read "mubayyana" with a fatha on the ya'. Nafi' and Abu 'Amr read it with a kasra. A group read "yudā'if" with a kasra on the 'ayn, with the verb attributed to Allah, exalted is He. Abu 'Amr, as related by Kharija, read "nuḍā'if" with a damma on the nun and the word "al-'adhāb" in the accusative case; this is the reading of Ibn Muhaysin. This is a form of "mufā'ala" from one party, like "ṭāraqtu al-na'l" and "'āqabtu al-liṣṣ". Nafi', Hamza and al-Kisa'i read "yuḍā'af" with a ya' and a fatha on the 'ayn, with "al-'adhāb" in the nominative case. This is the reading of al-Hasan, Ibn Kathir and 'Isa. Ibn Kathir and Ibn 'Amir read "nuḍa''if" with a nun and a kasra on the 'ayn with shadda, with "al-'adhāb" in the accusative case.

Muqatil said: This doubling of the punishment is only in the Hereafter, because the giving of the reward twice is also in the Hereafter. This is good, because the wives of the Prophet ﷺ do not commit a lewdness that entails a hadd. Ibn 'Abbas said: The wife of a prophet never committed adultery at all; rather, she betrayed in faith and obedience.

Some commentators said: The punishment with which they were threatened, "twofold", is the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, and so too is the reward. Ibn 'Atiyya said: This is weak, unless it is meant that the wives of the Prophet ﷺ will not have the worldly hardship lifted from them as the punishment of the Hereafter, according to the state of people, by the ruling of the hadith of 'Ubada ibn al-Samit [[The wording of the hadith as in the Sahih of al-Bukhari, in the commentary on Surat al-Mumtahina: (He said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:) "Will you pledge allegiance to me that you will not associate anything with Allah, will not commit adultery, will not steal," and he recited the verse of the women: "O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you..." "Whoever of you fulfils it, his reward is with Allah. Whoever commits any of that and is punished for it, it is an expiation for him. Whoever commits any of that and Allah conceals it, it is up to Allah: if He wills He punishes him, and if He wills He forgives him."]]. This is a matter that has not been related concerning the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, nor has its establishment been preserved. The people of tafsir hold that "the generous provision" is Paradise, as mentioned by al-Nahhas.
