**Qurtubi's commentary (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 33, verse 32:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any one of the women, if you fear God.﴾ He means in excellence and nobility. He said "like any one" (*ka-ahad*) and did not say "like one" (*ka-wahidah*), because *ahad* is a negation (*nafy*) [[Thus in the original manuscripts; he means that it is a general negation applying to the masculine and the feminine, the singular and the plural.]] applying to the masculine and the feminine, the singular and the plural. It may also be used of non-human things; one says: "There is no *ahad* in it, neither a sheep nor a camel." Women were singled out for mention because among those who came before them were Asiya and Maryam. Qatadah pointed to this. The disagreement over the preference of these women among themselves has already been mentioned in "Al 'Imran," so reflect on it there [[See vol. 4, p. 3 (82)]]. Then He said: ﴿if you fear God⦈, i.e., if you are fearful of God. He thereby made clear that their excellence is only complete on the condition of piety, because of what God had granted them of companionship with the Messenger, of his great standing with them, and of the Qur'an being revealed concerning them.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So do not be soft in speech⦈. The verb is in the position of a jussive after the prohibition, except that it is indeclinable (*mabni*) just as the past tense is indeclinable. This is the view of Sibawayh, meaning: do not soften your speech. God commanded them that their speech should be firm and their words decisive, and not be in a manner that makes the heart think of what appears in it of softness, as was the custom among the women of the Arabs in speaking to men, with a trilling and softening of the voice, like the speech of the women who arouse suspicion and of the openly immoral. So He forbade them from such.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿so that one ... may aspire⦈. It is in the accusative (*fa-yat'ama*) as a response to the prohibition. ﴿In whose heart is a disease⦈ means doubt and hypocrisy, according to Qatadah and al-Suddi. It was also said: the aspiration to immorality, which is lewdness and flirtation, as said by Ikrimah. This is more correct, and hypocrisy has no place in this verse. Abu Hatim relates that al-A'raj read *fa-yatma'a* with a *fatha* on the *ya'* and a *kasra* on the *mim*. Al-Nahhas said: I think this is an error, and that he may have read *fa-yat'ama* with a *fatha* on the *mim* and a *kasra* on the *ayn*, by conjunction with *takhda'na*. This is a good and sound reading. It is also permissible to read *fa-yat'ama* meaning that the softness or the speech would arouse aspiration.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and speak a good word⦈. Ibn Abbas said: He commanded them to enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil. A woman is required to be restrained when addressing strangers, and likewise those who are forbidden to her by marriage, toward harshness in speech, without raising the voice, for the woman is commanded to lower her speech. In general, the "good word" is the correct word which neither the Sharia nor sound minds reject.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 33:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And stay in your houses, and do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance.﴾ On this verse there are four issues.

**The first issue:** His saying "waqarna." The majority of reciters read "wiqarna" with a kasra on the qaf. 'Asim and Nafi' read it with a fatha on the qaf. As for the first reading, it may bear two meanings.

One: it comes from *al-waqar* (dignity, composure). You say: *waqara yaqirru waqaran*, meaning he became calm and settled. The imperative is *qir*, and for women it is *qirna*, like *'idna* and *zinna*.

The second: this is the view of al-Mubarrad [in one copy: al-Farra']. It comes from *al-qarar* (staying). You say: *qarartu bil-makan* (with a fatha on the ra') *aqirru*. The original is *aqrirna* (with a kasra on the ra'), so the first ra' was deleted for lightness, as they said *zilt* for *zalilt* and *mist* for *massasta*. Its vowel was transferred to the qaf, and the connecting hamza (*hamzat al-wasl*) was dispensed with because the qaf is now vowelled.

Abu 'Ali said: rather, the ra' was changed into a ya' out of dislike of doubling, as it was changed in *qirat* and *dinar*. The ya' takes the vowel of the letter it replaced, so the assumed form is *iqyirna*. Then the vowel of the ya' is placed on the qaf, out of dislike of a ya' vowelled with a kasra. The ya' falls because two consonants meet, and the connecting hamza falls because what follows it is vowelled, so it becomes *qarna*.

As for the reading of the people of Medina and of 'Asim, it follows the usage of the Arabs: *qarirtu fi al-makan* (with a kasra on the ra') *aqarru* (with a fatha on the qaf), from the pattern of *hamida yahmadu*. This is the dialect of the Hijaz. Abu 'Ubayd mentioned it in *al-Gharib al-Musannaf* on the authority of al-Kisa'i, who was one of his most eminent teachers. Al-Zajjaj and others also mentioned it. The original is *aqrirna*; the first ra' was deleted because of the heaviness of doubling, and its vowel was placed on the qaf, so one says *qarna*.

Al-Farra' said: it is like when you say *ahasta sahibaka* (did you perceive your companion?), meaning *hal ahsasta*.

Abu 'Uthman al-Mazini said: *qarirtu bihi 'aynan* (with a kasra only) comes from *qurrat al-'ayn* (the coolness of the eye). It is not permitted to say *qarirtu fi al-makan* (with a kasra); it is *qarartu* (with a fatha on the ra').

Whatever he denied of this does not discredit the reading if it is established from the Prophet ﷺ. What is established from him in recitation is used as evidence for the soundness of the language.

Abu Hatim also claimed that *qarna* has no basis (*madhhab*) in the speech of the Arabs.

Al-Nahhas said: as for Abu Hatim's saying "it has no basis," it has been contradicted. There are two views on it. One is what al-Kisa'i related. The other is what I heard 'Ali ibn Sulayman say: he said, "It is from *qarirtu bihi 'aynan aqarru*, and the meaning is *waqrarna bihi 'aynan fi buyutikunna*" (and let your eyes be cooled in your houses). This is a good view, except that the hadith indicates it is from the first meaning. It is related that Ammar said to 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her: "Indeed Allah has commanded you to stay (*taqarri*) in your home." She said: "O Abu al-Yaqzan, you have always been a speaker of the truth!" He said: "Praise be to Allah, who made me so through your tongue."

Ibn Abi 'Ablah recited *waqrirna* with a connecting hamza and two ra's, the first with a kasra.

**The second issue:** The meaning of this verse is a command to remain in the house. Although the address is to the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, others are included in its meaning. This would be so even if no evidence specifically covered all women. How much more so, since the Shari'ah abounds with the principle that women should remain in their homes and refrain from leaving them except out of necessity, as has preceded in more than one place.

Allah commanded the wives of the Prophet ﷺ to remain in their homes, addressing them thus to honor them. He forbade them from *tabarruj* (displaying one's adornment and beauty), and informed them that it is the deed of the former *jahiliyyah*, saying: "and do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance."

The meaning of *tabarruj* was mentioned in surah al-Nur [see vol. 12, p. 309]. Its reality is the display of what is better concealed. It is derived from spaciousness; one says *fi asnanihi baraj* when the teeth are spaced apart. This was said by al-Mubarrad.

People differed about *al-jahiliyyah al-ula* (the former ignorance). It was said: it is the era in which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was born, when women wore armor of pearls and walked in the middle of the road presenting themselves to men. Al-Hakam ibn 'Uyaynah said: it is the period between Adam and Nuh, eight hundred years, and wicked conduct was related of them. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the period between Nuh and Idris. Al-Kalbi said: between Nuh and Ibrahim. It was said: women wore pearl armor not sewn at the sides, and wore thin garments that did not cover their bodies. A group said: it is the period between Musa and 'Isa. Al-Sha'bi said: between 'Isa and Muhammad ﷺ. Abu al-'Aliyah said: it is the time of Dawud and Sulayman, when a woman had a shirt of pearls not sewn at the sides.

Abu al-'Abbas al-Mubarrad said: *al-jahiliyyah al-ula* is like saying *al-jahiliyyah al-jahla'* (the utter ignorance). He said: in the utter ignorance, women used to display what is ugly to display, until a woman would sit with her husband and her close friend (*khilluhu*, meaning intimate companion), and her friend would be alone with what was above the *izar* (waist-wrap), and her husband would be alone with what was below it, and one of them would ask the other for a exchange.

Mujahid said: women used to walk among the men, and that is the *tabarruj*.

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: what appears to me is that it points to the *jahiliyyah* in which they were, and they were commanded to move away from their conduct in it, which was the conduct of the disbelievers before the Shari'ah, because they had no jealousy, and the affairs of women were without veil. Calling it "first" is in relation to what they were in; the meaning is not that there is another *jahiliyyah*. The name *jahiliyyah* has been applied to that period before Islam, so they say *jahili* in the case of the poets. Ibn 'Abbas said in al-Bukhari: "I heard my father in the *jahiliyyah* saying..." and so on, to other than this.

I say: this is a good view. It is objected that the Arabs were for the most part a people of frugality and hardship, that luxury and the display of adornment occurred in earlier eras, and that these are what is meant by *al-jahiliyyah al-ula*. The aim of the verse is to oppose the conduct of those women who came before them, such as walking with coquetry and swaying, displaying their attractions to men, and other things that are not permitted by the Shari'ah. This includes all the views and encompasses them. Therefore they must remain in their homes. If the need to go out arises, they should go out in *tabadhdhul* (humble, unadorned dress, without displaying beauty out of humility) and complete concealment. And Allah is the Granter of success.

**The third issue:** Al-Tha'labi and others mentioned that 'A'isha, when she recited this verse, would weep until her *khimar* (headscarf) was soaked. It is also mentioned that Sawda was asked: "Why do you not perform the hajj and the 'umrah as your sisters do?" She said: "I have performed the hajj and the 'umrah, and Allah commanded me to stay in my house." The narrator said: "By Allah, she did not leave the door of her chamber until her funeral was carried out." May Allah be pleased with her!

Ibn al-'Arabi said: I have entered more than a thousand villages, and I have not seen women more protective of their households or more chaste than the women of Nablus, where al-Khalil (ﷺ) was thrown into the fire. I stayed there, and I did not see a woman on the road by day except on Friday, when they go out to it until the mosque is filled with them. When the prayer is finished and they return to their homes, my eyes did not fall on one of them until the next Friday. I have also seen, in al-Masjid al-Aqsa, chaste women who did not leave their place of seclusion until they were martyred there.

**The fourth issue:** Ibn 'Atiyyah said: 'A'isha's weeping was on account of her journey during the Battle of the Camel (*al-Jamal*). At that time Ammar said to her: "Allah has commanded you to stay in your house."

Ibn al-'Arabi said: the Rafidah (an extremist Shi'i sect; may Allah curse them) cling to this verse against the Mother of the Believers 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her. They say she opposed the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when she went out leading armies, engaging in wars, and plunging into the thick of spear-thrusts and blows, in what was neither obligatory for her nor permissible for her. They say: "'Uthman was besieged, and when she saw that, she ordered her mounts to be brought to set out for Makkah. Marwan said to her: 'Stay here, O Mother of the Believers, and turn back these rabble, for reconciling between people is better than your hajj.'"

Ibn al-'Arabi said: our scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, said: 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, had vowed to perform the hajj before the strife, so she did not see abstaining from her vow. Had she gone out during that upheaval, it would have been correct for her. As for her going out to the Battle of the Camel, she did not go out to fight. Rather, people clung to her and complained to her of the great strife they had fallen into and the chaos among the people. They hoped for her blessing and hoped to be shamed by her when she stood among the creatures, and she thought that [so she went out], following Allah's saying: ﴿There is no good in much of their secret talk, except for one who enjoins charity or what is right or reconciliation between people﴾ [al-Nisa': 114], and His saying: ﴿If two groups of believers fight, then make peace between them﴾ [al-Hujurat: 9].

The command to reconcile is addressed to all people, male and female, free and slave. Allah, by His prior decree and His executed judgment, did not will that reconciliation should take place. Rather, there were stabbings and wounds until both sides nearly perished. Some of them went to the camel and hamstrung it. When the camel fell on its side, Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr reached 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, and carried her to Basra. She went out with thirty women, whom 'Ali assigned to accompany her until they delivered her to Madinah, a pious, devout, striving woman, correct in what she interpreted and rewarded for what she did, since every mujtahid (one who exerts independent juristic effort) in the rulings is correct.

The name of this camel was mentioned in surah al-Nahl [see vol. 10, p. 73 onward], and by it that day is known.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And establish the prayer, and give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning in what He commanded and forbade. ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, O people of the household, and to purify you thoroughly﴾.

Al-Zajjaj said: it has been said that what is meant is the wives of the Prophet ﷺ. It has also been said that what is meant is his wives and his family, who are the people of his household, as will be explained later. *Ahla al-bayt* (people of the household) is in the accusative by way of praise (*al-madh*). He said: if you wish, it may be in apposition (*badal*). He said: the nominative and the genitive are also permitted.

Al-Nahhas said: if it is put in the genitive as an apposition to the *kaf* and *mim* (the pronoun suffixes of "you"), it is not permitted according to Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Yazid. He said: one does not make an apposition from the second-person address nor from the one addressed, because they do not need clarification.

﴿And purify you thoroughly﴾: *tathhiran* is a verbal noun (*masdar*) which carries the sense of emphasis.

The commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 34:

There are three issues. The first concerns God's words: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the revelations of God and the wisdom﴾. These words indicate that the People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt) are his wives. The scholars have differed about who the People of the House are. 'Ata', 'Ikrimah and Ibn 'Abbas said: they are his wives specifically, with no man among them. They held that "the house" refers to the dwellings of the Prophet (ﷺ), based on God's words: "and remember what is recited in your houses." A group including al-Kalbi said: they are 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn specifically, and there are reports from the Prophet (peace be upon him) on this. They argued with God's words: "God only wishes to remove from you the impurity, People of the House, and to purify you," using the masculine pronoun (bikum, "you" masculine). Had it been for the women specifically, it would have been "anhunna and yutahhirakunna" (feminine). However, it is possible that it came in the form of the word "ahl," as a man says to his companion, "How is your family?" meaning his wife and women, and he replies, "They are well." God said: "Are you amazed at the command of God? The mercy of God and his blessings be upon you, People of the House" [Hud: 73]. [[See vol. 9, p. 70.]] What appears from the verse is that it is general, covering all the People of the House, including the wives and others. He said "and purify you" because the Messenger of God (ﷺ), 'Ali, al-Hasan and al-Husayn were among them, and when the masculine and feminine are together, the masculine is given precedence. The verse therefore implies that the wives are among the People of the House, since the verse concerns them, and the address to them is indicated by the context of the discourse. And God knows best.

As for the report that Umm Salamah said: "This verse was revealed in my house. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) summoned 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and he entered with them under a Khaybari cloak and said: (These are the People of my House)," and he recited the verse, and said: (O God, remove from them the impurity and purify them thoroughly). Umm Salamah said: "And I am with them, O Messenger of God?" He said: (You are in your place, and you are upon good). It was narrated by al-Tirmidhi and others, and he said: "This is a gharib (rare) hadith." Al-Qushayri said: Umm Salamah said, "I put my head into the cloak and said: 'Am I one of them, O Messenger of God?' He said: '(Yes).'" Al-Tha'labi said: they are the Banu Hashim. This indicates that the house is meant as the house of lineage, so al-Abbas, his paternal uncles and their sons would be among them. A similar report was transmitted from Zayd ibn Arqam, may God be pleased with them all.

According to the view of al-Kalbi, God's words "and remember" would be the beginning of a new address by God, meaning an address by the command of God, the Mighty and Majestic, to the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), by way of admonition and enumerating the blessing, by mentioning what is recited in their houses of the revelations of God and the wisdom. The scholars of exegesis (ta'wil) said: "the revelations of God" means the Qur'an, and "the wisdom" means the sunnah (the Prophet's practice and teaching). The correct view is that God's words "and remember" are joined to what precedes them. He said "ankum" (from you) because of his words "ahl" (People), and "ahl" is masculine. So He addressed them with the masculine form, although they are females, and therefore "ankum" occurs. There is no weight to the view of al-Kalbi and those like him, for there are found in this exegesis (tafsir) things which, had they existed in the time of the righteous predecessors (al-salaf al-salih), they would have prevented him from them and restricted him. All the verses, from His words, "O Prophet, say to your wives," to His words, "Indeed God is ever Subtle and Acquainted," are joined to one another. How then could a separate statement for others come in the middle? This is only something that occurred in the reports: when this verse was revealed to the Prophet (peace be upon him), he summoned 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and the Prophet (ﷺ) went to a cloak and wrapped them in it, then raised his hand to the sky and said: (O God, these are the People of my House. O God, remove from them the impurity and purify them thoroughly). This was a supplication by the Prophet (ﷺ) for them after the verse was revealed, wishing to include them in the verse addressed to the wives. Al-Kalbi and those who agreed with him made it specific to them, but it is a supplication for them outside the revealed text.

The second issue: the word "remembrance" (dhikr) may bear three meanings. The first: remember the place of blessing, since God placed you in houses in which the revelations of God and the wisdom are recited. The second: remember the revelations of God, esteem their worth, reflect upon them until they are present in your minds, so that you may be admonished by the admonitions of God, and one whose condition is this should have his actions made good. The third: "remember" means preserve, recite, and keep on your tongues, as though He were saying: preserve the commands and prohibitions of God, and that is what is recited in your houses of the revelations of God. So God, glorified and exalted, commanded that they relate what is revealed of the Qur'an in their houses, and what they see of the actions of the Prophet (peace be upon him), and what they hear of his sayings, so that they may convey that to the people, and they may act and follow. This indicates the permissibility of accepting the report (khabar) of a single transmitter (khabar al-wahid), whether man or woman, in religion.

The third issue: Ibn al-'Arabi said: In this verse there is a wonderful point, which is that God, exalted is He, commanded His Prophet (peace be upon him) to convey what was revealed to him of the Qur'an and to teach what He had taught him of the religion. So when he recited to one person or to whoever it happened to be, the obligation was discharged from him, and it became incumbent upon the one who heard it to convey it to others. He was not obliged to mention it to all the Companions, nor was it incumbent upon him, when he taught that to his wives, to go out to the people and say, "Such-and-such was revealed" or "Such-and-such was the case." Therefore we say: it is permissible to act upon the report of Busra [[She is Busra bint Safwan ibn Nawfal, who related from the Prophet (ﷺ).]] regarding the obligation of wudu' (ablution) from touching the penis, because she related what she heard and conveyed what she retained. It is not necessary that this be conveyed by men, as Abu Hanifah said. Moreover, it has been transmitted from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and Ibn 'Umar.

**The first issue:** Al-Tirmidhi narrated from Umm 'Umara al-Ansariyya that she came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "I see that everything is only for men, and I do not see women being mentioned for anything!" So this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women...﴾ to the end of the verse. This is a hasan gharib hadith. "Al-Muslimin" is the subject of "inna" (indeed), and "al-muslimat" is coordinated with it. In the view of the Basrians, their (the feminine plurals') nominative case is also permissible. But al-Farra' held that it is not permissible, except in cases where the grammatical inflection (i'rab) is not visibly distinguished.

**The second issue:** In this verse, God began with mention of Islam, which encompasses faith and the actions of the limbs, and then mentioned faith specifically, drawing attention to the fact that it is the greatest part of Islam and its pillar. "Al-qanit" is the worshipper who is obedient. "Al-sadiq" means, regarding what one has been bound to, that he fulfils it. "Al-sabir" is one who is patient regarding desires and steadfast in acts of obedience, in hardship and in ease (al-makrah wa al-manshat). [[Al-makrah (with a fatha on the mim): the disliked thing. Al-manshat: the matter for which you feel energized and eager and prefer to do, and it is a verbal noun meaning vigour.]] "Al-khashi'" is one who fears God. "Al-mutasaddiq" is one who gives charity, whether obligatory or voluntary. It was said: only obligatory charity is meant, but the first (the broader meaning) is more praiseworthy. "Al-sa'im" is likewise. "Wa al-hafizin furujahum wa al-hafizat" means: guarding them from what is not lawful, such as fornication and other things.

In His words "wa al-hafizat" there is an elision that is indicated by what precedes it. Its estimated form is: wa al-hafizat-ha (and those who guard it), and what preceded is sufficient for it. The same applies to "al-dhakirat" as well. A similar example is the verse of the poet:

*"And dark-red (horses), bloodied, as if their backs
were covered by the running of [the one who] wore over them, and the shade of gilded (metal)"*

[[Al-kumt: plural of akmat, a redness tending toward blackness. Al-mudamma: intensely red like blood. Al-muttun: plural of matn, the back. Istash'arat: made it their covering. Al-mudhahhab: overlaid with gold. The verse is by Tufayl al-Ghanawi (cited from Sibawayh and al-'Ayni).]]

Sibawayh narrated "lawna mudhhabin" with the accusative. The nominative is permissible only by omitting the pronoun, as if he had said: "wa istash'arathu" (and she made it her covering), according to the one who reads "lawnun" in the nominative.

As for "al-dhakir" (the one who remembers), it was said: [he remembers God] after the prayers, morning and evening, in bed, and upon waking from sleep. All of this has already been explained in detail in its proper places, along with the benefits and rulings that follow from it, so there is no need to repeat it. [[See vol. 1 p. 331, vol. 4 pp. 82 and 310.]] And praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds.

Mujahid said: One is not considered a person who remembers God abundantly until he remembers Him standing, sitting and lying down.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Whoever wakes his family at night and they both pray four rak'ahs, they are written among those who remember God abundantly, and the women who remember.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 36:

There are four issues in this.

The first: Qatadah, Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid narrated concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed marriage to Zaynab bint Jahsh, and she was his paternal aunt's daughter. She thought the proposal was for himself, but when it became clear that he wanted her for Zayd, she disliked it, refused and declined, and the verse was revealed. Zaynab then submitted and married him. In another narration: she refused, and her brother 'Abdullah also refused, because of her lineage from Quraysh, and because Zayd had been a slave the day before, until this verse was revealed. Her brother then said to him: "Command me with whatever you wish," and he married her to Zayd.

It was also said: it was revealed concerning Umm Kulthum bint 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'it, who had offered herself to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he married her to Zayd ibn Harithah. She and her brother disliked that and said: "We only wanted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he married us to someone else." So the verse was revealed on account of that, and they agreed to the marriage to Zayd. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

Al-Hasan said: It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah the Mighty and Majestic and His Messenger (ﷺ) decree a matter, that they should have a choice in their affair.

The second: the expression "ma kana" and "wa ma yanbaghi" and similar phrases have the meaning of prohibition and forbidding. They are used to prohibit a thing and to rule that it shall not occur, as in this verse. Sometimes the impossibility of that thing is rational, as in the words of the Exalted: ﴿Could you not have made its trees grow?﴾ [[See vol. 13, p. 221.]] [An-Naml: 60]. Sometimes the knowledge of its impossibility is legal, as in the words of the Exalted: "It is not for a human that Allah should give him the Book and the wisdom and prophethood" [[See vol. 4, p. 121.]], and His words: ﴿It is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a veil﴾ [[See vol. 16, p. 53.]] [Ash-Shura: 51]. Sometimes it is used regarding recommended matters, as when you say: "It is not for you, O so-and-so, to abandon the supererogatory prayers," and similar.

The third: in this verse there is evidence, indeed an explicit text, that equality (kafa'ah) is not considered in lineage but is considered in religion, contrary to Malik, al-Shafi'i, al-Mughirah and Sahnun. That is because the freedmen married into Quraysh: Zayd married Zaynab bint Jahsh; al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad married Dubaa'ah bint al-Zubayr; Abu Hudhayfah married Salim to Fatimah [[In the originals and Ibn al-'Arabi: (Hind), and the correction is from the books of the Companions.]] bint al-Walid ibn 'Utbah; and Bilal married the sister of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf. This meaning has already been mentioned in more than one place. [[See vol. 3, p. 69 and vol. 13, p. 278.]]

The fourth: the words of the Exalted: ﴿that they should have a choice in their affair﴾. The Kufans read "an yakuna" with the yaa'. This is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd, because the feminine noun has been separated from its verb. The rest read it with the taa', because the word "khiyarah" is feminine, so feminizing its verb is good. The masculine form is based on the meaning that "al-khiyarah" means "al-takhyir", so "al-khiyarah" is a verbal noun in the sense of "al-ikhtiyar". Ibn al-Sumayq read "al-khiyrah" with a sukun on the yaa'. This verse falls within the context of the Exalted's words: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than themselves﴾ [[See p. 121 of this volume.]] [Al-Ahzab: 6]. Then the Exalted threatened and informed that whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed.

This is the strongest evidence for what the majority of our jurists, the jurists of the companions of Imam al-Shafi'i, and some of the usulis hold: that the form "af'il" (imperative) is, in its original usage, for obligation. For Allah, blessed and exalted, negated the choice of the responsible person upon hearing His command and the command of His Messenger (ﷺ); then He applied the name of disobedience to whoever still had a choice when the command was issued; then He attached straying to that disobedience. Therefore it is necessary to read the command as obligatory. And Allah knows best.

**Ninth of the issues:** (Note: the passage's numbering is kept as it appears.) There are nine issues in this verse.

**The first issue:** al-Tirmidhi narrated: Ali ibn Hujr told us, Dawud ibn al-Zibriqan told us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Sha'bi, from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: "If the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had concealed any part of the revelation, he would have concealed this verse: 'And when you said to the one on whom Allah bestowed favour and you bestowed favour: "Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah," while you concealed within yourself that which Allah was to bring to light, and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him' ... up to his words: 'and the command of Allah is ever executed.'" (She meant by "the one on whom Allah bestowed favour" the bestowal of Islam, and by "you bestowed favour" the manumission, when he freed him.) "And when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married her, they said: 'He has married the wife of his son.' So Allah the Exalted revealed: 'Muhammad is not the father of any man among you, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets' [al-Ahzab: 40]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had adopted him when he was young, and he remained until he became a man called Zayd ibn Muhammad. Then Allah, blessed and exalted is He, revealed: 'Call them by [the names of] their fathers; that is more just in the sight of Allah. But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients' [al-Ahzab: 5]. So it was said: 'So-and-so, the client of so-and-so, and so-and-so, the brother of so-and-so,' which is more just in the sight of Allah [meaning 'more equitable'].[[Addition from the Sahih of al-Tirmidhi.]]"

Abu Isa (al-Tirmidhi) said: "This is a gharib (rare) hadith [[Addition from the Sahih of al-Tirmidhi.]]. It has also been narrated from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: 'If the Prophet (ﷺ) had concealed any part of the revelation, he would have concealed this verse: "And when you said to the one on whom Allah bestowed favour and you bestowed favour."' This phrase has not been narrated in its full length."

I say: This extent of the narration is what Muslim included in his Sahih, and it is what al-Tirmidhi authenticated in his Jami'. In al-Bukhari, it is narrated from Anas ibn Malik that this verse, "And you concealed within yourself that which Allah was to bring to light," was revealed concerning Zaynab bint Jahsh and Zayd ibn Harithah.

Umar, Ibn Mas'ud, Aisha and al-Hasan said: "Allah did not reveal to His Messenger any verse more severe for him than this verse." Al-Hasan and Aisha also said: "If the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had concealed any part of the revelation, he would have concealed this verse, because of its severity upon him."

It is related in a report: Zayd entered the evening and went to his bed. Zaynab said: "Zayd did not approach me, and I do not refuse him anything except what Allah has prevented him from taking from me, so he cannot have power over me." This is the narration of Abu Isma Nuh ibn Abi Maryam, who traced the report back to Zaynab that she said this.

In some narrations: "Zayd felt a swelling from her when he wished to approach her," and this is close to that.

Zayd came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Zaynab hurts me with her tongue, and does this and that! And I want to divorce her." He said to him: "Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah," the verse. So Zayd divorced her, and then this was revealed: "And when you said to the one on whom Allah bestowed favour and you bestowed favour..." up to the end of the verse.

The people differed in interpreting this verse. Qatadah, Ibn Zayd and a group of commentators, among them al-Tabari and others, held that the Prophet (ﷺ) had developed a liking for Zaynab bint Jahsh while she was in the marriage of Zayd, and he was eager that Zayd would divorce her so that he could marry her himself. Then, when Zayd informed him that he intended to separate from her, complaining of her harshness of speech, disobedience to his command, harm by her tongue, and her arrogance due to her nobility, he said to him: "Fear Allah," meaning regarding what you say about her, and "Keep your wife to yourself," while he concealed his eagerness for Zayd to divorce her. This is what he was concealing within himself, but he adhered to what was obligatory of enjoining good.

Muqatil said: The Prophet (ﷺ) married Zaynab bint Jahsh to Zayd, and she stayed with him for some time. Then one day he (peace be upon him) came to Zayd seeking him, and he saw Zaynab standing. She was fair, beautiful, and tall, one of the most complete women of Quraysh. He was captivated by her and said: "Glory be to Allah, the Turner of hearts!" Zaynab heard this glorification and mentioned it to Zayd. Zayd understood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, permit me to divorce her, for she has pride; she exalts herself over me and hurts me with her tongue." He (peace be upon him) said: "Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah."

It was also said: Allah sent a wind which lifted the curtain while Zaynab was dressed lightly[[To be dressed lightly (tafaddalat) means she wore her house clothes, or was wearing only one garment.]] in her house. He saw Zaynab and she fell into his heart, and it fell into Zaynab's heart that she had fallen into the heart of the Prophet (ﷺ). This was when he came seeking Zayd, so she informed him of that, and it came into Zayd's heart to divorce her.

Ibn Abbas said: "And you concealed within yourself" means the love for her. "And you feared the people" means you were shy of them. It was also said: you feared and disliked the blame of the Muslims, if you had said: "Divorce her," and they would say: "He ordered a man to divorce his wife, then married her when he divorced her." "And Allah has more right that you fear Him" in all circumstances. It was also said: "And Allah has more right that you be shy before Him, and that you not command Zayd to keep his wife after Allah informed you that she would be your wife." So Allah rebuked him for all of this.

It is related from Ali ibn al-Husayn that Allah the Exalted had revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) that Zayd would divorce Zaynab, and that he would marry her by Allah's marriage of her to him. When Zayd complained to the Prophet (ﷺ) about Zaynab's character, that she did not obey him, and informed him that he wanted to divorce her, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him, by way of good manners and counsel: "Fear Allah in your speech, and keep your wife to yourself." While he knew that he would separate from her and that he would marry her. This is what he concealed within himself. He did not want to order him to divorce her, because he knew that he would marry her. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) feared that a saying from the people would attach to him, about marrying Zaynab after Zayd, while Zayd was his freedman and he had commanded him to divorce her. So Allah the Exalted rebuked him for this measure of fearing the people regarding a matter which Allah had permitted him, by saying: "Keep [your wife]," while knowing that he would divorce her. And He informed him that Allah has more right to be feared, that is, in all circumstances.

Our scholars, may Allah have mercy upon them, said: This is the best of what has been said in interpreting this verse, and it is the view of the verifying commentators and the firmly grounded scholars, such as al-Zuhri, Qadi Bakr ibn al-Ala al-Qushayri, Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi and others. The meaning of Allah's words "and you feared the people" is only the rumour of the hypocrites that he had forbidden marrying the wives of sons, and that he had married the wife of his son.

As for what is narrated, that the Prophet (ﷺ) became enamoured of Zaynab, the wife of Zayd, and some frivolous people have used the word "fell in love with," this comes only from someone ignorant of the infallibility of the Prophet (ﷺ) from such things, or someone who makes light of his sanctity.

Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim, in Nawadir al-Usul, transmitted from Ali ibn al-Husayn this statement: "Ali ibn al-Husayn brought this from the treasury of knowledge, a gem among gems and a pearl among pearls: that Allah rebuked him only because He had informed him that this woman would be among your wives. So how could he then say to Zayd: 'Keep your wife to yourself,' while the fear of the people had seized you, that they would say: 'He married his son's wife'? And Allah has more right that you fear Him."

An-Nahhas said: Some scholars said: This was not a sin from the Prophet (ﷺ). Do you not see that he was not commanded to repent of it or to seek forgiveness for it? A thing may not be a sin, yet something else may be better than it. He concealed that within himself for fear that the people would be tested.

**The second issue:** Ibn al-Arabi said: If it is asked, for what purpose did he say to him, "Keep your wife to yourself," when Allah had informed him that she was his wife? We say: He wanted to test from him what Allah had not made him know of his desire for her or his aversion from her. Zayd showed him an aversion and dislike toward her which he had not known from him regarding her matter.

If it is said: How could he order him to hold on to her when he knew that separation was unavoidable? This would be a contradiction. We say: Rather, it is sound for the sound purposes of establishing the proof and knowing the outcome. Do you not see that Allah the Exalted commands the servant to believe while He knows that he will not believe? So there is nothing in the contradiction between the object of the command and the object of the knowledge that prevents commanding it, by reason or by ruling. This is from the precious knowledge, so be certain of it and accept it.

His saying: "And fear Allah" means regarding her divorce, so do not divorce her. He intended a recommendation of avoidance (nahy tanzih), not a prohibition of unlawfulness (nahy tahrim), because the preferable course is not to divorce.

It was also said: "Fear Allah," so do not blame her in regard to her arrogance and her harm to her husband.

"And you concealed within yourself": it was said this is the attachment of his heart. It was also said: the separation of Zayd from her. It was also said: his knowledge that Zayd would divorce her, since Allah had informed him of that.

**The third issue:** It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said to Zayd: "I find no one in my soul more trustworthy than you, so propose to Zaynab on my behalf." He said: "So I went, and I turned my back to her out of reverence for the Prophet (ﷺ), and I proposed to her. She rejoiced and said: 'I will do nothing until I consult my Lord.' So she went to her place of worship, and the Qur'an was revealed. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) married her and consummated the marriage with her."

I say: The meaning of this hadith is established in the Sahih. Al-Nasa'i titled it: "The prayer of a woman when she is proposed to, and her seeking guidance from her Lord (istikhara)."

The imams narrated, and the wording is that of Muslim, from Anas, who said: "When the waiting period of Zaynab expired, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Zayd: 'Mention her to me.'" He said: "So Zayd set off until he came to her, and she was kneading her dough." He said: "When I saw her, she became great in my chest, so that I could not look at her, because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had mentioned her. So I turned my back to her and backed away on my heels. I said: 'O Zaynab, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has sent to mention you.' She said: 'I will do nothing until I consult my Lord.' So she went to her place of worship, and the Qur'an was revealed." And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came and entered upon her without permission. [Anas] said: "And indeed I saw that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fed us bread and meat when the day had stretched on..." the hadith. In one narration: "until they left him."

In another narration from Anas as well, he said: "I never saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) hold a wedding feast for any of his wives as he held one for Zaynab. He slaughtered a sheep."

Our scholars said: His (peace be upon him) saying to Zayd, "Mention her to me," means: propose to her, as the first hadith explained. This was a trial and test for Zayd, so that his patience, submission and obedience would become apparent.

I say: From this it may be inferred that a person may say to his companion: "Propose to so-and-so on my behalf," to the woman who was divorced from him (the companion), and there is no harm in that. And Allah knows best.

The fourth issue: when she entrusted her affair to God and her delegation of it to Him was valid, God Himself took charge of her marriage. For this reason He said: "So when Zayd had no further need of her, We gave her to you in marriage" (33:37). Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad related from his forefathers, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the reading "When he had no further need of her, I gave her to you in marriage." When God informed him of this, he entered upon her without permission, without renewing the contract, without fixing a dower, and without any of the things that are a condition for our rights [[In manuscript Sh: (huqoqaha).]] and are prescribed for us. This was one of his (ﷺ) particular privileges, in which no one shares with him, by the consensus (ijma') of the Muslims. For this reason Zaynab used to boast to the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) and say: "Your fathers married you off, but God Most High married me off." Al-Nasa'i related it from Anas ibn Malik, who said: Zaynab used to boast over the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), saying: "God, Mighty and Majestic, married me off from above the heavens." In this matter the verse of hijab (veiling) was also revealed, as will come.

The fifth issue: the one upon whom God bestowed favour in this verse is Zayd ibn Harithah, as we have explained, and his story has already been mentioned at the beginning of the surah [[See p. 118 of this part.]]. It is related that his uncle met him one day, when he had come to Makkah on some business, and said: "What is your name, boy?" He said: "Zayd." He said: "Son of whom?" He said: "Son of Harithah." He said: "Son of whom?" He said: "Son of Shara'il al-Kalbi." He said: "What is your mother's name?" He said: "Su'da." I had been among my maternal relatives, Tayy. So he (the uncle) pressed him to his chest. He sent for his brother and his people, and they came. They wanted him to stay with them, and they said: "Whose are you?" He said: "Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah's." So they came to him and said: "This is our son; return him to us." He (the Prophet) said: "Present him with the choice; if he chooses you, take him by the hand." He then sent for Zayd and said: "Do you recognise these people?" He said: "Yes! This is my father, this is my brother, and this is my uncle." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Then what kind of companion have I been to you?" He wept and said: "Why do you ask me about that?" He said: "I give you the choice; if you wish to join them, then join them; and if you wish to stay, then I am the one you know." He said: "I will not prefer anyone over you." His uncle then pulled him and said: "Zayd, you have chosen slavery over your father and your uncle!" He said: "Yes, by God! Slavery with Muhammad is dearer to me than being with you." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Bear witness that I am his heir and he is my heir." So he continued to be called Zayd ibn Muhammad, until the words of God Most High were revealed: "Call them by their fathers' names" (33:5), and "Muhammad is not the father of any man among you" (33:40).

The sixth issue: Abu al-Qasim 'Abd al-Rahman al-Suhayli, may God be pleased with him, said: He used to be called Zayd ibn Muhammad until the verse "Call them by their fathers' names" (33:5) was revealed, and he said: "I am Zayd ibn Harithah." It became forbidden for him to say: "I am Zayd ibn Muhammad." When this honour and this pride were taken from him, and God knew his distress over that, He honoured him with a distinction that He did not grant to any other of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ). It is that He named him in the Qur'an, saying: "So when Zayd had no further need of her" (33:37), meaning of Zaynab. Whoever God Most High names in the Wise Remembrance, until his name becomes a Qur'an recited in the prayer niches, has been exalted by Him to the utmost exaltation. In this there was consolation for him and compensation for the pride of being the son of Muhammad (ﷺ). Do you not see the words of Ubayy ibn Ka'b when the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "God has commanded me to recite to you the surah such-and-such"? He wept and said: "Was I mentioned there?" His weeping was from joy when he was told that God Most High had mentioned him. So what of one whose name became a Qur'an recited, eternal and not perishing, recited by the people of this world when they read the Qur'an, and by the people of Paradise likewise forever? It remains on the tongues of the believers, just as it has remained specially mentioned before the Lord of the worlds. For the Qur'an is the eternal Word of God, and it remains and does not perish. So the name of this Zayd is in the honoured, exalted, purified pages, which the noble, righteous scribes (safarah) mention in recitation. This is not granted to the name of any believer except a prophet among the prophets. It is a compensation from God Most High to Zayd ibn Harithah for what was taken from him. In the verse He added: "And when you said to him on whom God had bestowed favour" (33:37), that is, with faith. This shows that he was among the people of Paradise, and that God knew this before he died. This is another virtue.

The seventh issue: God's words "wataran" (33:37). Al-watar is every need a person has in which he has a strong aspiration, and its plural is al-awtar. Ibn 'Abbas said: that is, he reached what he wanted of his need, meaning intercourse. There is an ellipsis in it, meaning: when he had fulfilled his need of her and divorced her, "We gave her to you in marriage." The reading of the Ahl al-Bayt is "I gave her to you in marriage." It was also said: al-watar is an expression for divorce; this was said by Qatadah.

The eighth issue: Some people derived from this verse, and from the words of Shu'ayb: "I want to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine" (28:27), that the proper order of this meaning in the dowries should be: "He married her to him," with the pronoun of the husband placed first, as in the two verses. Likewise the Prophet's words (peace be upon him) to the man with the cloak: "Go, I have married her to you for what you know of the Qur'an." Ibn 'Atiyyah said: This is not binding, because in the verse the husband is addressed, so it is good to mention him first; but in the dowries the two spouses are equal, so mention whichever you wish. No preference remains except by the degree of men, and that they are the protectors (qawwamun).

The ninth issue: God's words "We gave her to you in marriage" (33:37) are evidence for the establishment of a guardian (wali) in marriage, and the disagreement on this has already been mentioned [[See vol. 3, p. 72 onwards.]]. It is related that 'A'ishah and Zaynab boasted, and 'A'ishah said: "I am the one whom the angel brought to the Prophet (ﷺ) in a silk cloth (sariqah), and he said: 'This is your wife.'" Al-Sahih related it. Zaynab said: "I am the one whom God married off from above the seven heavens." Al-Sha'bi said: Zaynab used to say to the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "I take pride over you in three things, which none of your wives can claim: my grandfather and your grandfather are one; God married you to me from the heavens; and the envoy in that was Jibril." It is related from Zaynab that she said: "When I settled in the heart of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), Zayd could not overpower me; and I was not refusing him except in what God Most High prevents him from doing to me, so he cannot prevail over me."

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 38–39:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The way of Allah with those who passed away before﴾. This is an address from Allah, exalted is He, to the whole Muslim community (ummah). He informed them that this and the like is the ancient custom (sunan) concerning the prophets, that they should attain what Allah made lawful for them. That is, the broadening (tawsi'ah) granted to Muhammad ﷺ in marriage was made a custom (sunnah) like the customs of the earlier prophets, such as Dawud and Sulayman. Dawud had one hundred wives and three hundred concubines (suriyyah), and Sulayman had three hundred wives and seven hundred concubines. Al-Tha'labi related from Muqatil and Ibn al-Kalbi that the reference is to Dawud, peace be upon him, when Allah brought together him and those with whom he was tested.

"Sunnata" is in the accusative as an infinitive (masdar), meaning: Allah prescribed for him a broad custom. "Those who passed away" (alladhina khalaw) are the prophets, as evidenced by their being described afterward in His saying: ﴿who convey the messages of Allah﴾.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 40:

There are three issues (masa'il) in it.

The first: When he married Zaynab, people said, "He has married his son's wife." So the verse was revealed, meaning: he is not the father of any of them in the sense that his wife becomes forbidden to him by that relationship. Rather, he is the father of his community (ummah) in honour and reverence, and his wives are forbidden to them. Through this verse, Allah removed what had settled in the hearts of the hypocrites and others, and He made known that Muhammad was not in reality the father of any of the men of his time. This verse does not intend to say that the Prophet ﷺ had no sons, for males were born to him: Ibrahim, al-Qasim, al-Tayyib and al-Mutahhar. But no son of his lived to reach manhood. As for al-Hasan and al-Husayn, they were children, and they were not grown men contemporary with him.

The second: His exalted saying, ﴿but the Messenger of Allah﴾. Al-Akhfash and al-Farra' said: meaning, "but he was the Messenger of Allah." They also permitted "wa-lakin rasulu Allah wa-khatamu" with the nominative case (raf'). Likewise Ibn Abi 'Ablah and some people read "wa-lakin rasulu Allah" in the nominative, meaning "he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets." A group read "wa-lakinna" with a doubled nun and "rasula Allah" in the accusative, taking it as the subject of "lakinna," with the predicate omitted. "Wa-khatama" (with a fatha on the ta'): 'Asim alone read it with a fatha, meaning that they were sealed by him, so he is like the seal and stamp for them. The majority read it with a kasra on the ta', meaning that he sealed them, that is, he came last of them. It is said that al-khatam and al-khatim are two dialects, like taba' and tabi', daniq and daniq, and tabaq min al-lahm and tabiq.

The third: Ibn 'Atiyyah said: these expressions are, among the scholars of the community (ulama al-ummah), both earlier and later, received in complete generality, explicitly indicating that there is no prophet after him ﷺ. What al-Qadi Abu al-Tayyib mentioned in his book named al-Hidayah, permitting the possibility of other readings of the words of this verse, is weak. What al-Ghazali mentioned concerning this verse and this meaning in his book which he named al-Iqtisad is, in my view, heresy (ilhad) and a wicked approach to confusing the Muslims' belief in the finality of Muhammad's ﷺ prophethood. So beware, beware of it! And Allah is the Guide by His mercy.

I say: It has been related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "There is no prophethood after me except what Allah wills." Abu 'Umar said: he means dream visions (al-ru'ya), Allah knows best, which are a part of prophethood, as he ﷺ said: "Nothing will remain of prophethood after me except the good dream."

Ibn Mas'ud read: "min rijalikum, wa-lakin nabiyyan khatama al-nabiyyin." Al-Rummani said: by him ﷺ, the process of reform (al-istislah) was sealed; whoever is not reformed by him is despaired of being reformed.

I say: From this meaning is his ﷺ saying: "I was sent to perfect noble character." In Sahih Muslim, from Jabir, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "My example and the example of the prophets is like a man who built a house, completed it and perfected it, except for the place of one brick. The people began to enter it and marvel at it, saying, 'If only the place of the brick were filled!' — the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said — 'So I am the place of the brick; I came and sealed the prophets.'" A similar report is from Abu Hurayrah, except that he said: "So I am the brick, and I am the seal of the prophets."

Allah, exalted is He, commanded His servants to remember Him and to be thankful to Him, and to do so abundantly in return for the blessings He has bestowed upon them. Allah, exalted is He, made this without a fixed limit because it is easy for the servant, and because of the great reward attached to it. Ibn 'Abbas said: No one is excused for neglecting the remembrance of Allah except the one whose intellect has been overcome (i.e., one who has lost his mind). Abu Sa'id narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Remember Allah abundantly until they say, 'He is mad.'" It has also been said: abundant remembrance is that which proceeds from the heart with sincerity (ikhlas), while little remembrance is that which occurs in the manner of hypocrisy (nifaq), such as remembrance with the tongue alone.

That is: keep your tongues occupied for most of your times with tasbih (glorifying God, saying subhan Allah), tahlil (saying la ilaha illa Allah), tahmid (saying al-hamdu lillah) and takbir (saying Allahu akbar). Mujahid said: "These are words that the one in a state of purity, the one who has broken wudu, and the one in a state of major impurity (junub) may all say." It was also said: "Supplicate Him." Jarir said: "So do not neglect the tasbih of the forenoon (duha), for Yusuf supplicated his Lord and was chosen when he glorified Him."

It was also said: the meaning is "pray to God in the morning and the evening," and prayer is called tasbih. The fajr, maghrib and 'isha' prayers were singled out for mention because they are most deserving of being urged, since they are connected to the ends of the night [[In K: (with the ends of the day).]]. Qatadah and al-Tabari said: the reference is to the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer. Al-Asil means al-'ashi (the evening), and its plural is asa'il. Al-Usul is synonymous with al-asil, and its plural is al-asal, as stated by al-Mubarrad. Others said: Usul is the plural of asil, like raghif and rughuf. This has already been discussed [[See vol. 7, p. 355]].

Issue: This verse is Madinan, so there is no basis for those who claim that prayer was originally obligatory only as two prayers, at the two ends of the day. The narration to that effect is weak, so it should be neither considered nor relied upon. The discussion of how prayer was made obligatory, and what the scholars have said about it, has already passed in the commentary on Surat Subhan [[See vol. 10, p. 210]]. And praise be to God.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 43:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It is He who sends blessings upon you﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: When ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet﴾ [al-Ahzab: 56] was revealed, the Muhajirun and the Ansar said: "This is for you alone, O Messenger of Allah, and we have no share in it." So Allah, Exalted is He, revealed this verse. I say: This is a blessing from Allah, Exalted is He, upon this Ummah, one of the greatest of blessings, and evidence of its excellence [in some manuscripts: its virtue] over all other nations. He has said: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 110]. The blessing (salah) of Allah upon the servant is His mercy towards him and His favour concerning him. The blessing of the angels is their supplication for the believers and their seeking forgiveness for them, as He said: ﴿And they seek forgiveness for those who believe﴾ [Ghafir: 7], and it will come. In a hadith: The Children of Israel asked Musa (peace be upon him): "Does your Lord send blessings?" He regarded that as great, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "Indeed My blessing is that My mercy precedes My wrath." Mentioned by al-Nahhas. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: A group narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the blessing of Allah upon His servants?" He said: "Subbuh, Quddus, My mercy precedes My wrath." There has been disagreement about the interpretation of this saying. It is said: it is a word from the speech of Allah, Exalted is He, and it is His blessing upon His servants. It is also said: "Subbuh, Quddus" is from the speech of Muhammad (ﷺ), and he placed it before uttering the phrase which is the blessing of Allah, namely "My mercy precedes My wrath," because he understood from the questioner that he had conceived of an aspect of Allah's blessing upon His servants unbefitting Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so he placed the declaration of His transcendence and glorification before informing him.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That He may bring you out from darknesses into the light﴾. That is, from misguidance to guidance. The meaning of this is steadfastness upon guidance, because at the time of address they were upon guidance. Then Allah, Exalted is He, informed of His mercy towards the believers, as a comfort to them, saying: ﴿And ever is He merciful to the believers﴾.

The pronoun in "yalqawnahu" (they meet him): there is disagreement about what it refers back to. It was said that it refers to God, Exalted is He, meaning: He is merciful to the believers, so He grants them security from the punishment of God on the Day of Resurrection, and on that Day they meet Him. "Tahiyyatuhum" means the greeting of some of them to others. "Salam" means safety for us and for you from the punishment of God.

It was also said: this greeting is from God, Exalted is He. The meaning is: He greets them with safety from calamities, or He gives them the good news of security from what they fear. "Yawma yalqawnahu" means on the Day of Resurrection, after their entry into Paradise. Al-Zajjaj said this is its meaning, and he cited the words of God, Exalted and Majestic: ﴿And their greeting therein is "Peace"﴾ [Yunus: 10] [[see vol. 8, p. 313]].

It was also said: "yawma yalqawnahu" means the day they meet the Angel of Death. It has been reported that he does not seize the soul of a believer without greeting him with peace. It is narrated from al-Bara' ibn Azib, who said: "Their greeting on the day they meet Him is 'Peace'" — the Angel of Death greets the believer at the seizing of his soul, and he does not seize his soul until he has greeted him.

This verse contains consolation for the Prophet ﷺ and the believers, and honour for all of them. This verse includes six of his names ﷺ. Our Prophet ﷺ has many names and noble attributes, which are mentioned in the Qur'an, the Sunnah, and the earlier scriptures. Allah named him in His Book Muhammad and Ahmad. The Prophet ﷺ said, as reliable and trustworthy narrators reported from him: "I have five names: I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am al-Mahi (the Eraser), through whom Allah erases disbelief; I am al-Hashir (the Gatherer), at whose feet people will be gathered; and I am al-Aqib (the Last)." In Sahih Muslim, in the hadith of Jubayr ibn Mut'im, [it is stated that] Allah named him ﴿compassionate and merciful﴾. Also in it, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to name himself to us, saying: "I am Muhammad, Ahmad, al-Muqaffi (the Successor), al-Hashir (the Gatherer), the Prophet of repentance, and the Prophet of mercy." Al-Qadi Abu al-Fadl Iyad traced, in his book called al-Shifa, what came in the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ, and what was transmitted in the earlier [[In another manuscript: (the ancient)]] scriptures, and the community's application of many names and numerous attributes to him ﷺ. Their referents apply to him ﷺ, and their meanings are found in him. Al-Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi mentioned in his Ahkam, regarding this verse, sixty-seven names of the Prophet ﷺ. The author of Wasilat al-Mutabbidin ila Mutaba'at Sayyid al-Mursalin reported from Ibn Abbas that Muhammad ﷺ has one hundred and eighty names; whoever wishes to see them will find them there. Ibn Abbas said: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called Ali and Mu'adh, sent them to Yemen, and said: "Go, give good news and do not cause aversion, make things easy and do not make them difficult, for it has been revealed to me..." and he recited this verse.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿a witness﴾. Sa'id reported from Qatadah: "a witness" over his community through conveying the message to them, and over the rest of the nations through the conveying of their prophets' messages, and similar things. ﴿A bringer of good news﴾ means to the believers, of Allah's mercy and of Paradise. ﴿A warner﴾ means to the disobedient and the deniers, of the Fire and the torment of eternity.

﴿And as one who calls to Allah﴾: calling to Allah is conveying tawhid (monotheism), adhering to it, and confronting the disbelievers. ﴿By His permission﴾ here means: by His command to you and His decree of that at its proper time. ﴿And as a radiant lamp﴾ here is a metaphor for the light contained in His law.

It was said: "and a lamp" means a guide out of the darkness of misguidance, and you are like a shining lamp. He was described with illumination because some lamps do not give light when their oil (sulayt: oil) is scant and their wick is thin. In the words of some people: three things waste away: a messenger who is slow, a lamp that gives no light, and a table for which one waits for someone to come. Some people were asked about the two lonely ones, and they said: "a concealing darkness and a faint lamp." Al-Nahhas reported with a chain of narration: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Razi told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Salih al-Azdi told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi told us, from Shayban al-Nahwi, he said: Qatadah told us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the verse "O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness, a bringer of good news, and a warner, and as one who calls to Allah by His permission, and as a radiant lamp" was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called Ali and Mu'adh and said: "Set out, give good news and do not make things difficult, for tonight there has been revealed to me the verse: 'O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness, a bringer of good news, and a warner'" — [warner] from the Fire — and "as one who calls to Allah" — he said: the testimony that there is no god but Allah — "by His permission" — by His command — and "as a radiant lamp" — he said: by the Qur'an. Al-Zajjaj said: "and a lamp" means "and one possessing a radiant lamp," that is, a luminous Book. He also permitted that it mean: "and reciting the Book of Allah."

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 47–48:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾. The waw here is conjunctive, joining one clause to another, and the meaning is detached from what precedes it. He, exalted is He, commanded him to give good tidings to the believers of a great bounty from Allah, exalted is He. According to the view of al-Zajjaj, that it is "a lamp that gives light" (dhā sirājin munīr), or "and as one who calls, a light giving light" (wa-tāliyan sirājan munīran), it is governed by the kaf (you) and not by "We have sent you." Ibn 'Atiyyah said: My father, may Allah be pleased with him, said to us: "This is among the most hopeful verses in the Book of Allah, exalted is He, in my view, because Allah, mighty and majestic, has commanded His Prophet to give good tidings to the believers that they have with Him a great bounty. Allah, exalted is He, has explained the great bounty in His saying: ﴿But those who believe and do righteous deeds, they will have gardens of Paradise beneath which rivers flow; therein they will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty﴾ [al-Shura: 22] [[See vol. 16, p. (20)]]. So the verse in this surah is a report, and the one in Ha-Mim 'Ayn-Sin-Qaf is its explanation."

(And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites) That is, do not obey them in what they suggest to you of compromise in religion, and do not side with them. "The disbelievers": Abu Sufyan, 'Ikrimah and Abu al-A'war al-Sulami, who said: "O Muhammad, do not mention our gods with evil, and we will follow you." "The hypocrites": 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'd and Tu'mah ibn Ubayriq, who urged the Prophet (ﷺ) to accede to them under the pretext of public interest. (And leave off their harm) That is, leave off harming them in recompense for their harm to you. Thus He commanded him to abandon punishing them and to pardon their faults. On this interpretation the verbal noun is in the genitive of the object. On this interpretation, what concerns the disbelievers is abrogated from the verse, and its abrogating verse is the verse of the sword. There is a second meaning: turn away from their statements and what they inflict upon you, and do not occupy yourself with it. On this interpretation the verbal noun is in the genitive of the subject. This is the interpretation of Mujahid, and the verse is abrogated by the verse of the sword.

(And put your trust in Allah) He commanded him to rely upon Him and reassured him with His saying: "And sufficient is Allah as Guardian." The sense of the speech implies a promise of victory. The wakil is the one who protects and stands in charge of a matter.

There are seven issues in this passage.

The first concerns the words of God, ﴿O you who believe, when you marry believing women and then divorce them﴾. When the story of Zayd and his divorce of Zaynab came up, and she had been consummated with, and the Prophet (ﷺ) proposed to her after the end of her waiting period ('iddah, the period a divorced or widowed woman must observe before remarriage), as we have explained, God addressed the believers about the ruling for a wife who is divorced before consummation, and made that ruling clear to the community. So a divorced woman who has not been touched has no 'iddah, by the explicit text of the Book and the consensus (ijma', scholarly agreement) of the community on this. If he has consummated the marriage with her, then she has an 'iddah by consensus.

The second concerns the word nikah (marriage). It is literally used for sexual intercourse, and the contract is called nikah because it is connected to it, in that it is the means leading to it. A parallel is calling wine (khamr) sin (ithm),[[Khamr: it is used in both the feminine and masculine forms, with the feminine being more common.]] because it causes the commission of sin. The word nikah does not occur in God's Book except in the sense of the contract, since it is used in the sense of intercourse. It is among the courtesies of the Qur'an to refer to intercourse indirectly, using the words mulamasah (touching), mumassah (contact), qurban (approaching), taghshi (covering) and ityan (coming to).

The third issue: some scholars used God's words, "then you divorce them," and the delay implied by the particle "then" (thumma) to argue that divorce can only occur after a marriage, and that whoever divorces a woman before marrying her, even if he specifies her, is not bound by it. This was said by more than thirty people among the Companions, Successors and imams. Al-Bukhari named twenty-two of them,[[The number of those al-Bukhari named under the chapter "There is no divorce before marriage" is twenty-four.]] and a hadith is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ): "There is no divorce before marriage," meaning that divorce does not take effect until a marriage has taken place. Habib ibn Abi Thabit said: Ali ibn al-Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them both, was asked about a man who said to a woman, "If I marry you, you are divorced." He said: "It is nothing, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned marriage before divorce." Another group of scholars said that a divorce of a specific person, tribe or town is binding even before marriage. Among them are Malik and all his companions, and a great number of the scholars of the community. The discussion of this and the evidence of both sides has passed in (the chapter) "Bara'ah" [[See vol. 8, p. 211.]], and praise be to Allah. If he says, "Every woman I marry is divorced," and "Every slave I buy is free," nothing is binding on him. But if he says, "Every woman I marry within twenty years," or "If I marry from the town of so-and-so or from the clan of so-and-so, she is divorced," then divorce is binding on him, as long as he does not fear for himself the distress (anat, sin or hardship) over the long years, or unless his life in general will not last that long, in which case he may marry. Divorce is not binding on him when he generalises because he has restricted his own options for marriage. If we prevented him from marrying, he would be harmed and would fear for himself distress. Some of our companions said that if he finds what he can use as a concubine, he should not marry, but this is not correct, because necessities and valid excuses lift rulings. So this is, in terms of necessity, like someone who has not sworn an oath. This was said by Ibn Khuwayz Mandad.

The fourth issue: Dawud and those who agree with him argued that if a woman with a revocable divorce is taken back by her husband before her 'iddah ends, and then he divorces her before touching her, she does not have to complete her 'iddah or observe a new one, because she is a woman divorced before consummation. Atta ibn Abi Rabah and a group said she continues her 'iddah from her first divorce, which is one of the two opinions of al-Shafi'i, because his divorce of her when he has not touched her is in the ruling of one who divorced her during her 'iddah before taking her back. Whoever divorces his wife once in each tuhr (the purity period between menstrual cycles) has her continue and not start afresh. Malik said: if he separates from her before touching her, she does not build on what has passed of her 'iddah, but begins a new 'iddah from the day he divorced her. Her husband has wronged himself and erred if he took her back when he had no need of her. Most scholars hold this view, because she is in the ruling of wives who have been consummated in terms of maintenance (nafaqah), lodging and other matters, and therefore she starts a new 'iddah from the day she was divorced. This is the view of the majority of jurists of Basra, Kufa, Mecca, Medina and Syria. Al-Thawri said: "The jurists in our land have agreed on this."

The fifth issue: if she was ba'in (irrevocably divorced) but not mabtutah (absolutely divorced, having no further rights),[[Ba'in: divorce that is irrevocable or final, while mabtutah is the absolute divorce.]] and he marries her again during her 'iddah and then divorces her before consummation, scholars differ on this as well. Malik, al-Shafi'i, Zufar and Uthman al-Batti said: she has half the dowry (sadaq) and completes the rest of the first 'iddah. This is the view of al-Hasan, Ata', Ikrimah and Ibn Shihab. Abu Hanifah, Abu Yusuf, al-Thawri and al-Awza'i said: she has a full dowry for the second marriage and a new 'iddah, because they treated her as one who has been consummated, since she is observing 'iddah from his water. Dawud said: she has half the dowry, and she does not have to complete the first 'iddah or observe a new one. The more correct view is that of Malik and al-Shafi'i, and God knows best.

The sixth issue: this verse specifies the general statement of God, ﴿And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three periods﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:228], and His words, ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you doubt, their 'iddah is three months﴾ [al-Talaq 65:4]. This has passed in (the commentary on) "al-Baqarah" [[See vol. 3, p. 112 onwards, and p. 200 onwards.]], and the discussion of mut'ah (provision for a divorced woman) has passed there too [[See vol. 3, p. 112 onwards, and p. 200 onwards.]], so there is no need to repeat it here. ﴿And release them with a fair release﴾ has two interpretations. The first is that it means giving them mut'ah according to one's means and hardship; this was said by Ibn Abbas. The second is that it means divorcing her while she is in a state of purity without having had intercourse; this was said by Qatadah. It was also said: "release them" after the divorce to their families, so that a man and a divorced woman do not gather in one place. The seventh issue: God's words, ﴿then provide for them﴾. Sa'id said: it has been abrogated (mansukh, nullified by a later ruling, naskh) by the verse in al-Baqarah, which is His words, ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them, and you have already appointed for them a portion, then half of what you appointed﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:237], meaning that mut'ah is not mentioned there. The discussion of this has been completed in (the commentary on) "al-Baqarah" [[See vol. 3, p. 204 and p. 125.]]. As for His words, "release them," it means divorce them. Release (tasrih) is an indirect expression (kinayah) for divorce according to Abu Hanifah, because it is used in other senses, so it requires the intention. According to al-Shafi'i it is an explicit (sarih) expression. The discussion of this has passed in (the commentary on) "al-Baqarah," so there is no need to repeat it [[See vol. 3, p. 204 and p. 125.]]. "A fair release": a sunnah (prescribed practice), not an innovation (bid'ah).

In it there are nineteen issues.

**First:** Al-Suddi narrated from Abu Salih, from Umm Hani bint Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed to me, and I excused myself to him [[She said: "I am a woman with children (dhat sibyan)." In some narrations she said: "O Messenger of Allah, you are dearer to me than my hearing and my sight, but the right of a husband is great, and I fear that I may neglect the right of the husband."]], so he excused me. Then Allah the Exalted revealed: "Indeed, We have made lawful for you your wives whose bridal payments you have given, and those whom your right hand possesses from what Allah has returned to you (as spoils), and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts, and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts, who emigrated with you." She said: So I was not lawful for him, because I had not emigrated; I was among the Freed (al-Tulaqa'). Abu Isa (al-Tirmidhi) narrated it and said: This is a hasan hadith; we do not know it except through this route. Ibn al-'Arabi said: It is very weak, and this hadith has not come through a sound route that can be relied upon as evidence.

**Second:** When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave his wives the choice and they chose him, it was forbidden for him to marry others in place of them or to exchange them, as a reward to them for their action. The evidence for this is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Women are not lawful for you after this﴾, the verse. Was it lawful for him to divorce one of them after that? It was said: He may not do so, as a recompense to them for their choosing him. It was also said: It was lawful for him to do so, as with other men, but he could not marry another in her place. Then this prohibition was abrogated (naskh), and he was permitted to marry whomever he wished of women in addition to them. The evidence for this is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have made lawful for you your wives﴾, and "making lawful" (al-ihlal) implies a prior prohibition. His wives who were with him during his lifetime had not been forbidden to him; rather, what had been forbidden to him was marrying strangers, so the "making lawful" was directed towards them. Also, He said in the context of the verse: "and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts," and so on. It is known that none of the daughters of his paternal uncles, paternal aunts, maternal uncles or maternal aunts were ever married to him, so it is established that marrying these was made lawful for him from the outset. Although this verse comes first in the recitation, it was revealed later than the abrogated verse it abrogates, like the two verses on death in "al-Baqarah" (see vol. 3, pp. 273 and 226). People have differed in interpreting the saying of Allah the Exalted: "Indeed, We have made lawful for you your wives." It was said: What is meant is that Allah the Exalted made lawful for him to marry every woman to whom he gives her dower; this was said by Ibn Zayd and al-Dahhak. On this view, the verse permits all women except those within the prohibited degrees (dhawat al-mahram). It was also said: What is meant is: We have made lawful for you your wives, that is, those who are present with you, because they have chosen you over this world and the Hereafter; this was said by the majority of scholars. This is the apparent meaning, because His saying "whose bridal payments you have given" is in the past tense, and a past-tense verb does not carry the meaning of the future except under certain conditions.
