On this interpretation the command is restrictive for the Prophet (ﷺ). This interpretation is supported by what Ibn 'Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to marry from among the people whomever he wished, and this distressed his wives. When this verse was revealed, and women other than those named were forbidden to him by it, his wives were delighted by that. I say: The first view is more correct for the reasons we have mentioned. Also, what al-Tirmidhi narrated from 'Ata' supports its soundness: he said, A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not die until Allah the Exalted had made women lawful for him. He said: This is a hasan sahih hadith.

**Third:** His saying: ﴿and those whom your right hand possesses﴾. Allah the Exalted made concubines lawful for His Prophet (ﷺ) and for his community without restriction, and He made wives lawful for His Prophet, peace be upon him, without restriction, while for other creatures He made them lawful within a specified number. His saying "from what Allah has returned to you" means: that which He returned to you from the unbelievers. Spoils of war are sometimes called fay' (returned property), that is: from what Allah has returned to you of women taken by force and conquest.

**Fourth:** His saying: ﴿and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts﴾. That is, We have made this lawful for you in addition to the wives whose bridal payments you have given and those whom your right hand possesses, according to the view of the majority. This is because if He had meant "We have made lawful for you every woman you marry and whose bridal payment you have given," He would not have said after that: "and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts," since these are included in what came before. I say: This objection does not apply; rather, these were singled out for mention to honour them, just as He said: ﴿In both of them are fruit and date palms and pomegranates﴾ [al-Rahman: 68] (see vol. 17, p. 185). And Allah knows best.

**Fifth:** His saying the Exalted: (who emigrated with you). There are two views concerning this. The first: It is not lawful for you from among your relatives, such as the daughters of your paternal uncle al-'Abbas and others from the sons of 'Abd al-Muttalib, and the daughters of the sons of the daughters of 'Abd al-Muttalib, and the daughters of the maternal uncle from the sons of the daughters of 'Abd Manaf ibn Zuhrah, except those who embraced Islam, because of the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe, and the emigrant (muhajir) is one who abandons what Allah the Exalted has forbidden." The second: It is not lawful for you from among them except those who emigrated to Medina, because of the saying of Allah the Exalted: "And those who believed but did not emigrate, you have no guardianship over them at all until they emigrate" [[See vol. 8, p. 55.]]. Whoever has not emigrated has not been perfected, and whoever has not been perfected is not fit for the Prophet (ﷺ), who was perfected, honoured and exalted, (ﷺ).

**Sixth:** His saying: ﴿with you﴾. The "being with" (al-ma'iyyah) here means sharing in the emigration, not accompanying one another in it. Whoever emigrated was made lawful for him, whether or not he was in company with him when he emigrated. One says: So-and-so entered with me and left with me, meaning his action was like my action even if your two actions were not joined together. If you said, "We went out together," this would imply both meanings: sharing in the act and being united in it.

**Seventh:** Allah, blessed and exalted, mentioned the paternal uncle in the singular and the paternal aunts in the plural. Likewise He said: (maternal uncle) and (maternal aunts). The wisdom in this is that "paternal uncle" (al-'amm) and "maternal uncle" (al-khal), in general usage, are collective nouns like "the poet" and "the reciter of rajaz verse," whereas "paternal aunt" (al-'ammah) and "maternal aunt" (al-khalah) are not like that. This is a linguistic convention, and the speech came in its clearest form to remove any ambiguity. This is subtle, so consider it carefully; so said Ibn al-'Arabi.

**Eighth:** His saying: ﴿and a believing woman﴾ is coordinated with "We have made lawful". The meaning is: and We have made lawful for you a woman who gives herself (to you) without a dowry. This meaning has been disputed. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: No woman was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) except by a marriage contract or by right of ownership (milk yamin). As for gifting (hibah), none of them was with him. Others said: There was with him a woman who had been gifted. I say: What is in the two Sahihs strengthens and supports this latter view. Muslim narrated from A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) that she said: I used to be jealous of those who had given themselves to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I would say: Is a woman not ashamed to give herself to a man? Until Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿You may postpone whom you will of them and take to you whom you will﴾ [al-Ahzab: 51], and I said: By Allah, I see that your Lord only hastens to satisfy your desire. Al-Bukhari narrated from A'ishah that she said: Khawlah bint Hakim was among those who gave themselves to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This indicates that they were more than one. And Allah knows best. Al-Zamakhshari said: It has been said that the women who were gifted were four: Maymunah bint al-Harith, Zaynab bint Khuzaymah Umm al-Masakin al-Ansariyyah, Umm Sharik bint Jabir, and Khawlah bint Hakim.

I say: There is some disagreement about some of this. Qatadah said: She was Maymunah bint al-Harith. Al-Sha'bi said: She was Zaynab bint Khuzaymah Umm al-Masakin, a woman from the Ansar. 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: She was Umm Sharik bint Jabir al-Asadiyyah. 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr said: She was Umm Hakim bint al-Awqas al-Sulamiyyah.

**Ninth:** There is disagreement about the name of the woman who gave herself. It was said: She was Umm Sharik al-Ansariyyah, whose name was Ghuzayyah. It was also said: Ghuzaylah. It was said: Layla bint Hakim. It was also said: She was Maymunah bint al-Harith, when the Prophet (ﷺ) proposed to her; the proposer came to her while she was on her camel, and she said: The camel and what is on it belong to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It was said: She was Umm Sharik al-'Amiriyyah, who was married to Abu al-'Akar al-Azdi; it was also said she was with al-Tufayl ibn al-Harith and bore him a son, Sharik. It was said that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married her, but this has not been established. And Allah knows best; this was mentioned by Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr. Al-Sha'bi and 'Urwah said: She was Zaynab bint Khuzaymah, Umm al-Masakin. And Allah knows best.

**Tenth:** Most people recited "in wahabat" (if she gives herself) with a kasrah on the alif (إِنْ). This implies a new beginning of the matter, meaning: if it occurs, then it is lawful for him. It has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid that they said: No woman who had been gifted was with the Prophet (ﷺ). We have already shown the opposite. The imams narrated, through the route of Sahl and others, in the authentic collections, that a woman said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "I have come to give myself to you." He remained silent until a man stood up and said: "Marry her to me, if you have no need of her." Had this gift not been permissible, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not have remained silent, for he does not approve of falsehood when he hears it. Yet it is possible that his silence was awaiting clarification, and then the verse was revealed with the permission and the option, and he chose to leave her and married her to someone else. It is also possible that he remained silent, reflecting on the matter, until the man stood up asking for her. Al-Hasan al-Basri, Ubayy ibn Ka'b and al-Sha'bi recited "an" (أَنْ) with a fatha on the alif. Al-A'mash recited "wamra'atan mu'minatan wahabat" (and a believing woman who gave herself). Al-Nahhas said: The kasrah of "in" is more comprehensive in meaning, because it has been said that they were women (in general). When it is read with a fatha, the meaning refers to one specific woman, because the fatha is in apposition to "a woman," or it has the sense of "because" (li-anna).

**The Eleventh:** His, may He be exalted, saying, ﴿believing﴾, indicates that a disbelieving woman is not lawful to him. Imam al-Haramayn said: There has been disagreement over whether a free disbelieving woman is forbidden to him. Ibn al-'Arabi said: The correct view, in my opinion, is that she is forbidden to him. By this he is distinguished over us, for whatever is on the side of virtues and honor, his share in it is greater, and whatever is on the side of deficiencies, his side is purer from them. So marrying free women from the People of the Book was permitted for us, while for him, ﷺ, because of his exalted rank, it was restricted to believing women. And if one who did not emigrate is not lawful to him, because of the deficiency in the merit of emigration, then it is more fitting that a disbelieving woman, a free woman of the People of the Book, is not lawful to him, because of the deficiency of disbelief.

**The Twelfth:** His, may He be exalted, saying, ﴿if she gives herself in gift﴾, is evidence that marriage is a contract of exchange upon specific attributes, which has been discussed earlier in "al-Nisa'" [[See vol. 5, p. 127 onward.]] and elsewhere. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of "if she gives herself in gift to the Prophet" is that she becomes lawful. Al-Hasan recited "an wahabat" with a fatha on the hamza. The "an" is in the accusative position. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, "because." Others said: "in wahabat" is a substitution of inclusion (badal ishtimal) for "imra'atan" (a woman).

**The Thirteenth:** His, may He be exalted, saying, ﴿if the Prophet desires to marry her﴾, means: if a woman gives herself in gift and the Prophet, ﷺ, accepts her, she becomes lawful to him; but if he does not accept her, that is not binding on him. This is like when you gift a man something, he is not obliged to accept it. Nevertheless, it is among the noble characteristics of our Prophet that he accepts a gift from the one who gives it. Men of honor regard refusing it as a disgrace in custom, a stain upon the giver, and a harm to his heart. So God clarified that regarding His Messenger, ﷺ, and made it a Qur'an to be recited, to remove hardship from him, and to nullify the people's customs and sayings in their practice.

**The Fourteenth:** His, may He be exalted, saying, ﴿exclusively for you﴾, means: the gifting of women of themselves is exclusively and specially permitted to you, and not permitted [to others]. So it is not lawful for a woman to give herself in gift to a man. The aspect of this particularity is that if she requested the obligatory dower before consummation, she would not be entitled to it. As for among us, a woman who has delegated her dower (mufawwadah) may request her dower before consummation, and the equivalent dower (mahr al-mithl) after consummation.

**The Fifteenth:** The scholars have reached consensus (ijma') that a woman's gifting of herself is not permissible [[i.e., it is an impermissible matter.]], and that this wording of gift does not complete a marriage contract, except what is reported from Abu Hanifa and his two companions, for they said: If she gives herself in gift and he makes himself a witness to a dower, that is permissible. Ibn 'Atiyya said: Their statement is nothing but a permission of expression and of the word "gift." Otherwise, the acts they required are the very acts of marriage. This issue has been discussed fully in "al-Qasas" [[See vol. 13, p. 272.]]. And praise be to God.

**The Sixteenth:** God, may He be exalted, distinguished His Messenger in the rulings of the Sharia with meanings in which no one shared with him, in the domain of obligation, prohibition, and permissibility, a distinction over the Ummah [[In Ibn al-'Arabi: "and a gift (wahibah) given to him."]] that was given to him, and a rank with which he was singled out. Certain things were obligatory upon him that were not obligatory upon others, certain acts were forbidden to him that were not forbidden to them, and certain things were made lawful to him that were not made lawful to them, some of which are agreed upon and some of which are disputed.

As for what was made obligatory upon him, it is nine: The first is the night prayer (tahajjud). It is said that the night vigil was obligatory upon him until he died, based on His saying, ﴿O you who wrap yourself, stand [in prayer] the night﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 1–2], to the end of the verse. The established position is that it was obligatory upon him, then it was abrogated (naskh) by His saying, ﴿And from the night, pray with it as a supererogatory act for you﴾ [al-Isra': 79], and it will come. The second is the forenoon prayer (duha). The third is the sacrifice (udhiyah). The fourth is the witr prayer, which falls under the category of tahajjud. The fifth is the siwak (tooth-cleaning). The sixth is paying the debt of one who died insolvent. The seventh is consulting people of understanding in matters other than the legal rulings (shara'i'). The eighth is choosing among women. The ninth is that when he did an act, he would confirm it. Another scholar added: It was also obligatory upon him that when he saw something reprehensible, he would denounce it and make it manifest, because his tacit approval of it for others would indicate its permissibility. This was mentioned by the author of "al-Bayan."

As for what was forbidden to him, its total is ten: The first is that zakat is forbidden to him and to his family. The second is voluntary charity (sadaqat al-tatawwu') to him, and regarding his family there is detail, with disagreement. The third is the "treachery of the eyes" (khA'inat al-a'yun), which is to show the opposite of what one conceals, or to deceive regarding what is obligatory. [[KhA'inah means treachery, and is among the verbal nouns that came in the form of the active participle, like 'afiyah. When a person restrains his tongue and gestures with his eye, he has betrayed; and when that state appears from the eye, it is called "treachery of the eyes."]] He once condemned some disbelievers when they asked permission, then spoke gently to him when he entered. [[See the books of al-Bukhari and Muslim (chapter on manners).]] The fourth: God forbade him, when he put on his armor [[al-lamah (its hamza may be dropped): armor. It is said: weapons.]], to take it off, or to let God judge between him and his enemy. The fifth is eating while reclining. The sixth is eating foods with foul odors. The seventh is exchanging his wives, which will come. The eighth is marrying a woman who dislikes his company. The ninth is marrying a free woman of the People of the Book. The tenth is marrying a slave woman.

God forbade him things He did not forbid to others, to exalt and purify him. So God forbade him writing and composing poetry and teaching it, to affirm his proof and to explain his miracle. God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿You did not recite before it any Book, nor did you write it with your right hand﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 48]. Al-Naqqash mentioned that the Prophet, ﷺ, did not die until he had written, but the first is the well-known view. And it was forbidden to him to extend his eyes toward what people have been given to enjoy. God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Do not extend your eyes toward what We have given to pairs of them﴾ [al-Hijr: 88], to the end of the verse.

As for what was made lawful to him, ﷺ, its total is sixteen: The first is the choice portion of the spoils (safi al-maghnam). The second is the exclusive right to a fifth of the fifth (khums al-khums) or the fifth. The third is continuous fasting (al-wisal). The fourth is exceeding four wives. The fifth is marriage with the wording of gift. The sixth is marriage without a guardian (wali). The seventh is marriage without a dower (sadaq). The eighth is marrying while in the state of ihram. The ninth is that the rotation (qasm) among wives was waived for him, which will come. The tenth: If his gaze fell upon a woman, her husband was obligated to divorce her, and it became lawful for him to marry her. Ibn al-'Arabi said: Thus said Imam al-Haramayn, and what the scholars said in the story of Zayd regarding this meaning has already passed. The eleventh: He freed Safiyyah and made her freedom her dower. The twelfth: His entering Makkah without ihram, and regarding us there is disagreement. The thirteenth: Fighting in Makkah. The fourteenth: That he is not inherited from. This was mentioned under the category of permissibility because when a man draws near death through illness, most of his property departs from him, and only the third remains exclusively his. The ownership of the Messenger of God, ﷺ, remained as has been established in its explanation in the verse of inheritance [[See vol. 5, p. 59.]], and in "Surat Maryam" [[See vol. 11, p. 18.]] its explanation also. The fifteenth: The continuation of his marital bond after death. The sixteenth: If he divorced a woman, his prohibition upon her remains, so she may not be married [to another]. These three categories, most of which were discussed in detail in their places earlier, will come again, God willing, may He be exalted. [And it was permitted for him, upon him be peace, to take food and drink from the hungry and thirsty, even if the one who is with him fears for his own life, based on His saying, ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than themselves﴾ [al-Ahzab: 6]. And it is obligatory upon every Muslim to protect the Prophet, ﷺ, with his own self. And it was permitted for him to reserve for himself [[In Sh: "bi-nafsihi" with ba' instead of lam, and the sentence is not clear.]]. God honored him by making the spoils lawful. The earth was made for him and for his Ummah a place of prostration and a purifier. Among the prophets there were some whose prayers were valid only in houses of worship. He was supported with awe, so the enemy feared him from a month's distance. He was sent to all of creation, whereas previously a prophet was sent to some people and not others. His miracles were made like the miracles of the prophets before him, and more. The miracle of Musa, peace be upon him, was the staff and the water gushing from the rock. The moon was split for the Prophet, ﷺ, and water flowed from between his fingers, ﷺ. The miracle of 'Isa, peace be upon him, was the raising of the dead and the healing of the blind and the leper. Pebbles glorified God in the hand of the Prophet, ﷺ, and the trunk of a palm tree yearned for him, and this is more eloquent. God favored him over them by making the Qur'an a miracle for him, and by making his miracle in it lasting until the Day of Resurrection. For this reason his prophethood was made eternal, not to be abrogated until the Day of Resurrection [[What is between the brackets is missing from j and k.]]].

**The Seventeenth:** His, may He be exalted, saying, ﴿that he marry her [yastankiha]﴾, means: that he marry her. It is said: nakaha and istankaha, like 'ajiba and ista'jaba, and 'ajila and ista'jala. It is possible that istinkah comes meaning seeking marriage or seeking intercourse. And ﴿exclusively﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal), said by al-Zajjaj. It was said: it is a state from a pronoun attached to a verb implied by the pronoun, its estimated form being: We made lawful for you your wives, and We made lawful for you a believing woman, which We made lawful exclusively by the wording of gift, without dower and without guardian.

**The Eighteenth:** His, may He be exalted, saying, ﴿apart from the believers﴾, its benefit is that the disbelievers, although according to us they are addressed by the secondary rulings of the Sharia, have no part in that, because the application of rulings concerning them is only upon the assumption of Islam.

His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿We have certainly known what We have enjoined upon them concerning their wives﴾, means: what We have obligated upon the believers, which is that they not marry more than four women, with a dower, a witness, and a guardian. Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Qatadah, and others said this.

**The Nineteenth:** His, may He be exalted, saying, ﴿so that there will be no difficulty for you﴾, means: no constriction in a matter in which you are in need of ease. That is, We explained this explanation and clarified this clarification, ﴿so that there will be no difficulty for you﴾. The phrase "li-kay" (so that) relates to His saying, "We have made lawful for you your wives," meaning: so that your heart will not be constricted, such that it appears from you that you have sinned before your Lord in something. Then God, may He be exalted, comforted all the believers with His forgiveness and mercy, saying, ﴿And God is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

There are eleven issues in it.

**First:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You may postpone whom you will of them﴾. It was read with hamza and without hamza, and both are dialects. It is said: *arjaytu al-amr* and *arja'tuhu* when one delays the matter. "*Wa tu'wi*" means "you take in" or "you shelter." It is said: *awa ilayhi* (with a long alif) meaning he took him in, and *awa* (with a short alif) meaning he took refuge with him.

**Second:** The scholars differed in interpreting this verse, and the most sound of what has been said about it is that it grants latitude to the Prophet (ﷺ) in abandoning the rotation (*qasm*), so that he was not obliged to observe rotation among his wives. This view agrees with what precedes it, and its meaning is established in the Sahih from ʿĀʾisha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: "I used to be jealous of those women who had given themselves to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I would say: 'Does a woman give herself to a man?' Then when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿You may postpone whom you will of them, and take to you whom you will, and whoever you desire of those you have set aside﴾, she said: 'I said: By Allah, I see that your Lord only hastens to gratify your desire.'"

Ibn al-ʿArabi said: "This which is established in the Sahih is what should be relied upon. The intended meaning is that the Prophet (ﷺ) had the choice regarding his wives: if he wished to observe rotation, he observed it, and if he wished to leave rotation, he left it. The Prophet (ﷺ) was singled out in that the matter was left to him, but he would observe rotation of his own accord without it being obligatory upon him, to console their hearts and to protect them from words of jealousy that lead to what is not fitting."

It was also said: rotation was obligatory upon the Prophet (ﷺ), then that obligation was abrogated (*nusikha*) for him by this verse. Abu Razin said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had resolved to divorce some of his wives, so they said to him: 'Observe rotation for us as you wish.' Among those he took in were ʿĀʾisha, Ḥafsa, Umm Salama and Zaynab, and their share from him, both of himself and of his property, was equal among them. Among those he postponed were Sawda, Juwayriya, Umm Ḥabība, Maymūna and Ṣafiyya, and he would observe rotation for them as he willed."

It was also said that the intended meaning is the women who gave themselves. Hisham ibn ʿUrwa related from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, regarding His saying ﴿You may postpone whom you will of them﴾, that she said: "This refers to those who gave themselves." Al-Shaʿbi said: "They are those who gave themselves; the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married some of them and left others." Al-Zuhri said: "We do not know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) postponed any of his wives; rather he took in all of them." Ibn ʿAbbas and others said: the meaning concerns divorcing whom he willed of those in his marriage and keeping whom he willed. It was also said other than this. On every interpretation, the verse means latitude and permission granted to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). What we have chosen is the most sound, and Allah knows best.

**Third:** Hibat Allah, in his work on naskh (abrogation, the verse that cancels an earlier ruling), held that His saying ﴿You may postpone whom you will﴾ abrogates His saying ﴿Women are not lawful for you after this﴾ [al-Ahzab: 52]. He said: "There is no abrogating verse in the Book of Allah that precedes what it abrogates other than this." His statement is weakened from several angles. In al-Baqara, the waiting period of a widow is four months and ten days, which abrogates the one-year period, and that abrogating verse came before it.[[See vol. 3, pp. 174 and 226.]]

**Fourth:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and whoever you desire of those you have set aside﴾. *Ibtaghayta* means you sought, and *ibtigha'* means seeking. *ʿAzalta* means you removed, and *al-ʿuzla* means removal; that is, if you wish to take to yourself a woman from those whom you have set aside from the rotation and join her to you, there is no blame upon you in that. The same ruling applies to postponement, so one of the two cases indicates the other.

**Fifth:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾, meaning there is no inclination (*junuh* from *janahat*), as one says *janahat al-safina*, meaning the ship leaned toward the ground. That is: there is no leaning of blame or reproach upon you.

**Sixth:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is more suitable that their eyes may be comforted﴾. Qatada and others said: that is, that choice which We gave you regarding their companionship is nearer to their contentment, since it came from Us. When they know that the matter is from Allah, their eyes are comforted and they are content, because when a person knows he has no right to something, he is content with what is given to him of it, however little. But if he knows he has a right, what is given to him does not satisfy him, his jealousy grows intense, and his greed becomes great in it. So what Allah did for His Messenger, by entrusting the matter to him regarding the circumstances of his wives, is closer to their contentment with him, and to the settling of their eyes with what he permits for them, without their hearts being attached to more than that.

It is recited *tuqarra aʿyunuhunna* with a *ḍamma* on the *tāʾ* and the *aʿyun* in the accusative, and *tuqarru aʿyunuhunna* with the passive form. Even with this, the Prophet (ﷺ), peace be upon him, would exert himself greatly in observing equality among them, to console their hearts, as we have already mentioned. He would say: "O Allah, this is my ability in what I control, so do not blame me in what You control and I do not." He meant his heart, because of his preference for ʿĀʾisha (may Allah be pleased with her), though he would not let that appear in any of his actions.

During his final illness he was carried around to the houses of his wives until he asked their permission to stay in the house of ʿĀʾisha. ʿĀʾisha said: "The first time the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell ill was in the house of Maymūna, so he asked his wives to be nursed in her house, meaning the house of ʿĀʾisha, and they permitted him..." The hadith, which the Sahih has recorded.

Also in the Sahih, from ʿĀʾisha (may Allah be pleased with her), she said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would examine his circumstances [[So in MSS Sh and K; in al-Bukhari it reads *layataʿadhdhar*. Al-Qastallani said: with the unpointed ʿayn and the dotted dhal, meaning he sought an excuse for what he was attempting regarding moving to the house of ʿĀʾisha. In al-Qabisi's copy it reads *yataqaddar*, with qaf and undotted dal, meaning he asked about the remaining measure until her day, so that some of what he experienced would be easier for him, since a sick person finds with some of his family what he does not find with others of comfort and tranquillity.]], saying: 'Where am I today? Where am I tomorrow?' seeking the day of ʿĀʾisha (may Allah be pleased with her). She said: 'When it was my day, Allah took him, between my chest and my throat' [[She means between my side and my chest. *Al-sahr* is the lung, and it was applied to the side by metonymy, naming the place after what is in it. *Al-nahr* is the chest.]], (ﷺ)."

**Seventh:** A man must treat his wives with equity, giving each one a day and a night. This is the view of the majority of scholars. Some held that equity is obligatory at night but not during the day. A wife's illness or menstruation does not cancel her right, and he must remain with her during her day and night. He must also treat them equally during his illness as he does in his health, except that if he is unable to move, he stays where the illness has overtaken him, and when he recovers he resumes the rotation. Slave women, free women, Christian women and Muslim women are equal in this. ʿAbd al-Malik said: "A free wife has two nights and a slave wife has one night." As for concubines (*sarari*), there is no rotation between them and free women, and they have no share in it.

**Eighth:** He should not bring them together in one dwelling except with their consent, and he should not enter the room of one of them on the day and night of another without need. There is disagreement about entering for a necessity or a pressing need. Most scholars, Malik and others, permit it. In the Kitab of Ibn Habib it is prohibited. Ibn Bukayr related from Malik, from Yahya ibn Saʿid, that Muʿadh ibn Jabal had two wives, and on the day of one of them he would not drink water from the house of the other. Ibn Bukayr said: "Malik related to us from Yahya ibn Saʿid that Muʿadh ibn Jabal had two wives who both died in the plague, so he drew lots between them as to which should be brought down first."

**Ninth:** Malik said: "He should treat them equally in maintenance and clothing if their circumstances are comparable. This is not required among those of differing status. Malik permitted him to favour one of them in clothing without it being a form of partiality. As for love and hatred, these lie outside what one earns, so equity in them is impossible, and this is what is meant by the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying regarding his division: 'O Allah, this is my action in what I control, so do not blame me in what You control and I do not.'" Al-Nasa'i and Abu Dawud recorded it from ʿĀʾisha (may Allah be pleased with her). In the Kitab of Abu Dawud it reads: "meaning the heart." To this points His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You will never be able to be equitable between wives, even if you should strive to do so﴾ [al-Nisa': 129], and His saying, exalted is He: "and Allah knows what is in your hearts." This is the reason for singling it out here, as a warning to us that He knows the inclination in our hearts toward some of the women we have over others. He is the All-Knowing of everything: ﴿nothing is hidden from Him on earth or in heaven﴾ [Al 'Imran: 5], ﴿He knows the secret and what is more hidden﴾ [Ta-Ha: 7]. But He is lenient in this, since a servant cannot turn his heart away from that inclination, and to this His saying returns: "And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."

It has been said regarding His saying: ﴿That is more suitable that their eyes may be comforted﴾, and this is the **tenth** point: that means it is nearer to their not grieving when he does not bring one of them together with the other and they do not witness favouritism and inclination. Abu Dawud related from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever has two wives and inclines to one of them will come on the Day of Resurrection with one side leaning."

(And they are all content with what you have given them) is an emphatic (*tawkid*) of the pronoun, meaning: and all of them are content. Abu Hatim and al-Zajjaj permitted "*wa yarḍayna bima ataytahunna kulluhunna*" as an emphasis of the pronoun hidden in *ātaytahunna*. Al-Farra' did not permit it, because the meaning does not support it: the meaning is "each one of them is content," not "with what you gave them all." Al-Nahhas said: "What he said is good."

**Eleventh:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah knows what is in your hearts﴾ is a general statement, and it refers to what is in the heart of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of love for one person over another. In the same way, the believers are also included in its meaning. In al-Bukhari, from ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs, the Prophet (ﷺ) sent him in command of the army of Dhat al-Salasil. He said: "I came to him and said: 'Who among the people is most beloved to you?' He said: 'ʿĀʾisha.' I said: 'From among the men?' He said: 'Her father.' I said: 'Then who?' He said: 'ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab...' and he named men." The discussion of the heart has already been given sufficiently at the beginning of al-Baqara,[[See vol. 1, p. 187.]] and at the beginning of this surah.[[P. 117 of this part.]]

It is related that Luqman the Wise was a slave carpenter, and his master said to him: "Slaughter a sheep and bring me its two best pieces." He brought him the tongue and the heart. Then he ordered him to slaughter another sheep and said: "Throw away its two most wicked pieces." He threw away the tongue and the heart. His master said: "I ordered you to bring me its two best pieces, and you brought me the tongue and the heart; and I ordered you to throw away its two most wicked pieces, and you threw away the tongue and the heart?" He said: "There is nothing better than these two when they are good, and nothing more wicked than them when they are corrupt."

**First issue:** There are seven issues concerning this verse. The scholars differed over the interpretation of His words, "It is not lawful for you to take women after this" (*Lā yaḥillu laka al-nisāʾu min baʿdu*), in seven opinions. The first: it was abrogated (*mansūkhah*, i.e., *naskh*, abrogation) by the Sunnah, and the abrogating text is the hadith of ʿĀʾishah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not die until women were made lawful for him." This has already been mentioned [[p. 207 of this part.]]. The second: it was abrogated by another verse. Al-Ṭaḥāwī narrated from Umm Salamah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not die until Allah made it lawful for him to marry whichever women he wished, except one who was within the prohibited degrees (*dhāt maḥram*), and that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: '*You may postpone whom you wish of them, and take to yourself whom you wish.*'" Al-Naḥḥās said: "This, and Allah knows best, is the most preferable of what has been said concerning the verse, and it agrees with the statement of ʿĀʾishah regarding abrogation. It is possible that ʿĀʾishah meant that this was made lawful for him by the Qur'an." It is also the view of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn and al-Ḍaḥḥāk. Some of the jurists of Kufa objected, saying: "It is impossible that this verse, meaning '*You may postpone whom you wish of them*,' abrogates '*It is not lawful for you to take women after this*,' when it comes before it in the Mushaf upon which the Muslims have agreed." He preferred the view of those who said it was abrogated by the Sunnah. Al-Naḥḥās said: "This objection is not binding, and its proponent is mistaken, because the Qur'an is in the position of a single sūrah, as is authentically reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: 'Allah sent down the Qur'an all at once to the lowest heaven in the month of Ramaḍān.' And what makes clear that the objection of this objector is not binding is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: '*Those of you who die and leave wives behind—a bequest for their wives: provision for a year without eviction*' [[see vol. 3, p. 226.]] [al-Baqarah: 240], which is abrogated, according to the people of interpretation (*ahl al-taʾwīl*)—we know of no disagreement among them—by the verse before it: '*Those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days*' [[see vol. 3, pp. 174, 226.]] [al-Baqarah: 234]." The third: it was forbidden to him (ﷺ) to marry over his wives, because they chose Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode. This is the view of al-Ḥasan, Ibn Sīrīn and Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām. Al-Naḥḥās said: "This view may be as it is, and then it was abrogated." The fourth: when it was forbidden for them to marry after him, it was forbidden for him to marry others than them. This was said by Abū Umāmah ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf. The fifth: "*It is not lawful for you to take women after this*" means after the categories that were named. This was said by Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, ʿIkrimah and Abū Razīn, and it is the choice of Muḥammad ibn Jarīr [al-Ṭabarī]. Whoever says that the permission was unrestricted for him says that "*It is not lawful for you to take women*" means: the Jewish women and the Christian women are not lawful for you. This is a far-fetched interpretation. It is also reported from Mujāhid, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and ʿIkrimah. This is the sixth view. Mujāhid said: "So that a disbeliever does not become a mother of the believers." This view is far-fetched, because it implies the supposition: "after the Muslim women," and no mention of Muslim women has preceded. Likewise, the supposition is made for "*nor to exchange them for other wives*," meaning: nor to divorce a Muslim woman in order to replace her with a People of the Book. The seventh: the Prophet (ﷺ) was permitted to marry whomever he wished, and then this was abrogated. He said: "And likewise were the prophets before him (ﷺ)." This was said by Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurẓī.

**The second issue:** His saying, "*nor to exchange them for other wives*." Ibn Zayd said: "This was a practice that the Arabs used to follow: one of them would say, 'Take my wife and give me your wife.'" Al-Dāraqutnī narrated from Abū Hurayrah, who said: "Exchange (*al-badal*) in the Jāhiliyyah was that a man would say to another man, 'Step down for me from your wife, and I will step down for you from my wife, and I will add to it for you.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: '*nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you*.'" He said: "Then ʿUyaynah ibn Ḥiṣn al-Fazārī entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while ʿĀʾishah was with him, and he entered without permission. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: '(O ʿUyaynah, where is the seeking of permission?)' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have not sought permission from a man of Muḍar since I came of age.' He said: 'Who is this Ḥumayrāʾ beside you?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: '(This is ʿĀʾishah, Mother of the Believers).' He said: 'Shall I not step down for you from the best of creation?' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: '(O ʿUyaynah, Allah has forbidden that).' He said: When he left, ʿĀʾishah said: 'O Messenger of Allah, who was this?' He said: '(A fool who is obeyed, and he, as you see, is indeed the chief of his people).'" Al-Ṭabarī, al-Naḥḥās and others denied what Ibn Zayd related from the Arabs, that they used to exchange their wives. Al-Ṭabarī said: "The Arabs never did this at all. As for what is narrated in the hadith of ʿUyaynah ibn Ḥiṣn, that he entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while ʿĀʾishah was with him… the hadith, it is not an exchange, nor did he intend that. He only belittled ʿĀʾishah because she was a young girl, so he said this statement." I say: What we have mentioned from the hadith of Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Abū Hurayrah, that exchange was in the Jāhiliyyah, indicates the opposite of what was denied concerning this, and Allah knows best. Al-Mubarrad said: "*Lā yaḥillu*" has also been read with the yāʾ and with the tāʾ. Whoever reads with the tāʾ does so according to the meaning of the group of women, and with the yāʾ from below according to the meaning of all women. Al-Farrāʾ claimed, saying: "The readers (*al-qurrāʾ*) have agreed that the recitation is with the yāʾ." This is an error. How can it be said that the readers agreed, when Abū ʿAmr recited with the tāʾ without any disagreement from him!

**The third issue:** His saying, "*even if their beauty pleases you*." Ibn ʿAbbās said: "This was revealed on account of Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays. When Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib died and left her, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was pleased by her beauty, so he wished to marry her, and the verse was revealed." This is a weak hadith, said Ibn al-ʿArabī.

**The fourth issue:** In this verse there is evidence for the permissibility of a man looking at the woman he intends to marry. The Prophet (ﷺ) told al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah, who wished to marry a woman: "(Look at her, for it is more likely to make the affection between you two last (*yaduma*)." [[That is: more fitting for the affection between you to endure. It is said: Allah made affection (*adama*) between them, meaning he joined them together and granted them success.]] And he (peace be upon him) said to another: "(Look at her, for there is something in the eyes of the Anṣār)." This is recorded in the Ṣaḥīḥ. Al-Ḥumaydī and Abū al-Faraj al-Jawzī said: "That is, [a defect like] yellowness or blueness." And it was said: "a discharge (*ramaṣāʾ*)." [[*al-ramaṣ* (with a vowel on the middle letter): a dirt that gathers in the corner of the eye; if it flows, it is *ghamaṣ*, and if it dries, it is *ramaṣ*.]]

**The fifth issue:** The command to look at the woman being proposed to is only by way of guidance towards what is beneficial, for when he looks at her, he may see in her what makes him desire to marry her. What shows that the command is by way of guidance is what Abū Dāwūd narrated from the hadith of Jābir, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "When one of you proposes to a woman, if he can look at her in a way that draws him to marry her, then let him do so." His saying, "*if he can, then let him do so*," is not said in the case of an obligation. This is the view of the majority of jurists: Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, the Kufans and others, and the people of the apparent meaning (*Ahl al-Ẓāhir*). Some people disliked this, but their opinion is not to be heeded, in view of the authentic hadiths and His saying, "*even if their beauty pleases you*." Sahl ibn Abī Ḥathmah said: "I saw Muḥammad ibn Maslamah chasing Thubayʾah bint al-Ḍaḥḥāk over a *ijjār* (roof) of the *ajājīr* of Madinah. I said to him: 'Do you do this?' He said: 'Yes!' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: '(When Allah places in the heart of one of you the proposal of a woman, there is no harm in his looking at her).'" *Al-ijjār*: the roof, in the dialect of the people of Syria and the Ḥijāz. Abū ʿUbayd said: The plural of *al-ijjār* is *ajājīr* and *ajājirah*.

**The sixth issue:** There has been disagreement over what is permissible to look at from her. Mālik said: He looks at her face and her palms, and he should not look except with her permission. Al-Shāfiʿī and Aḥmad said: with her permission and without her permission, if she is covered. Al-Awzāʿī said: He looks at her and makes an effort, and he looks at the places of flesh on her. Dāwūd said: He looks at her entire body, holding to the apparent wording. But the foundations of the Sharīʿah refute him regarding the prohibition of gazing at what is intimate (*al-ʿawrah*). And Allah knows best.

**The seventh issue:** His saying, "*except what your right hand possesses*" (*illā mā malakat yamīnuka*). The scholars differed concerning the lawfulness of a disbelieving slave-woman (*amah*) for the Prophet (ﷺ), in two opinions. The first: she is lawful, based on the generality of His saying, "*except what your right hand possesses*." This was said by Mujāhid, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ʿAṭāʾ and al-Ḥakam. They said: His saying, Mighty and Majestic, "*It is not lawful for you to take women after this*" means: women other than Muslim women are not lawful for you. As for Jewish women, Christian women and polytheist women, they are forbidden to you—i.e., it is not lawful for you to marry a disbeliever, lest she become a mother of the believers, even if her beauty pleases you, *except what your right hand possesses*, for it is permissible for him to take such a one as a concubine (*yatasarra*). The second view: she is not lawful, out of exalting his station above intimacy with a disbeliever. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said: '*And do not hold fast to the ties of disbelieving women*' [[see vol. 18, p. 65.]] [al-Mumtaḥanah: 10]. So how about him (ﷺ)?

As for "*mā*" in His saying, "*except what your right hand possesses*": it is in a nominative position as a substitute (*badal*) for "*al-nisāʾ*" (the women). It may also be in an accusative position as an exception, but this is weak. It may also be a verbal-noun particle (*maṣdariyyah*), and the supposition is: "except the possession of your right hand." And *malak* in the sense of *mamlūk* (possessed/owned), and it is in an accusative position because it is an exception from a different category than the first.

**Question 16 of this commentary: the Qur'anic verse 33:53, part 1 of 2**

**The first issue:** God's words, ﴿Do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are given permission﴾. The particle "an" (that) is in the accusative position, meaning: "except by being given permission to you." The exception is not part of the preceding clause.

﴿to a meal, without waiting for it to be ready﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: do not enter in this state. "Ghayra" (without) cannot be in the genitive as an attribute (na't) of "ṭa'ām" (meal), because if it were an attribute, the subject pronoun would have to be made explicit, and it would say: "ghayra nāẓirīna innāhu antum" (without you waiting for it to be ready). A parallel in grammar is: "This is a man with a man who is attached to him," and if you wish you can say: "This is a man with a man who is attached to him, he." This verse contains two matters: the first is the etiquette regarding food and sitting; the second is the command of the veil (ḥijāb). Ḥammād ibn Zayd said: this verse was revealed concerning those who linger heavily (thuqalā', i.e., overstaying guests).

As for the first matter, the majority of exegetes hold that its cause was that when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) married Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, the former wife of Zayd [[i.e., she had been Zayd's wife, then he divorced her and her waiting period (ʿidda) from him ended.]], he held a wedding feast (walīma) for her. He invited the people, and when they had eaten, groups of them sat talking in the house of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), while his wife turned her face to the wall. They were burdensome to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Anas said: "I do not know whether I or the Prophet (ﷺ) informed him that the people had left, or whether he informed me." He said: "So he went until he entered the house, and I went to enter with him, but he let the curtain fall between me and him, and the veil was revealed." He said: "The people were admonished with what they were admonished with, and God, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not enter the houses of the Prophet...﴾ up to His words: ﴿Indeed that was a grave matter in the sight of God﴾." This was narrated by the Ṣaḥīḥ (collection of al-Bukhārī).

Qatādah and Muqātil said, in the book of al-Thaʿlabī: this cause occurred in the house of Umm Salamah. But the first is the sound one, as narrated in the Ṣaḥīḥ.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: it was revealed concerning some of the believers who used to watch for the Prophet's (ﷺ) food, and they would enter before the food was ready, sit until it was ready, then eat and not leave. Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Ḥakīm said: this is a lesson (adab) which God taught to the burdensome guests.

Ibn Abī ʿĀʾisha said, in the book of al-Thaʿlabī: "It is enough of burdensome guests that the Sharia could not tolerate them."

As for the matter of the veil, Anas ibn Mālik and a group said: its cause was the command about sitting in Zaynab's house, the story mentioned just above. ʿĀʾisha (may God be pleased with her) and a group said: its cause was that ʿUmar said: "I said: O Messenger of God, your wives are entered upon by the righteous and the wicked, so if you ordered them to veil..." and then the verse was revealed.

The Ṣaḥīḥ narrated from Ibn ʿUmar that ʿUmar said: "I agreed with my Lord in three matters: concerning the station of Abraham, concerning the veil, and concerning the captives of Badr." This is the most authentic of what has been said regarding the matter of the veil. All other sayings and narrations besides these two are weak, none of them standing firm, and the weakest of them is what is narrated from Ibn Masʿūd: that ʿUmar ordered the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) to veil, and Zaynab bint Jaḥsh said: "O son of al-Khaṭṭāb, you are jealous of us, while revelation descends in our houses!" So God revealed: ﴿And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a curtain﴾. But this is false, because the veil was revealed on the day of Zaynab's consummation, as we have explained. It was narrated by al-Bukhārī, Muslim, al-Tirmidhī and others.

It was also said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was eating with some of his companions, and the hand of one of them touched the hand of ʿĀʾisha, and the Prophet (ﷺ) disliked this, so the verse of the veil was revealed.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: it was the custom of the people, when they had a wedding feast or the like, that whoever wished would come early to the invitation, waiting for the food to be cooked and ready. Likewise, when they finished, they would sit in the same way. So God forbade the believers from such things in the house of the Prophet (ﷺ), and the prohibition included all the believers. The people adhered to God's etiquette for them in this matter, so He forbade them from entering without permission at the time of eating, lest they be waiting for the food to be ready.

**The second issue:** God's words, ﴿houses of the Prophet﴾, are evidence that the house belongs to the man and is attributed to him as its owner, since God attributed it to him. If it is said: God has said: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the signs of God and wisdom; indeed God is Subtle and Aware﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 34] (see p. 182 of this part), we say: the attribution of the houses to the Prophet (ﷺ) is an attribution of ownership, while the attribution of the houses to the wives is an attribution of place (maḥall), as evidenced by His making permission in them for the Prophet (ﷺ), and permission only belongs to the owner.

**The third issue:** The scholars differed about the houses of the Prophet (ﷺ), since his wives lived in them after his death: were they their property or not? There are two opinions. One group said: they were their property, as evidenced by the fact that they lived in them after the Prophet's (ﷺ) death until their deaths, and that the Prophet (ﷺ) had given them these during his lifetime. The second: that this was a grant of residence, as a man lodges his wife, and it was not a gift, and their residence in them continued until death. This is the sound view, and it is what Abū ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr, Ibn al-ʿArabī and others approved, because this is from their maintenance (maʾūna), which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had excepted for them, just as he excepted their expenses when he said: "My heirs shall not divide a dinar or a dirham; what I leave after the expenses of my family and the maintenance of my worker is charity." Thus said the people of knowledge. They said: what indicates this is that their heirs did not inherit these dwellings from them. They said: had it been their property, their heirs would undoubtedly have inherited it from them. They said: the heirs' leaving it is evidence that it was not their property, but that it was only a dwelling for their lifetimes. When they died, it was added to the mosque, which benefits all Muslims, just as the expenses that were theirs from the estate of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) were added to the principal of the wealth when they passed on, and it was spent on the benefit of the Muslims in a way that benefits all of them. And God is the Granter of success.

**The fourth issue:** God's words, ﴿Without waiting for it to be ready﴾, i.e., not waiting for the time of its readiness. "Ināhu" is a short (maqṣūr) form, and it has dialects: "ināy" with a kasra on the hamza. Al-Shaybānī said:

*And Kisrā, when his sons divided him*
*With swords, as the meat is divided by the butcher,*
*Death twisted for him on a day that reached him [anā]*
*And for every pregnant woman there is completion.*

[[(anā) here is a past verb meaning reached and arrived, as in Lisān al-ʿArab and Sharḥ al-Qāmūs.]]

Ibn Abī ʿAblah read: "ghayri nāẓirīna ināhu," in the genitive as an attribute of "ṭaʿām." Al-Zamakhsharī said: this is not the correct reading, because it departs from what it belongs to; the pronoun referring to what it belongs to must be made explicit in the wording, so it would say: "ghayru nāẓirīna, ināhu antum," like your saying: "Hind, Zayd, her hitter is she."

"Anā" (with a fatḥa) and "anāʾ" (with a fatḥa on the hamza and an elongation) are also said. Al-Ḥuṭayʾa said:

*And I delayed the evening meal until Suhayl*
*Or al-Shiʿrā, and the waiting (anāʾ) lengthened for me.*

He means until the rising of Suhayl. "Ināhu" is the verbal noun of "anā al-shayʾu yaʾnī," when it finishes, comes due, and arrives.

**The fifth issue:** God's words, ﴿But when you are invited, enter; and when you have eaten, disperse﴾. He emphasized the prohibition and specified the time of entry as being upon permission, out of etiquette and to preserve the noble presence from unwanted familiarity. Ibn al-ʿArabī said: the sense of the sentence is: "But when you are invited and permission is given to you to enter, then enter; otherwise the invitation itself is not sufficient permission to enter." The "fa" (then) in the answer to "idhā" (when) is obligatory because of the conditional meaning it contains.

**The sixth issue:** God's words, ﴿and when you have eaten, disperse﴾. After eating, God commanded that all of them scatter and disperse. What is meant is obligating departure from the house when the purpose of eating is accomplished. The evidence for this is that entry is forbidden, and it was permitted only for the sake of eating; so when the eating ends, the permitting cause disappears and the prohibition returns to its original state.

**The seventh issue:** This verse is evidence that the guest eats on the property of the host, not on his own property, because He said: ﴿and when you have eaten, disperse﴾. He did not grant him more than eating, nor attributed anything else to him, and ownership remained in its original state.

**The eighth issue:** God's words, ﴿nor seeking familiar conversation﴾, are conjoined to His words: ﴿without waiting for it to be ready﴾, and "ghayr" is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause from the kāf and mīm in "lakum," i.e., not waiting and not seeking familiar conversation. The intended meaning: do not stay seeking familiar conversation, as the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) did at the wedding feast of Zaynab.

﴿Indeed that was hurtful to the Prophet, and he was shy of you, but God is not shy of the truth﴾. That is, He does not refrain from stating and manifesting it. Since that happens among humans out of the cause of shyness, God, exalted, is removed from the cause that necessitates that in humans. In the Ṣaḥīḥ, from Umm Salamah, she said: Umm Sulaym came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, God is not shy of the truth; is a woman obliged to perform a ritual bath if she has a wet dream?" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Yes, if she sees the water."

**The ninth issue:** God's words, ﴿And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a curtain﴾, the verse. Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī narrated from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: ʿUmar said: "I agreed with my Lord in four matters..." the hadith. In it: "I said: O Messenger of God, if only you would drape the veil over your wives, for the righteous and the wicked enter upon them." So God, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a curtain﴾.

Scholars differed about "matāʿ" (something). It was said: what is enjoyed of borrowed goods (al-ʿawārī), [[al-ʿawārī: plural of ʿāriyya, what they pass among themselves.]] and it was said: it is the pages of the Qur'an. The correct view is that it is general to everything that can be requested of utensils and all facilities for religion and worldly life.

**The tenth issue:** This verse is evidence that God permitted asking them from behind a curtain, in a need that arises or a question on which they are asked for a fatwa. This includes all women in meaning, and by what the foundations of the Sharia contain, that the woman is entirely an ʿawra (something to be covered): her body and her voice, as has preceded. So it is not permissible to uncover that except for a need, such as testifying against her, or an ailment in her body, or asking her about something that arises and is specific to her.

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Qur'an) on Surah 33, verse 53 (Part 2 of 2)**

The tenth issue: Some scholars cited the people taking (rulings) from the wives of the Prophet ﷺ from behind a screen (ḥijāb) as evidence for the admissibility of the testimony of a blind person (shahādat al-a'mā), and also that a blind man may have intercourse with his wife because he recognizes her by her voice. Most scholars permit his testimony, but Abu Hanifa, al-Shafi'i and others did not permit it. Abu Hanifa said: It is permitted in matters of lineage (al-ansāb). Al-Shafi'i said: It is not permitted except regarding what he saw before his sight was lost.

The eleventh issue: His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿That is purer for your hearts and their hearts﴾. He means (purer) from the passing thoughts that come to men regarding women and to women regarding men. That is, this is more effective in removing suspicion, further from accusation, and stronger in protection. This indicates that no one should trust himself when alone with someone who is not lawful for him, for avoiding that is better for his condition, more protective of himself, and more complete in his preservation (from sin).

The twelfth issue: His, the Exalted's, saying: "And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah" (up to the end of the verse). This is a repetition of the reason and an emphasis on its ruling, and the emphasis of reasons is stronger in rulings.

The thirteenth issue: His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Nor that you should marry his wives after him, ever﴾. Ismail ibn Ishaq narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn Ubayd told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, that a man said: "If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dies, I will marry Aisha." So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: "And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah" (up to the end of the verse). And (the verse) was revealed: "And his wives are their mothers" [al-Ahzab 6].

Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr Abd al-Rahman said: Ibn Abbas said: A man, one of the chiefs of Quraysh, from among the ten who were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on Hira, said within himself: "If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dies, I will marry Aisha, for she is my paternal cousin." Muqatil said: He was Talha ibn Ubayd Allah. Ibn Abbas said: That man regretted what he had said within himself, so he walked to Mecca on foot, gave ten mounts in the way of Allah, and freed slaves, and Allah forgave him for it.

Ibn Atiyya said: It is narrated that it was revealed because some of the Companions said: "If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dies, I will marry Aisha," and this reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was hurt by it. Thus Ibn Abbas referred to him only as "some of the Companions." Makki related from Ma'mar that he said: It was Talha ibn Ubayd Allah.

I say: Likewise al-Nahhas related from Ma'mar that it was Talha, but this is not authentic. Ibn Atiyya said: How excellent is the understanding of Ibn Abbas! In my view, this is not authentic regarding Talha ibn Ubayd Allah.

Our shaykh, the Imam Abu al-Abbas, said: This statement has been attributed to some of the distinguished Companions, but may they be far removed from the like of it! The falsehood lies in its transmission. Such a statement befits only the ignorant hypocrites. It is narrated that a man among the hypocrites said, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Umm Salama after Abu Salama, and Hafsa after Khunays ibn Hudhafa: "What is the matter with Muhammad, marrying our women! By Allah, if he dies, we will cast lots for his wives!" So the verse was revealed concerning this, and Allah forbade marrying his wives after him, and gave them the ruling of mothers. This is among his distinctive features, a distinction of his nobility and an indication of his rank ﷺ.

Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The wives of the Prophet ﷺ whom he left by death, it is not lawful for anyone to marry them, and whoever deems that lawful is a disbeliever, due to His, the Exalted's, saying: "And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah, nor that you should marry his wives after him, ever." It has also been said: He was prevented from marrying (after him) his wives because they are his wives in Paradise, and a woman in Paradise belongs to her last husband. Hudhayfa said to his wife: "If it pleases you to be my wife in Paradise, should Allah gather us there, then do not marry after me, for a woman belongs to her last husband." We have mentioned what the scholars say on this in (the book) al-Tadhkira, in the chapters on Paradise.

The fourteenth issue: The scholars differed regarding the wives of the Prophet ﷺ after his death: did they remain wives, or did the marriage end with death? And if the marriage ended with death, do they have an ʿidda (waiting period) or not? It was said: They have an ʿidda, because he died leaving them, and the ʿidda is an act of worship. It was also said: They have no ʿidda, because it is a period of waiting which is not awaited for permission (to remarry). This is the correct view, due to his, peace be upon him, saying: "I leave nothing after the maintenance of my dependents" (ʿiyāl). It is also narrated as "my family" (ahl), and this is a term specific to marital relationship. So maintenance and residence were preserved for them for the duration of their lives, because they are his women, and they are forbidden to others. This is the meaning of the continuation of the marriage. The death of the Prophet ﷺ was treated with respect to them as absence (al-mughayyab) is treated with respect to others, because they are definitely his wives in the Hereafter, unlike other people, for a man is not known to be with his family in one abode; perhaps one of them is in Paradise and the other in the Fire. Thus the cause (of the waiting period) ended with respect to creation, but remained with respect to the Prophet ﷺ. He, peace be upon him, also said: "My wives in this world are my wives in the Hereafter." And he, peace be upon him, said: "Every cause and lineage will be cut off except my cause and my lineage, for it remains until the Day of Resurrection."

Branch (farʿ): As for the wives whom he, peace be upon him, divorced during his lifetime, such as al-Kalbiyya and others, was it lawful for others to marry them? There is a difference of opinion. The correct view is that it is permissible, because it is narrated that al-Kalbiyya, whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divorced, was married by Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl, as previously mentioned. It has also been said that the one who married her was al-Ash'ath ibn Qays al-Kindi. Al-Qadi Abu al-Tayyib said: The one who married her was Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya, and no one denied that, which indicates that it is a consensus (ijmāʿ).

The fifteenth issue: His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Indeed, that is in the sight of Allah an enormity﴾. He means harming the Messenger of Allah ﷺ or marrying his wives. So that was counted among the major sins, and there is no sin greater than it.

The sixteenth issue: We have already explained the reason for the revelation of the veil (ḥijāb) from the hadith of Anas and the statement of Umar. Umar used to say to Sawda, when she went out, and she was a tall woman: "We have recognized you, O Sawda," out of eagerness that the veil be revealed, and so Allah revealed the verse of the veil. There is no improbability in the verse being revealed on account of all these causes, Allah knows best. However, when Zaynab bint Jahsh died, he (Umar) said: "None shall attend her funeral except a mahram (close relative) of hers," in observance of the veil that was revealed because of her. Then Asma bint Umays showed him the screen over her bier in the litter (qubba), and informed him that she had seen this in the land of Abyssinia, so Umar adopted it. It is also narrated that this was done at the funeral of Fatima, daughter of the Prophet ﷺ.

The Creator, glorified and exalted is He, knows what is manifest and what is hidden, what has been and what has not been. Nothing of the past that has passed away, nor of the future that is yet to come, is hidden from Him. This statement is in general terms, a praise of Him, and He is worthy of praise and commendation. Its intended meaning here, however, is rebuke and warning for those who were alluded to in the verse before it, by His words, "That is purer for your hearts and their hearts" [33:53], and for those who were alluded to in His words, "It is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah, nor to marry his wives after him, ever" [33:53]. So it was said to them in this verse: indeed Allah, exalted is He, knows what you conceal of these beliefs and disturbing thoughts, and He will recompense you for them. Thus this verse is linked to what precedes it and clarifies it. And Allah knows best.

There are three issues in this verse.

The first: when the verse of hijab was revealed, the fathers, the sons and the relatives said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "We too may speak to them from behind a screen?" So this verse was revealed.

The second: in this verse Allah the Exalted mentioned those to whom a woman may appear unveiled, and He did not mention the paternal uncle (ʿamm) and the maternal uncle (khāl), because they take the place of the parents. The paternal uncle may also be called a father, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿We shall worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael﴾ [al-Baqarah: 133], and Ishmael was the paternal uncle (of Yaʿqub). Al-Zajjaj said: The paternal uncle and the maternal uncle may describe a woman to their sons, for a woman is lawful to the son of her paternal uncle and the son of her maternal uncle, so seeing her was disliked for them. Al-Shaʿbi and ʿIkrimah disliked that a woman should take off her khimar (head covering) in the presence of her paternal uncle or her maternal uncle. Some of the mahram relatives are mentioned in this verse, and all of them are mentioned in Surat an-Nur, so this verse is part of that, and the discussion there has already been given in full (see vol. 12, p. 622), and praise be to Allah.

The third: the words of Allah the Exalted ﴿and fear Allah﴾. When Allah the Exalted mentioned the permission regarding these categories and the permissibility was made definite, He joined the command to them to be mindful of God (taqwa) by way of a separate sentence. This is in the utmost eloquence and conciseness, as if He said: Limit yourselves to this, and fear Allah regarding it, lest you go beyond it to something else. He singled out women for mention and specified them in this matter, because of the weakness of their self-restraint and the frequency of their laxity. And Allah knows best. Then the Exalted warned with His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of all things, Witness﴾.

This verse is one by which Allah honored His Messenger ﷺ in his life and in his death, and it mentions his high station with Him. By it Allah also cleared away the evil of those who harbored an evil thought about him, whether concerning his household or similar matters. Prayer (ṣalāh) from Allah means His mercy and His good pleasure, from the angels it means supplication and seeking forgiveness, and from the Muslim community it means supplication and magnifying his command.

**Issue:** The scholars differed about the pronoun in His words ﴿yuṣallūna﴾ ("they send blessings"). One group said the pronoun refers to Allah and the angels, and that this is a statement from Allah which honors His angels by joining them with Him. It is therefore not subject to the objection raised in the words of the speaker: "Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has been guided, and whoever disobeys them has gone astray." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Wretched orator are you! Say: 'And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger.'" This was recorded in the Ṣaḥīḥ. They said: it is not permitted for anyone to join the mention of Allah the Exalted with another in one pronoun, but Allah may do as He wills in that matter.

Another group said: there is an omission in the speech, its meaning being "Indeed Allah sends blessings, and His angels send blessings," and there is no joining in one pronoun in the verse, and that is permissible for people to do. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not say "Wretched orator are you" for this meaning. He said it because the speaker paused at "and whoever disobeys them" and made a pause.

They cited what Abu Dawud related from ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim, that a speaker gave a sermon in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, and whoever disobeys them." He said: "Stand up, or go away, wretched orator are you." However, it is possible that when he corrected him for his pause and said to him, "Wretched orator," he afterwards corrected the whole of his speech for him, saying: "Say: 'And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger,'" as in the Book of Muslim. This supports the first view, that he did not pause at "and whoever disobeys them."

Ibn ʿAbbās read ﴿wa-malāʾikatuh﴾ with a nominative ending, on the basis of the place of the name of Allah before ﴿inna﴾ entered. The majority read it in the accusative, coordinating it with what is written.

His words the Exalted: ﴿O you who believe, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace﴾. In this there are five issues.

**The first:** His words the Exalted: ﴿O you who believe, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace﴾. Allah the Exalted commanded His servants to send blessings upon His Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ, and not upon his fellow prophets, honoring him. There is no disagreement that sending blessings upon him is obligatory once in one's lifetime, and at every time it is obligatory like the emphasized sunnahs (sunan al-muʾakkadah, practices strongly recommended and not to be neglected), which one may not leave, and which no one neglects except one who has no good in him.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: If you ask, is sending blessings upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ obligatory or recommended? I say: Rather, it is obligatory. And they differed concerning the manner of its obligation. Among them are those who made it obligatory whenever he is mentioned. In a ḥadīth: "Whoever is mentioned in his presence and does not send blessings upon me, enters the Fire, and Allah has removed him far away." It was related that it was said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about the saying of Allah Mighty and Majestic: 'Indeed Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet'?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "This is from the hidden knowledge, and had you not asked me about it, I would not have told you about it. Indeed Allah the Exalted has appointed two angels for me. I am not mentioned in the presence of a Muslim and he sends blessings upon me except that those two angels say: 'May Allah forgive you,' and Allah the Exalted and His angels say in response to those two angels: 'Amen.' And I am not mentioned in the presence of a servant who is a Muslim, and he does not send blessings upon me, except that those two angels say: 'May Allah not forgive you,' and Allah the Exalted and His angels say to those two angels: 'Amen.'"

Among them are those who said: it is obligatory in every gathering once, even if his mention is repeated, as he said regarding the verse of prostration and the blessing upon one who sneezes. Likewise at the beginning and end of every supplication. Among them are those who made it obligatory once in one's lifetime. Likewise he said regarding the declaration of the two testimonies (shahādatayn).

What precaution (iḥtiyāṭ) requires is to send blessings at every mention of him, because of the reports that have come concerning that.

**The second:** The reports differed concerning the manner of sending blessings upon him ﷺ. Mālik related from Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us while we were in the gathering of Saʿd ibn ʿUbāda, and Bashīr ibn Saʿd said to him: "Allah has commanded us to send blessings upon you, O Messenger of Allah, so how should we send blessings upon you?" He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was silent until we wished that he had not been asked. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Say: O Allah, bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, as You blessed Ibrāhīm, and send blessings upon Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrāhīm and the family of Ibrāhīm, in the worlds; indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. And peace, as you already know."

Al-Nasāʾī related it from Ṭalḥa, the same, with the omission of his words "in the worlds" and his words "and peace, as you already know."

On this subject there are reports from Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra, Abū Ḥumayd al-Sāʿidī, Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Abū Hurayra, Burayda al-Khuzāʿī, and Zayd ibn Khārija, who is also called Ibn Ḥāritha. The imams of the people of ḥadīth recorded them in their books. Al-Tirmidhī graded the ḥadīth of Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra as ṣaḥīḥ. Muslim recorded it in his Ṣaḥīḥ together with the ḥadīth of Abū Ḥumayd al-Sāʿidī.

Abū ʿUmar said: Shuʿba and al-Thawrī related from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, the son of Ibn Abī Laylā, from Kaʿb ibn ʿUjra, who said: When the words of Allah the Exalted were revealed, "O you who believe, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace," a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, this greeting of peace upon you, we have known it, so what is the sending of blessings?" He said: "Say: O Allah, bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, as You blessed Ibrāhīm, and send blessings upon Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, as You blessed Ibrāhīm and the family of Ibrāhīm; indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious." This is the wording of the ḥadīth of al-Thawrī, not the ḥadīth of Shuʿba. It enters into the explanation traced back to the saying of Allah the Exalted: "Indeed Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who believe, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace." So He explained how to send blessings upon him, and taught them in the tashahhud how to greet him with peace, which is His saying: "Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings."

Al-Masʿūdī related from ʿAwn ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū Fākhita, from al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh (ibn Masʿūd), that he said: "When you send blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ, then do it well, for you do not know, perhaps that is presented to him." They said: "Then teach us." He said: "Say: O Allah, make Your blessings, Your mercy and Your blessings upon the master of the messengers, the leader of the God-fearing, the seal of the prophets, Muḥammad, Your servant, Your prophet and Your messenger, the leader of good, the guide of good, and the messenger of mercy. O Allah, raise him to a praiseworthy station which the first and the last will envy him for. O Allah, bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, as You blessed Ibrāhīm and the family of Ibrāhīm; indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah, bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, as You blessed Ibrāhīm and the family of Ibrāhīm; indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious."

We related with a connected chain in the book al-Shifāʾ of al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "[The Prophet] counted them on the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: 'Jibrīl counted them on my hand and said: Thus were they sent down from the Lord of Might: O Allah, bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, as You blessed Ibrāhīm and the family of Ibrāhīm; indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah, bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, as You blessed Ibrāhīm and the family of Ibrāhīm; indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah, have mercy upon Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, as You had mercy upon Ibrāhīm and the family of Ibrāhīm; indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah, show tenderness upon Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, as You showed tenderness to Ibrāhīm and the family of Ibrāhīm; indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.'"

Ibn al-ʿArabī said: Among these reports some are sound and some are weak, and the soundest of them is what Mālik related, so rely upon it. The report of other than Mālik, with the addition of mercy alongside the blessing and other things, is not strong. People should examine their religion as they examine their wealth. They do not accept a defective dinar in trade, but choose the sound and good one. Likewise, from the reports from the Prophet ﷺ, one should accept only what is established from the Prophet ﷺ in its chain, so that one does not enter into the realm of lying against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Thus, while he seeks the excess, he may fall into deficiency, and perhaps even into manifest loss.

**The third:** Concerning the virtue of sending blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ, it is established from him ﷺ that he said: "Whoever sends one blessing upon me, Allah sends ten blessings upon him for it." Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: Sending blessings upon Muḥammad ﷺ is the best of the acts of worship, because Allah the Exalted undertook it Himself with His angels, and then commanded the believers with it, whereas the rest of the acts of worship are not like that. Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī said: Whoever wishes to ask Allah for a need, let him begin with sending blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ, then ask Allah his need, then conclude with sending blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ, for Allah the Exalted accepts the two blessings, and He is too generous to reject what lies between them.

Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab related from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Supplication is veiled from the heaven until one sends blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ, and when the blessing upon the Prophet ﷺ comes, the supplication is raised." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever sends blessings upon me and greets me with peace in a writing, the angels will continue to send blessings upon him as long as my name is in that..."

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 56 (part 2 of 2):

...al-Kitab). The fourth issue: The scholars differed concerning sending blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ within the prayer (salah). The position held by the great majority and the vast bulk of scholars is that this is among the sunan (recommended practices) and mustahabbat (desirable acts) of the prayer. Ibn al-Mundhir said: It is recommended that no one perform a prayer without sending blessings upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ within it.
