If someone omits this, his prayer is valid according to the schools of Malik, the people of Madina, Sufyan al-Thawri, the people of Kufa among the proponents of ra'y (personal reasoning), and others. This is also the view of the majority of scholars. It is related from Malik and Sufyan that it is recommended in the final tashahhud, and that one who omits it in the tashahhud has done something blameworthy. Al-Shafi'i stood alone in obligating the repetition of the prayer upon one who omits it within the prayer. Ishaq obligated repetition only when it is omitted deliberately, not through forgetfulness. Abu 'Umar said: Al-Shafi'i said: If one does not send blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ in the final tashahhud, after the tashahhud and before the taslim, he must repeat the prayer. He said: If he sends blessings upon him before that, it does not suffice him. This is a view related from him by Harmala ibn Yahya, and it is hardly found in this form from al-Shafi'i except through the narration of Harmala from him. He was one of the senior companions who wrote down his books. The followers of al-Shafi'i have adopted this view, inclined towards it and debated on its basis, and for them it is the essence of his school. Al-Tahawi claimed that no one among the scholars held this view other than him. Al-Khattabi, who was himself one of the companions of al-Shafi'i, said: It is not obligatory in the prayer. This is the view of the group of jurists other than al-Shafi'i, and I know of no precedent for him in this matter. The evidence that it is not among the obligatory elements (furud) of the prayer is the practice of the righteous predecessors (al-salaf al-salih) before al-Shafi'i and their consensus upon it. He was severely criticized on this issue. This is the tashahhud of Ibn Mas'ud which al-Shafi'i preferred, and it is the one the Prophet ﷺ taught him; it contains no sending of blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ, and likewise every tashahhud narrated from him ﷺ. Ibn 'Umar said: Abu Bakr used to teach us the tashahhud from the pulpit just as you teach children in the kuttab. 'Umar also taught it from the pulpit, and there is no mention in it of sending blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ. I say: Muhammad ibn al-Mawwaz, one of our companions (Malikis), as mentioned by Ibn al-Qassar and Abd al-Wahhab, held that sending blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ in the prayer is obligatory, and Ibn al-'Arabi preferred this on the basis of the sound hadith: Indeed Allah has commanded us to send blessings upon you, so how should we send blessings upon you? So he taught the manner of the prayer and its time, and thus its manner and time became specified. Al-Daraqutni related from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn that he said: If I performed a prayer in which I did not send blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ or upon his family, I would consider that prayer incomplete. It is related with a marfu' chain from him, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet ﷺ. The correct view is that it is the statement of Abu Ja'far, as said by al-Daraqutni. The fifth issue: The words of Allah, the Exalted: (And greet him with a worthy greeting). Al-Qadi Abu Bakr ibn Bukayr said: This verse was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ, and Allah commanded his companions to greet him. Likewise, those after them were commanded to greet him when visiting his grave and when he is mentioned. Al-Nasa'i related from Abd Allah ibn Abi Talha, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came one day with cheerfulness visible on his face, and I said: Indeed we see the glad tidings on your face! He said: (The angel came to me and said: O Muhammad, your Lord says: Are you not pleased that no one sends blessings upon you except that I send blessings upon him ten times, and no one greets you except that I greet him ten times.) And from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (There is none among you who greets me when I die except that his greeting reaches me with Jibril, saying: O Muhammad, so-and-so son of so-and-so greets you, and I say: And upon him be peace, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.) Al-Nasa'i also related from Abd Allah who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Indeed Allah has angels wandering on the earth who convey to me the greetings of my ummah). Al-Qushayri said: The taslim is your saying: Peace be upon you.

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 57:**

In this verse there are five issues.

**The first issue:** The scholars differed over what harming Allah consists of. The majority of scholars said: its meaning is disbelief, attributing a consort, a child, or a partner to Him, and describing Him with what is not befitting to Him. Such is the saying of the Jews, may Allah curse them: "The Jews say, 'Allah's hand is shackled'" (5:64). And the Christians: "The Messiah is the son of Allah." And the polytheists: "The angels are the daughters of Allah," and "the idols are His partners."

In Sahih al-Bukhari, Allah the Exalted said: "The son of Adam denies Me, and it is not for him to do so; and he insults Me, and it is not for him to do so..." and the hadith continues. This has already been mentioned in the commentary on surah Maryam [see vol. 11, p. 159].

In Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Lord, blessed and exalted, said: "The son of Adam harms Me: he says, 'O misfortune of time!' So let none of you say, 'O misfortune of time!' For I am Time (al-dahr). I turn over its night and its day, and when I wish, I seize them both." This hadith has come down in this narration as a statement (mawquf) of Abu Hurayrah. But it has also come down as a marfu' report from him: "The son of Adam harms Me, he reviles Time, and I am Time; I turn over the night and the day." It was also related by Muslim.

Ikrimah said: its meaning is by making images and by encroaching upon an act that none does but Allah, such as carving images and the like. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah curses the image-makers." I say: This supports the view of Mujahid on the prohibition of depicting trees and other things, since all of that is a quality of originating creation and an imitation of the act of Allah, which He alone performs, glory be to Him, and exalted is He. This has already been mentioned in the commentary on surah al-Naml [see vol. 13, p. 221], and all praise is due to Allah.

Another group said: this is by way of omitting a noun, its implied sense being: "They harm the friends of Allah."

As for harming His Messenger (ﷺ), it is everything that hurts him, of words without any justification, and also of deeds. As for their words: "Sorcerer, poet, soothsayer, madman." As for their deeds: breaking his incisor and wounding his face on the day of Uhud, and in Makkah throwing the entrails of a slaughtered animal onto his back while he was prostrating. And so on.

Ibn Abbas said: it was revealed concerning those who slandered him when he married Safiyyah bint Huyayy.

The harm to Allah and His Messenger is stated without qualification, whereas the harm to the believing men and women is qualified, because harming Allah and His Messenger never occurs except without right, ever. As for harming the believing men and women, some of it is permissible and some of it is not.

**The second issue:** Our scholars said: Disparaging the appointment of Usamah ibn Zayd is a harm to him (peace be upon him). The Sahih narrates from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) dispatched a military expedition and appointed Usamah ibn Zayd over them. People criticised his command. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up and said: "If you criticise his command, you already used to criticise the command of his father before him. By Allah, he was indeed fit for command, and he was indeed among the dearest of people to me, and this one [Usamah] is indeed among the dearest of people to me after him."

This expedition, Allah knows best, is the one for which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) equipped Usamah, appointed him over them, and ordered him to raid Ubna, which is a village near Mu'tah, the place where his father Zayd was killed together with Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and Abdullah ibn Rawahah. So he was ordered to take vengeance for his father. Those in whose hearts there was doubt criticised his command, on the grounds that he was a freedman, and on the grounds that he was young, for he was then eighteen years old. The Prophet (ﷺ) died while this expedition had set out from Madinah but had not yet fully departed from it, so Abu Bakr carried it out after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) [may Allah bless him and grant him peace].

**The third issue:** In this hadith is the clearest proof of the permissibility of a freedman, or a less excellent person, leading others, in matters other than the supreme imamate. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) placed Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfah, in charge of the prayer at Quba. He would lead them, and among them were Abu Bakr, Umar, and other elders of Quraysh.

The Sahih narrates from Amir ibn Wathilah that Nafi' ibn Abd al-Harith met Umar at Usfan, and Umar used to appoint him over Makkah. Umar said: "Whom have you appointed over this valley?" He said: "Ibn Abza." He said: "And who is Ibn Abza?" He said: "A freedman from among our freedmen." He said: "You have appointed a freedman over them!" He said: "Indeed he is a reciter of the Book of Allah, and he is knowledgeable in the laws of inheritance (al-fara'id)." Umar said: "Indeed your Prophet has said: 'Allah raises up peoples by this Book and lowers others by it.'"

**The fourth issue:** Usamah, may Allah be pleased with him, was the beloved son of the beloved, and by this he was called. He was extremely black in complexion, whereas his father Zayd was white like cotton. This is how Abu Dawud related it from Ahmad ibn Salih. Others besides Ahmad said: Zayd was bright-complexioned, and Usamah had very dark skin.

It is reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to make Usamah handsome when he was young, wiping his nose and cleaning his nostrils, and saying: "If Usamah were a girl, we would have adorned him, prepared him, and made him beloved to husbands."

It has been mentioned that the cause of the apostasy of the Arabs after the Prophet (ﷺ) was this: when he (peace be upon him) was in the Farewell Pilgrimage at the Mount of Arafat on the evening of Arafah, at the time of departure, the Prophet (ﷺ) delayed briefly because of Usamah, until he came to him. They said: "He only delayed for the sake of this one!" belittling him. And this saying of theirs was the cause of their apostasy. Al-Bukhari mentioned it in his History, with this meaning. And Allah knows best.

**The fifth issue:** Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to assign to Usamah in the stipend five thousand, and to his son Abdullah two thousand. Abdullah said to him: "You have preferred Usamah over me, though I witnessed what he did not witness!" He said: "Indeed Usamah was more beloved to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) than you were, and his father was more beloved to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) than your father was." So may Allah be pleased with him, he preferred the beloved of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) over his own beloved. And thus it is obligatory to love what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) loved and to hate whom he hated.

Marwan countered this love with its opposite. He passed by Usamah ibn Zayd while he was praying at the door of the Prophet's (ﷺ) house, and Marwan said to him: "I only wanted us to see your place, and we have seen your place. May Allah do such and such to you!" And he said an ugly thing. Usamah said to him: "You have harmed me, and you are vile and foul-mouthed. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Indeed Allah, the Exalted, hates the vile and foul-mouthed.'" So look at the difference between the two deeds, and measure the difference between the two men. The Banu Umayyah harmed the Prophet (ﷺ) through his beloved ones, and opposed him regarding what he loved.

**His saying, the Exalted:** ﴿Allah has cursed them﴾ means: they were banished from every good. Cursing (al-la'n) in the language means banishment, and from it comes li'an (mutual cursing). "And He has prepared for them a humiliating punishment" (33:57), whose meaning has already been explained in more than one place. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

Harm to the believing men and women is also through deeds and wicked words, such as slander and vile, fabricated accusation. This verse is similar to the verse in al-Nisa': ﴿And whoever earns a sin or a transgression and then throws it onto an innocent person has certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin﴾ [An-Nisa: 112], just as it says here. It has been said that among harm is insulting him with a blameworthy lineage, or a blameworthy profession, or anything that weighs heavily on him when he hears it, because harming him is in general unlawful. Allah, exalted is He, distinguished between harming him, harming the Messenger, and harming the believers: He made the first kufr, and the second a major sin. He said concerning harming the believers: "they have borne slander and a manifest sin," and we have explained it. It is narrated that Umar ibn al-Khattab said to Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "Last night I recited this verse and it frightened me: ﴿And those who harm believing men and believing women without their having earned it﴾ [al-Ahzab: 58], by Allah, I indeed strike them and rebuke them." Ubayy said to him: "O Commander of the Believers, you are not among them; you are only a teacher and corrector." It has also been said that the occasion of revelation of this verse was that Umar saw a young woman of the Ansar and struck her, disliking what he saw of her adornment; her family came out and harmed Umar with their tongues, so Allah revealed this verse. It has been said: it was revealed concerning Ali, for the hypocrites used to harm him and lie against him. May Allah be pleased with him.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 59:

There are six issues in it.

**The first issue:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say to your wives and your daughters﴾. The discussion of the preference of his wives, one by one, has already passed [[See p. 162 onward in this part.]]. Qatadah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died leaving nine wives. Five were from Quraysh: 'A'ishah, Hafsah, Umm Habibah, Sawdah, and Umm Salamah. Three were from the rest of the Arabs: Maymunah, Zaynab bint Jahsh, and Juwayriyah. One was from the Banu Harun: Safiyyah.

As for his children, the Prophet (ﷺ) had sons and daughters. Of the sons: al-Qasim, whose mother was Khadijah, and by whom he was given his kunyah (teknonym). He was the first of his sons to die, and he lived two years. 'Urwah said: Khadijah bore the Prophet (ﷺ) al-Qasim, al-Tahir, 'Abd Allah, and al-Tayyib. Abu Bakr al-Barqi said: It is said that al-Tahir is al-Tayyib, and he is 'Abd Allah. Ibrahim, whose mother was Mariyah the Copt, was born in Dhu al-Hijjah in the eighth year of the Hijrah (migration). He died at the age of sixteen months, and it is said eighteen. al-Daraqutni mentioned this. He was buried in al-Baqi'. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed he has a place where he will complete his nursing in Paradise." All the children of the Prophet (ﷺ) were from Khadijah except Ibrahim. All his sons died during his lifetime, except that none survived him.

As for the daughters of the Prophet (ﷺ), among them: Fatimah al-Zahra', daughter of Khadijah. Her mother bore her while Quraysh were rebuilding the Ka'bah, five years before the prophethood. She was the youngest of his daughters. 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with both of them) married her in the second year of the Hijrah, in Ramadan, and he consummated the marriage with her in Dhu al-Hijjah. It is said that he married her in Rajab. She died shortly after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and she was the first of his household to join him. May Allah be pleased with her.

Among them: Zaynab, whose mother was Khadijah. Her cousin on her mother's side, Abu al-'As ibn al-Rabi', married her. Abu al-'As's mother was Halah bint Khuwaylid, the sister of Khadijah. The name of Abu al-'As was Laqit. It is said Hashim. It is said Hushaym. It is said Miqsam. She was the eldest of the daughters of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and she died in the eighth year of the Hijrah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) got down into her grave.

Among them: Ruqayyah, whose mother was Khadijah. 'Utbah ibn Abi Lahab married her before the prophethood. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent and the revelation came to him: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾ [[See vol. 20, p. 234.]] [al-Masad: 1], Abu Lahab said to his son: "My head is forbidden to your head unless you divorce his daughter." So he separated from her, and he had not consummated the marriage with her. She became Muslim when her mother Khadijah became Muslim, and she and her sisters pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when the women pledged allegiance. 'Uthman ibn 'Affan married her, and the women of Quraysh used to say when 'Uthman married her:

"The finest of two persons a man has seen: Ruqayyah and her husband 'Uthman."

She made the two migrations with him to the land of Abyssinia. She had miscarried a child by 'Uthman, and afterward she bore 'Abd Allah. 'Uthman was given the kunyah by him in Islam. He reached six years of age, and a rooster pecked him in the face, and he died. She bore him nothing after that. She migrated to Medina and fell ill while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was preparing for Badr, so he left 'Uthman in charge of her. She died while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was at Badr, at the start of the seventeenth month after the Hijrah. Zayd ibn Harithah came as a bearer of good news from Badr, and he entered Medina just as the dust was being smoothed over Ruqayyah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not attend her burial.

Among them: Umm Kulthum, whose mother was Khadijah. 'Utaybah ibn Abi Lahab, the brother of 'Utbah, married her before the prophethood. His father ordered him to divorce her for the reason mentioned in the matter of Ruqayyah. He had not consummated the marriage with her, so she stayed in Mecca with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). She became Muslim when her mother became Muslim, and she pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with her sisters when the women pledged allegiance. She migrated to Medina when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) migrated. When Ruqayyah died, 'Uthman married her, and for this reason he was called Dhu al-Nurayn (the possessor of two lights). She died during the lifetime of the Prophet (ﷺ), in Sha'ban of the ninth year of the Hijrah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat by her grave, and 'Ali, al-Fadl, and Usamah got down into her grave.

Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar mentioned that the eldest child of the Prophet (ﷺ) was al-Qasim, then Zaynab, then 'Abd Allah, who was called al-Tayyib and al-Tahir, and he was born after the prophethood and died young. Then Umm Kulthum, then Fatimah, then Ruqayyah. Al-Qasim died in Mecca, then 'Abd Allah died.

**The second issue:** Since it was the custom of Arab women to go about without concern for covering themselves, and they would uncover their faces as slave women do, and this was an occasion for men to look at them and for thoughts to wander about them, Allah commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to tell them to let down their outer garments (jalabib) over themselves when they wished to go out to their needs. They used to relieve themselves in the open desert before latrines were made. So a distinction would arise between them and slave women, and free women would be recognized by their covering, and whoever was an oppressor or a youth would refrain from harassing them. Before the revelation of this verse, a woman among the believing women would go out to relieve herself, and some of the wicked would approach her, thinking she was a slave woman. She would shout at him, and he would leave. They complained of that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and the verse was revealed because of that. This was the explanation of al-Hasan and others.

**The third issue:** His saying, exalted is He: (from their jalabib). The jalabib are the plural of jilbab, which is a garment larger than the khimar (head covering). It was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud that it is the rida' (wrap). It has been said that it is the qina' (veil). The correct view is that it is the garment that covers the whole body.

In Sahih Muslim, from Umm 'Atiyyah: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, what if one of us has no jilbab?" He said: "Let her sister clothe her with one of her jilbabs."

**The fourth issue:** People differed about the form of letting it down. Ibn 'Abbas and 'Abidah al-Salmani said: It is that the woman wraps it so that nothing of her shows except one eye with which she sees. Ibn 'Abbas also said, and Qatadah: It is that she wraps it over the forehead and fastens it, then brings it down over the nose, and even if her eyes show, it covers the chest and most of the face. al-Hasan said: She covers half her face.

**The fifth issue:** Allah, glorified is He, commanded all women to cover themselves, and that can only be done with what does not describe the shape of the skin. But when she is with her husband, she may wear whatever she wishes, because he may enjoy her however he wishes.

It is established that the Prophet (ﷺ) awoke one night and said: "Glory be to Allah! What trials have been sent down tonight, and what treasures have been opened! Who will awaken the companions of the chambers? How many a clothed one in this world will be naked in the Hereafter!"

It was also narrated that Dihyah al-Kalbi, when he returned from Heraclius, was given a Coptic garment by the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Make one half a shirt for yourself and give your companion the other half to cover her head with." The half (sadi') means the half. Then he said to him: "Tell her to put something underneath it so that it does not show the shape."

Abu Hurayrah mentioned the thinness of women's clothing and said: "The clothed-yet-naked, the pampered ones (al-mutan'immat in one manuscript), the wretched ones."

Some women of the Banu Tamim entered upon 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) wearing thin garments. 'A'ishah said: "If you are believers, this is not the clothing of believing women, and if you are not believers, then enjoy it [[This word appears garbled in the manuscripts of the original, and it is perhaps (fa-tamatta'na bihi).]]."

A bride was brought in to 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) wearing a Coptic khimar dyed with safflower. When she saw her, she said: "A woman who wears this has not believed in Surat al-Nur."

It is firmly established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Women who are clothed yet naked, who lead astray and are led astray, whose heads are like the humps of the Bukht camels; they will not enter Paradise nor smell its fragrance."

'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "What prevents the Muslim woman, if she has a need, from going out in her worn-out clothes, or the worn-out clothes of her neighbour, discreetly, so that no one knows about her until she returns to her house?"

**The sixth issue:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is more suitable that they be recognized﴾, meaning the free women, so that they are not mixed up with slave women. When they are recognized, they will not be approached with any harassment, out of respect for the rank of freedom, and desires for them will be cut off. The meaning is not that the woman should be recognized so that it is known who she is. 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), when he saw a slave woman who had veiled herself, would strike her with a whip, to preserve the dress of free women.

It has been said that covering and veiling is now obligatory for all, free women and slave women alike. This is like the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prohibiting women from the mosques after the death of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), despite his saying: "Do not prevent the female servants of Allah from the mosques of Allah." Until 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "If the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had lived until our time, he would have prevented them from going out to the mosques, just as the women of the Children of Israel were prevented."

﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾: a reassurance to women regarding leaving off the jalabib before this command was legislated.

There are five issues in it.

The first concerns His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿If the hypocrites do not desist﴾, to the end of the verse. The people of tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis) hold that the three descriptions refer to one group. This is as Sufyan ibn Sa'id related from Mansur, from Abu Razin, who said: "The hypocrites, those in whose hearts is a disease, and the agitators in Medina," and he said: "They are one thing," meaning that they had combined these qualities. The conjunction *wa* ("and") is *muqhama* (superfluous, inserted), as the poet said:

*ilā al-malik al-qarm wa-bni al-humām ... wa-laythi al-katība fī al-muzdaḥam*

("To the noble king and the son of the brave warrior ... and the lion of the battalion in the throng.")

He meant: "To the noble king, the son of the brave warrior, the lion of the battalion." This has already been discussed in *al-Baqara* [[See vol. 1, p. 385.]].

It has also been said that some of them were agitators, some pursued women for illicit purposes, and some cast doubt upon the Muslims. Ikrima and Shahr ibn Hawshab said: "Those in whose hearts is a disease" means those in whose hearts is fornication (*al-zina*). Tawus said: this verse was revealed concerning the matter of women. Salama ibn Kuhayl said: it was revealed concerning the people of immoral acts, and the meanings are close to one another.

It has also been said: "The hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease" are one group, referred to with two expressions; the proof is the verse on the hypocrites at the beginning of *al-Baqara* [[See vol. 1, p. 192.]].

"The agitators in Medina" were people who informed the believers of things that would grieve them concerning their enemy. When the expeditions (*sara*ya) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out, they would say: "They have been killed or defeated," and "the enemy has come upon you." Qatada and others said this.

It was also said that they would say: "The People of the Bench (*ahl al-Suffa*) are unmarried men," and so they would approach women. It was said: they are Muslims who spread false reports out of love for strife. Among the people of the slander (*ahl al-ifk*) there were Muslims who nevertheless engaged in it out of love for strife.

Ibn 'Abbas said: *al-irjaf* is seeking strife. *Al-irjaf* is spreading falsehood and untruth in order to cause distress (*al-ightimam*) by it. [[In MS. Z: "al-ihtimam" (concern); in MS. Sh: "al-ighmam" (distress).]]

It has also been said: *irjaf* is the stirring of hearts. It is said: "the earth quaked" (*rajafat al-ard*), meaning it shook and was convulsed, and it quakes with a quaking (*rajfan*). *Al-rajafan* is violent agitation, and *al-rajjaf* is the sea, named so for its turbulence. The poet said:

*al-muṭ'imūna al-laḥma kulla ʿashiyyatin ... ḥattā tughība al-shamsu fī al-rajjāf*

("They who feed meat every evening, until the sun sets in the *rajjaf*.") [[Ibn Barri said: the verse is by Matrud ibn Ka'b al-Khuza'i, lamenting 'Abd al-Muttalib, grandfather of our Master, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Before it is:

*yā ayyuhā al-rajulu al-muḥawwal raḥluhu ... hallā nazalta bi-āli ʿAbdi Manāf*

("O man who loads his saddle, why did you not alight among the family of 'Abd Manaf?")]]

*Al-irjaf* is the singular of *arajif al-akhbar* (rumours). They have *arjafū fī al-shay'*, meaning they engaged in it. The poet said:

*fa-innā wa-in ʿayyartumūnā bi-qatlihi ... wa-arjafa bi-al-islāmi bāghin wa-ḥāsidu*

("Though you reproach us for his killing ... and an aggressor and an envious one spread falsehood against Islam.")

Another said:

*abi-al-arājīfi yā ibna al-lu'mi tuʿaddinī ... wa-fī al-arājīfi khiltu al-lu'ma wa-al-khawara*

("Do you threaten me with rumours, O son of baseness? In rumours I see baseness and weakness.") [[The verse is by al-'Ayn al-Minqari, satirising al-'Ajjaj or Ru'ba. The well-known version is:

*abi-al-arājīzi yā ibna al-lu'mi tuʿaddinī ... wa-fī al-arājīzi khiltu al-lu'ma wa-al-khawara*

*Al-arajiz* is the plural of *urjuza*, meaning *rajaz*, a metre of poetry. Grammarians cited it as evidence that *khilta* ("I thought") is among the verbs whose operation is nullified when placed between its two objects. Had one put *al-lu'ma wa-al-khawara* in the accusative as objects, it would have been permissible.

(See Sibawayh's *Kitab*, vol. 1, p. 61, and the chapter on *zanna* and its sisters in the grammar books.)]]

Therefore *al-irjaf* is forbidden, because it causes harm. The verse thus indicates the prohibition of harming others through *irjaf*.

The second issue concerns His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then We shall surely incite you against them﴾. That is, We shall empower you over them, so that you uproot them by killing. Ibn 'Abbas said: they did not desist from harming women, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, incited him against them. Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And do not pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave﴾ [at-Tawba: 84], and He commanded him to curse them, and this is the *ighra'*. Muhammad ibn Yazid said: He incited him against them in the verse that follows this one, with the continuity of the discourse, which is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Wherever they are found, they will be seized and killed, killed thoroughly.﴾ This contains the meaning of a command to kill them and seize them; that is, this is their ruling when they persist in hypocrisy and agitation. There is a hadith from the Prophet ﷺ: "Five [kinds of animals] are to be killed in the sacred and non-sacred areas." This contains the meaning of a command, like the verse, exactly.

Al-Nahhas said: this is among the best of what has been said concerning the verse. It has also been said: they had desisted from agitation, so they were not incited against.

The *lam* in *la-nughriyannaka* is the *lam* of oath, the oath falls upon it, and the *lam* was introduced into *in* (in the protasis) as a preparation for it.

The third issue concerns His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then they will not be your neighbours in it﴾, that is, in Medina. ﴿Except briefly﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (*hal*) of the pronoun in *yujawiruna*. So the matter was as He, Blessed and Exalted, said, because they were only few. This is one of al-Farra's two answers, and it is the preferable one in his view: that is, they will not be your neighbours except in a state of their paucity. The other answer is that the meaning is "except for a brief time," that is, they will not remain with you except for a short period, meaning they will not be your neighbours in it except for a brief neighbourhood until they perish. It is then an adjective of a verbal noun or of an omitted adverb of time. It also indicates that whoever lives with you in Medina is a neighbour. This has already been discussed in *al-Nisa'* [[See vol. 5, p. 183 onwards.]].

The fourth issue concerns His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Cursed﴾. This is the complete sentence according to Muhammad ibn Yazid, and it is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier. Ibn al-Anbari said: "Briefly, cursed" is a good pause. Al-Nahhas said: it is also permissible for the complete sentence to be "except briefly," and "cursed" to be in the accusative as a term of abuse, as 'Isa ibn 'Umar read: *wa-imra'atuhu hammalata al-hatab* ("and his wife, the carrier of firewood"). It is related from some grammarians that he said the meaning is: "Wherever they are found, they will be seized as cursed." This is an error, since the conditional particle does not govern what precedes it (in the sense that the conditional clause cannot be governed by what comes before it). It has also been said that the meaning of the verse is: if they persist in hypocrisy, they will have no place in Medina except as those who are expelled and cursed. This was indeed done to them: when the chapter of *Bara'a* was revealed, they were gathered, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "O so-and-so, stand up and go out, for you are a hypocrite; and O so-and-so, stand up." Then their brothers among the Muslims stood up and undertook to expel them from the mosque.

The fifth issue concerns His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿The way of Allah﴾. It is in the accusative as an absolute object (*masdar*), meaning: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, established the ruling concerning those who spread rumours against the prophets and openly displayed their hypocrisy, that they should be seized and killed.

﴿And you will not find any change in the way of Allah﴾, that is, any alteration or modification. This was related by al-Naqqash. Al-Suddi said: it means that whoever is killed rightfully, there is no blood-money (*diya*) upon his killer.

Al-Mahdawi said: the verse contains evidence for the permissibility of not carrying out a threat, and the evidence for this is that the hypocrites remained with him until he died. What is known of people of virtue is to fulfil their promises of good and to delay their threats, and this has already passed in *Al 'Imran* [[See vol. 4, p. 303.]] and elsewhere.

There are five issues in it.

The first concerns His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿If the hypocrites do not desist﴾, to the end of the verse. The people of tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis) hold that the three descriptions refer to one group. This is as Sufyan ibn Sa'id related from Mansur, from Abu Razin, who said: "The hypocrites, those in whose hearts is a disease, and the agitators in Medina," and he said: "They are one thing," meaning that they had combined these qualities. The conjunction *wa* ("and") is *muqhama* (superfluous, inserted), as the poet said:

*ilā al-malik al-qarm wa-bni al-humām ... wa-laythi al-katība fī al-muzdaḥam*

("To the noble king and the son of the brave warrior ... and the lion of the battalion in the throng.")

He meant: "To the noble king, the son of the brave warrior, the lion of the battalion." This has already been discussed in *al-Baqara* [[See vol. 1, p. 385.]].

It has also been said that some of them were agitators, some pursued women for illicit purposes, and some cast doubt upon the Muslims. Ikrima and Shahr ibn Hawshab said: "Those in whose hearts is a disease" means those in whose hearts is fornication (*al-zina*). Tawus said: this verse was revealed concerning the matter of women. Salama ibn Kuhayl said: it was revealed concerning the people of immoral acts, and the meanings are close to one another.

It has also been said: "The hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease" are one group, referred to with two expressions; the proof is the verse on the hypocrites at the beginning of *al-Baqara* [[See vol. 1, p. 192.]].

"The agitators in Medina" were people who informed the believers of things that would grieve them concerning their enemy. When the expeditions (*sara*ya) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out, they would say: "They have been killed or defeated," and "the enemy has come upon you." Qatada and others said this.

It was also said that they would say: "The People of the Bench (*ahl al-Suffa*) are unmarried men," and so they would approach women. It was said: they are Muslims who spread false reports out of love for strife. Among the people of the slander (*ahl al-ifk*) there were Muslims who nevertheless engaged in it out of love for strife.

Ibn 'Abbas said: *al-irjaf* is seeking strife. *Al-irjaf* is spreading falsehood and untruth in order to cause distress (*al-ightimam*) by it. [[In MS. Z: "al-ihtimam" (concern); in MS. Sh: "al-ighmam" (distress).]]

It has also been said: *irjaf* is the stirring of hearts. It is said: "the earth quaked" (*rajafat al-ard*), meaning it shook and was convulsed, and it quakes with a quaking (*rajfan*). *Al-rajafan* is violent agitation, and *al-rajjaf* is the sea, named so for its turbulence. The poet said:

*al-muṭ'imūna al-laḥma kulla ʿashiyyatin ... ḥattā tughība al-shamsu fī al-rajjāf*

("They who feed meat every evening, until the sun sets in the *rajjaf*.") [[Ibn Barri said: the verse is by Matrud ibn Ka'b al-Khuza'i, lamenting 'Abd al-Muttalib, grandfather of our Master, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Before it is:

*yā ayyuhā al-rajulu al-muḥawwal raḥluhu ... hallā nazalta bi-āli ʿAbdi Manāf*

("O man who loads his saddle, why did you not alight among the family of 'Abd Manaf?")]]

*Al-irjaf* is the singular of *arajif al-akhbar* (rumours). They have *arjafū fī al-shay'*, meaning they engaged in it. The poet said:

*fa-innā wa-in ʿayyartumūnā bi-qatlihi ... wa-arjafa bi-al-islāmi bāghin wa-ḥāsidu*

("Though you reproach us for his killing ... and an aggressor and an envious one spread falsehood against Islam.")

Another said:

*abi-al-arājīfi yā ibna al-lu'mi tuʿaddinī ... wa-fī al-arājīfi khiltu al-lu'ma wa-al-khawara*

("Do you threaten me with rumours, O son of baseness? In rumours I see baseness and weakness.") [[The verse is by al-'Ayn al-Minqari, satirising al-'Ajjaj or Ru'ba. The well-known version is:

*abi-al-arājīzi yā ibna al-lu'mi tuʿaddinī ... wa-fī al-arājīzi khiltu al-lu'ma wa-al-khawara*

*Al-arajiz* is the plural of *urjuza*, meaning *rajaz*, a metre of poetry. Grammarians cited it as evidence that *khilta* ("I thought") is among the verbs whose operation is nullified when placed between its two objects. Had one put *al-lu'ma wa-al-khawara* in the accusative as objects, it would have been permissible.

(See Sibawayh's *Kitab*, vol. 1, p. 61, and the chapter on *zanna* and its sisters in the grammar books.)]]

Therefore *al-irjaf* is forbidden, because it causes harm. The verse thus indicates the prohibition of harming others through *irjaf*.

The second issue concerns His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then We shall surely incite you against them﴾. That is, We shall empower you over them, so that you uproot them by killing. Ibn 'Abbas said: they did not desist from harming women, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, incited him against them. Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And do not pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave﴾ [at-Tawba: 84], and He commanded him to curse them, and this is the *ighra'*. Muhammad ibn Yazid said: He incited him against them in the verse that follows this one, with the continuity of the discourse, which is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Wherever they are found, they will be seized and killed, killed thoroughly.﴾ This contains the meaning of a command to kill them and seize them; that is, this is their ruling when they persist in hypocrisy and agitation. There is a hadith from the Prophet ﷺ: "Five [kinds of animals] are to be killed in the sacred and non-sacred areas." This contains the meaning of a command, like the verse, exactly.

Al-Nahhas said: this is among the best of what has been said concerning the verse. It has also been said: they had desisted from agitation, so they were not incited against.

The *lam* in *la-nughriyannaka* is the *lam* of oath, the oath falls upon it, and the *lam* was introduced into *in* (in the protasis) as a preparation for it.

The third issue concerns His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then they will not be your neighbours in it﴾, that is, in Medina. ﴿Except briefly﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (*hal*) of the pronoun in *yujawiruna*. So the matter was as He, Blessed and Exalted, said, because they were only few. This is one of al-Farra's two answers, and it is the preferable one in his view: that is, they will not be your neighbours except in a state of their paucity. The other answer is that the meaning is "except for a brief time," that is, they will not remain with you except for a short period, meaning they will not be your neighbours in it except for a brief neighbourhood until they perish. It is then an adjective of a verbal noun or of an omitted adverb of time. It also indicates that whoever lives with you in Medina is a neighbour. This has already been discussed in *al-Nisa'* [[See vol. 5, p. 183 onwards.]].

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 33, verse 63:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The people ask you about the Hour﴾. These are the ones who harmed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When they were threatened with punishment, they asked about the Hour, deeming it far-fetched and denying it, giving the impression that it would not happen.

﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with Allah﴾. That is, answer them concerning their question and say: its knowledge is with Allah. The fact that Allah has concealed its time from me does not invalidate my prophethood, and it is not a condition of a prophet that he know the unseen without being taught by Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿And what will make you know?﴾ That is, what will inform you.

﴿Perhaps the Hour is near﴾. That is, in a near time. The Prophet ﷺ said: "I was sent, and the Hour is like these two," and he pointed to the index finger and the middle finger. It was narrated by the people of the Sahih (authentic collections).

It has also been said: the meaning is "The Hour is not near," so the feminine marker (ta' marbuta) has been dropped, going with the Hour to the Day, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good﴾ [al-A'raf: 56], and He did not say "qariba," going with the mercy to pardon, since its feminine form is not original. This has already been discussed in full [[See vol. 7, p. 227.]].

It has also been said: Allah concealed the time of the Hour only so that the servant would be prepared for it at every moment.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 33, verses 64–65:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers﴾, meaning He has expelled them and removed them far away. Al-la'n (cursing) is expulsion and removal from mercy. Its explanation has already passed in "al-Baqarah" [[See vol. 2, p. 25.]].

(And He has prepared for them a blazing fire (sa'ir), abiding therein forever.) He made al-sa'ir feminine because it means the Fire (al-nar).

(They will find no protector (waliyy) or helper (nasir).) Someone who would save them from the punishment of Allah and from remaining in it forever.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 33, verses 66–67:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿On the Day when their faces are turned over in the Fire﴾. The recitation of the common readers (al-'amma) is with a ḍamma on the tā' and a fatḥa on the lām, in the passive form (al-fi'l al-majhul), "tuqallabu" (تُقَلَّبُ). ʿIsa al-Hamdani and Ibn Ishaq read "nuqallibu" (نُقَلِّبُ) with a nūn and a kasra on the lām, and "wujūhahum" (وُجُوهَهُمْ) in the accusative. ʿIsa also read "tuqallibu" (تُقَلِّبُ) with a ḍamma on the tā' and a kasra on the lām, meaning that the Blaze turns their faces over. This turning (taqlib) is a change of their colours by the scorching of the Fire, so they become black at one time and green at another. And when their skins are replaced with other skins, then they will wish that they had not disbelieved (﴿They will say: "Oh, would that we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger!"﴾). It is also possible that the meaning is: they will say, on the Day when their faces are turned over in the Fire, "Oh, would that we had..."

﴿...and obeyed the Messenger﴾: that is, we did not disbelieve and so be saved from this punishment as the believers were saved. This alif falls at the ends of verses (al-fawasil), so one pauses upon it and does not connect it to what follows. Likewise "al-sabila" (السَّبِيلَا), which has passed at the beginning of the surah [see p. 145 of this part]. Al-Hasan read "Inna ati'na sadatana" (إنا أطعنا سَادَاتِنَا) with a kasra on the tā', the plural of "sadah" (سادة). In this there is a warning against blind following (taqlid). "Al-sadah" is the plural of "al-sayyid," which is of the pattern fa'alah, like kataba and fajara. "Sadatuna" is a plural of the plural. "Al-sadah" and "al-kubara'" have the same meaning. Qatada said: they are those who fed (the people) at the Battle of Badr. The more apparent view is that it is general, referring to the leaders and chiefs in polytheism and misguidance: that is, "we obeyed them in disobeying You and in what they called us to." ﴿...and they led us astray from the way﴾: that is, away from the way, which is monotheism (al-tawhid). When the preposition was removed, the verb reached its object and was put in the accusative. Misguidance (al-idlal) does not transitively take two objects without the intermediary of a preposition, as in His saying: "He indeed led me astray from the Reminder" [al-Furqan: 92] [see vol. 13, p. 25 onward].

"His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, give them double the punishment from the Fire﴾. Qatadah said: "The punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter." It was also said: "The punishment of disbelief and the punishment of misguiding others," meaning: punish them twice as much as You punish us, for they went astray and led others astray.

(And curse them with a great curse.) Ibn Mas'ud and his companions, Yahya and 'Asim read it with the letter bā' (kabīran, "great"), while the rest read it with the letter thā' (kathīran, "many"). Abu Hatim, Abu 'Ubayd and al-Nahhas preferred this reading, based on His saying: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah curses, and the cursers curse﴾ [al-Baqarah: 159], and this meaning is common. Muhammad ibn Abi al-Sarri said: "I saw in a dream as if I was in the mosque of 'Asqalan, and as if a man was debating with me about those who hate the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ). He said: 'And curse them with a great curse (la'nan kathiran),' and then he repeated it until he vanished from me, and he would not say it except with the thā'." The reading with the bā' returns in meaning to the thā', because whatever is great is also many and of immense magnitude.

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the hypocrites and the disbelievers who harmed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers, He warned the believers against exposing themselves to harm, and forbade them from imitating the Children of Israel in their harming of their prophet Musa (Moses). People differed over what Muhammad (ﷺ) and Musa were harmed with. Al-Naqqash reported that the harm done to Muhammad (peace be upon him) was their saying: "Zayd ibn Muhammad." Abu Wa'il said: his harm was that he (ﷺ) distributed a portion, and a man from the Ansar said: "This distribution was not intended for the sake of Allah's countenance." This was reported to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he became angry and said: "May Allah have mercy on Musa. He was harmed with more than this, and he was patient."

As for the harm done to Musa (peace be upon him), Ibn Abbas and a group said: it is what is contained in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), namely that he said: "The Children of Israel used to bathe naked, and Musa, peace be upon him, used to cover himself much and conceal his body. So some people said: 'He has a hernia (adar, a swelling of the scrotum) [[al-adarah (on the pattern of al-ghurfah): a swelling of the testicles.]], or he has leprosy, or he has some defect.' So one day he went out to bathe in a spring in the land of Syria, and he placed his garments on a rock, and the rock fled with his garments. Musa followed it naked, saying: 'My garment, O rock! My garment, O rock!' [[i.e., leave my garment, O rock.]] until he reached a gathering of the Children of Israel, and they saw him, and he was the most beautiful of them in form and the most proportioned in appearance, and he did not have what they claimed. So this is the statement of Allah, blessed and exalted: 'So Allah cleared him of what they said.'" Al-Bukhari and Muslim reported it with this meaning.

The wording of Muslim is: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Children of Israel used to bathe naked, looking at one another's private parts, and Musa, peace be upon him, used to bathe alone. So they said: 'By Allah, nothing prevents Musa from bathing with us except that he has a hernia.' He said: So one day he went to bathe and placed his garment on a rock, and the rock fled with his garment. He said: So Musa, peace be upon him, ran [[in Muslim: "once".]] [[jama, ran at full speed.]] after it, saying: 'My garment, O rock! My garment, O rock!' until the Children of Israel looked at Musa's private parts and said: 'By Allah, there is no defect in Musa.' Then the rock stopped until he looked at it. He said: So he took his garment and began striking the rock." Abu Hurayrah said: "By Allah, on the rock there are six or seven marks (nadab) from Musa's striking it." [[al-nadab (with a vowel on the first letter): a mark of a wound that has not risen above the skin, so the mark of the striking on the rock is likened to it.]]

This is one view. It is also reported from Ibn Abbas, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "They harmed Musa by saying: 'He killed Harun.' That was because Musa and Harun went out to the wilderness of al-Tih [[Yaqut said: al-fahs is every place that is inhabited, whether plain or mountain, on condition that it can be cultivated. Al-Tih is the place where Musa ibn Imran, peace be upon him, and his people went astray. It is a land between Aqabah (Ayla) and Egypt and the Red Sea (Bahr al-Qulzum). It is now the centre of the Sinai Peninsula.]], and Harun died there. Then Musa came, and the Children of Israel said to Musa: 'You killed him, and he was gentler to us than you and more loving.' So they harmed him with that. Allah, exalted is He, commanded the angels, and they carried him and passed him around among the Children of Israel, and they saw a great sign that indicated the truthfulness of Musa, and there was no trace of killing on him." It has also been said: the angels spoke of his death, and no one knew the location of his grave except the vulture (rakham), and Allah, exalted is He, made him deaf and mute. Harun died before Musa in the wilderness, and Musa died two months before the end of the period of the wandering.

Al-Qushayri reported from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that Allah, exalted is He, brought Harun back to life, and he informed them that he had not killed him, and then he died.

It has also been said that the harm done to Musa, peace be upon him, was their accusing him of sorcery and madness. The first view is the sound one. It is possible that they did all of that, and Allah cleared him of all of it.

Issue: Musa, peace be upon him, placing his garment on the rock and entering the water naked is evidence for the permissibility of that, and this is the position of the majority. Ibn Abi Layla prohibited it, and he argued with a hadith that is not authentic, namely his (ﷺ) saying: "Do not enter the water except with a waist-wrap, for the water has inhabitants." Qadi Iyad said: it is weak according to the people of knowledge. I say: As for the recommendation of covering oneself, it is supported by what Isra'il reported from Abd al-A'la, that al-Hasan ibn Ali entered a pool with a cloak wrapped around himself, and when he came out he was asked about it, and he said: "I only covered myself from one who sees me and whom I do not see," meaning from my Lord and the angels.

If it is asked: How did Musa, peace be upon him, call out to the rock with a call addressed to one who understands? It is answered: Because a deed of one who understands proceeded from the rock. "Hajar" (rock) is a singular vocative noun with the vocative particle omitted, as Allah said: ﴿Yusuf, turn away from this﴾ [Yusuf: 29] [[See vol. 9, p. 175.]]. "Thawbi" (my garment) is in the accusative by a hidden verb; the estimate is: "Give me my garment," or "Leave my garment," so the verb was omitted because the situation indicates it.

As for Allah's statement: ﴿and he was honourable (wajih) in the sight of Allah﴾, that means: great. In the usage of the Arabs, "wajih" means one of great rank and high status. It is related that whenever he asked Allah for something, Allah gave it to him. Ibn Mas'ud recited: "and he was a servant of Allah." It has also been said: the meaning of "wajihan" is that Allah spoke to him directly.

Abu Bakr al-Anbari said in (Kitab al-Radd): One who attacked the Qur'an claimed that the Muslims had altered "wakana 'inda Allahi wajihan" and that the correct reading in his view was "wakana 'abdan lillahi wajihan." This indicates the weakness of his aim, the deficiency of his understanding, and the scantiness of his knowledge. For if the verse were read as he suggested, "and he was a servant," the praise of Musa, peace be upon him, would be diminished. This is because "wajih" could refer to standing among worldly people, among people of his time, and among people of the Hereafter, so the place of praise would not be fixed. If he were honoured among worldly people, that would be a favour from Allah to him, and no praise from Allah would be manifest in it. But when Allah clarified the place of praise by saying "and he was honourable in the sight of Allah," he earned nobility and the greatest elevation, because honour is with Allah. Whoever changes the wording has deprived the Prophet of Allah of the most excellent praise and the greatest commendation.

O you who believe, fear Allah and speak words of appropriate correctness (sadid), [Qur'an 33:70]. That is, straightforward and true. Ibn 'Abbas said: that is, right (sawab). Qatadah and Muqatil said: meaning, speak words of rectitude concerning the matter of Zaynab and Zayd, and do not attribute to the Prophet (ﷺ) what is not lawful for him. 'Ikrimah and Ibn 'Abbas also said: the word of sadad is "There is no god but Allah." It was also said: it is that whose outward matches its inward. It was also said: it is that which is intended for the sake of Allah's countenance alone, not for anything else. It was also said: it is reconciliation between those who are quarrelling. It is derived from making an arrow straight (tasdid al-sahm) so that the target is hit. The word of sadad encompasses all good, so it is general to all that has been mentioned and to other things besides. The apparent meaning of the verse indicates that it points only to what would be the opposite of the harm that was spoken concerning the Messenger and the believers. Then the Mighty and Majestic promised that He would reward the word of sadad with the rectification of deeds and the forgiveness of sins, and that is sufficient for you as a rank and an elevation of station.

(And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger) — that is, in what He commands and what He forbids — (has indeed attained a great achievement).

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 33, verses 72–73 (part 1 of 2):

When Allah, the Exalted, had explained in this surah the rulings He explained, He commanded adherence to His commands.

The trust (al-amanah) encompasses all the duties of the religion according to the sound opinions, and this is the view of the majority (al-jumhur) of scholars.

Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim Abu 'Abd Allah narrated:

Isma'il ibn Nasr narrated to us from Salih ibn 'Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn Yazid [[In sources Sh and K: "Muhammad ibn Zayd," and we have not found a correction of it.]] ibn Jawhar, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Allah the Exalted said to Adam: 'O Adam, I offered the trust to the heavens and the earth, but they could not bear it. Will you bear it with what is in it?' He said: 'And what is in it, O Lord?' He said: 'If you bear it, you will be rewarded, and if you neglect it, you will be punished.' So he bore it with what is in it, and he did not remain in Paradise except for the time between the first prayer and the afternoon prayer, until Satan drove him out of it."

Therefore, the trust is the obligations which Allah entrusted to His servants.

There are differing opinions on the details of some of them. Ibn Mas'ud said: It refers to the trusts concerning wealth, such as deposits and others.

It is also reported from him that it refers to all obligations, and the most serious of them as a trust is wealth.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: Among the trust is that a woman is entrusted with her private part.

Abu al-Darda' said: The ritual bath from major impurity (ghusl al-janabah) is a trust, and Allah the Exalted did not entrust the son of Adam with anything of His religion other than it.

In a hadith traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) [marfu'], it says: "The trust is the prayer." If you wish, you may say, "I have prayed," and if you wish, you may say, "I have not prayed."

Likewise, the fast and the ritual bath from major impurity.

'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As said: The first thing Allah the Exalted created in the human being was his private part, and He said: "This is a trust that I have deposited with you, so do not squander it except in its rightful manner."

"So if you guard it, I shall guard you. The private part is a trust, the ear is a trust, the eye is a trust, the tongue is a trust, the belly is a trust, the hand is a trust, and the foot is a trust. And there is no faith for one who has no trustworthiness."

[[The wording of this sentence is as it appears in the manuscripts of the original. What is in Nawadir al-Usul is: "fa-la tabsil minha shay'an illa bi-haqqiha" (do not give up any of it except in its right). The word "ibsal" here means neglect, and this is the narration of al-Durr al-Manthur, which says: "fa-la tudayyi'uha illa fi haqqiha" (do not neglect it except in its right). One says: "absaltu fulanan" when I delivered him to destruction.]]

Al-Suddi said: It refers to Adam's entrusting his son Qabil with his offspring and his family, and his betrayal of that trust in killing his brother.

That is because Allah the Exalted said to him: "O Adam, do you know that I have a House on the earth?" He said: "No, O Lord." He said: "Indeed, I have a House in Makkah, so go to it." Then he said to the heaven: "Guard my son with the trust," but it refused. He said to the earth: "Guard my son with the trust," and it refused. He said the same to the mountains, and they refused. Then he said to Qabil: "Guard my son with the trust." He said: "Yes, go and return, and you will find your son as pleases you." So he returned and found that he had killed his brother. That is the meaning of His statement, blessed and exalted: "Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it..." — to the end of the verse.

Ma'mar narrated from al-Hasan that the trust was offered to the heavens, the earth and the mountains. They said: "And what is in it?" It was said to them: "If you do well, you will be rewarded, and if you do evil, you will be punished." They said: "No."

Mujahid said: When Allah created Adam, He offered it to him. He said: "And what is it?" He said: "If you do well, I will reward you, and if you do evil, I will punish you." He said: "Then I have taken it upon myself, O Lord."

Mujahid said: The time between his taking it upon himself and his being removed from Paradise was no more than the time between noon and the afternoon.

'Ali ibn Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His statement, the Exalted: "Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains," that he said: "The trust is the obligations. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, offered it to the heavens, the earth and the mountains. If they fulfilled it, He would reward them, and if they neglected it, He would punish them."

So they disliked that and feared it, without any disobedience, but out of glorification of the religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that they should not stand up to it.

Then He offered it to Adam, and he accepted it with what is in it.

Al-Nahhas said: This is the view upon which the people of tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis) rely.

It has also been said: When death approached Adam (peace be upon him), he was commanded to offer the trust to creation, so he offered it, and none accepted it except his children.

It has also been said: This trust is what Allah the Exalted deposited in the heavens, the earth, the mountains and creation, of the proofs of His lordship, that they should manifest it, and they manifested it, except for the human being, who concealed it and denied it. Some of the speakers (of kalam) said this.

The meaning of "offered" (ʿaradna) is "made manifest," as you say: "I displayed the slave girl for sale."

The meaning is: Indeed, We offered the trust and its loss to the people of the heavens and the people of the earth, from the angels, humans and jinn. "So they refused to bear it" — meaning, they refused to bear its burden, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens and burdens along with their burdens﴾ [Al-'Ankabut: 13]. [[See vol. 13, p. 330 onward.]]

"And man bore it." Al-Hasan said: The intended meaning is the disbeliever and the hypocrite.

"Indeed, he was a wrongdoer" to himself, "ignorant" of his Lord.

On this answer, it is then a metaphor (majaz), like: ﴿And ask the town﴾ [Yusuf: 82]. [[See vol. 9, p. 245 onward.]]

There is another answer in which it is taken in its literal sense (haqiqa): that He actually offered the trust and its loss to the heavens, the earth and the mountains, namely the reward and punishment. That is, He made this manifest to them, so they did not bear its burden, and they were fearful and said: "We do not seek reward or punishment." Each of them said: "This is a matter we cannot bear, but we are listeners to You and obedient in what we are commanded and subjected to." This was said by al-Hasan and others.

The scholars said: It is known that inanimate matter does not understand and does not answer, so on the last view it is necessary to assume life.

And this offering is an offering of choice, not of compulsion.

Offering to the human being, however, is compulsion.

Al-Qaffal and others said: The offering in this verse is a parable (darb mathal), meaning that the heavens and the earth, despite the greatness of their bodies, if they were such that they could be made responsible, the bearing of the laws would be too heavy for them because of the reward and punishment in it. That is, the obligation is a matter that the heavens, the earth and the mountains should be unable to bear, yet the human being has been charged with it, and he is a wrongdoer and ignorant, if he had understood.

This is like His statement: "Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain..." [Al-Hashr: 21] [[See vol. 18, p. 44.]] — then He said: ﴿And these parables We set forth for the people﴾ [Al-Hashr: 21].

Al-Qaffal said: Since it is established that He, the Exalted, sets forth parables, and there has come to us a report that cannot be understood except as a parable, it is obligatory to interpret it that way.

Some people said: The verse is figurative (majaz), meaning: When we compare the weight of the trust with the strength of the heavens, the earth and the mountains, we see that they cannot bear it, and that if they could speak, they would refuse and be fearful. So He expressed this meaning by His statement: "Indeed, We offered the trust..." — to the end of the verse.

This is like when you say: "I offered the load to the camel and it refused," while you mean: "I measured its strength against the weight of the load, and I saw that it fell short of it."

It has also been said: "We offered" means "We compared" the leadership (al-imamah) with the heavens, the earth and the mountains, so these things were too weak for the trust, and the trust outweighed them by its weight.

It has also been said: The offering of the trust to the heavens, the earth and the mountains was only from Adam (peace be upon him).

That is because when Allah, the Exalted, made him His successor over his descendants, and gave him power over all that is on the earth of livestock, birds and beasts, and made a covenant with him in which He commanded and forbade him, and made lawful and unlawful, he accepted it and never ceased to act upon it.

When death approached him, he asked Allah to inform him who would succeed him after him, and to entrust him with the trust that he himself had been entrusted with. So He commanded him to offer this to the heavens, on the condition that was taken from him: reward if he obeyed and punishment if he disobeyed. They refused to accept it out of fear [[Ash-shafaq and al-ishfaq: fear.]] of Allah's punishment.

Then He commanded him to offer it to the earth and all the mountains, and they refused it.

Then He commanded him to offer it to his children, and he offered it to them, and they accepted it on the condition. He did not take on what the heavens, the earth and the mountains had shrunk from.

"Indeed, he was a wrongdoer" to himself, "ignorant" of the consequence of what he had taken on for his Lord.

Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Ali said:

I am amazed at this speaker. From where did he bring this story?

If we look at the reports, we find them contrary to what he said. If we look at its outward meaning, we find it contrary to what he said. And if we look at its inward meaning, we find it far from what he said!

That is because he repeated the mention of the trust without mentioning what the trust is, except that in his statement he alludes to the fact that He gave him power over everything on the earth, and that Allah made a covenant with him in which was His command, His prohibition, His lawful and His unlawful. He claimed that He commanded him to offer this to the heavens, the earth and the mountains. So what do the heavens, the earth and the mountains do with the lawful and the unlawful?

And what is the power over the livestock, the birds and the beasts?

And how, when he offered it to his child and he accepted it, does it become a burden on the necks of his descendants after him?

In the beginning of the account in the revelation, He offered the trust to the heavens, the earth and the mountains until their refusal became manifest. Then He mentioned that the human being took it on, that is, of his own accord, not that it was imposed upon him. So He called him "wrongdoer," that is, to himself, "ignorant" of what it entailed.

As for the reports which contradict what has been mentioned, my father, may Allah have mercy on him, told me: al-Faydh ibn al-Fadl al-Kufi narrated to us: al-Sarri ibn Isma'il narrated to us from 'Amir al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said:

When Allah created the trust, He made a likeness of it as a rock. Then He placed it where He willed. Then He called upon the heavens, the earth and the mountains to carry it, and said to them: "Indeed, this is the 'trust,' and for it is reward, and against it is punishment." They said: "O Lord, we have no strength for it." Then the human being approached, before he was called, and said to the heavens, the earth and the mountains: "What is your standing?" They said: "Our Lord called us to carry this, and we feared it and could not bear it." He said: "Then he moved it with his hand and said: 'By Allah, if I willed to carry it, I would carry it.' So he carried it until he brought it up to his knees. Then he put it down and said: 'By Allah, if I willed to increase, I would have increased.' They said: 'It is yours!' So he carried it until he brought it up to his loins [[Al-hiqw (with a fatha or kasra on the ha'): the flank.]]. Then he put it down and said: 'By Allah, if I willed to increase, I would have increased.' They said: 'It is yours!' So he carried it until he placed it upon his shoulder. When he leaned to set it down, they said: 'Stay where you are! Indeed, this is the "trust," and for it is reward and against it is punishment. Our Lord commanded us to carry it and we feared it, but you carried it without being called to it. So it is upon your neck and upon the necks of your descendants until the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, you were a wrongdoer and ignorant.'"

He also mentioned reports from the Companions and the Successors (al-tabi'un), most of which have already been mentioned.

"And man bore it," that is, he undertook to carry out its right, and in doing so he was a wrongdoer to himself.

Qatada said: "[He was] a wrongdoer" to the trust; "ignorant" of the extent of what he entered into.

This is the interpretation of Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Jubayr.

Al-Hasan said: "Ignorant" of his Lord.

He said: The meaning of "bore it" is that he betrayed it.

Al-Zajjaj said: The verse concerns the disbeliever, the hypocrite and the disobedient, each according to his degree. This is on this interpretation.

Ibn 'Abbas and his companions, al-Dahhak and others said: "The human being" is Adam. He bore the trust, but not a single day passed for him before he committed the sin that expelled him from Paradise.

It is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas that Allah, the Exalted, said to him: "Will you bear this trust with what is in it?" He said: "And what is in it?" He said:

If you do good, you will be rewarded; and if you do evil, you will be punished.
He said:
"I will carry it with what is in it, between my ear and my shoulder."
So Allah the Exalted said to him:
"Indeed I will help you. I have made for your sight a veil, so shut it from what is not lawful for you, and for your private part a garment, so do not uncover it except for what I have made lawful for you."
And a people said:
"Al-insan" refers to the whole species.
This is good, along with the generality of the trust (amanah), as we mentioned at the beginning.
And al-Suddi said:
"Al-insan" is Qabil.
But Allah knows best.

(So that Allah may punish the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women.) The lam in "li-yu'adhdhiba" (so that He may punish) is connected to "hamala" (He bore it), meaning: He bore it so that He would punish the disobedient and reward the obedient. Thus it is the lam of causation (lam al-ta'lil), because punishment is the result of bearing the trust. It was also said that it is connected to "'aradna" (We offered), meaning: We offered the trust to all of them, then We entrusted it to the human being so that the polytheism of the polytheist and the hypocrisy of the hypocrite would become manifest, so that Allah would punish them, and the faith of the believer, so that Allah would reward him.

(And Allah turns in forgiveness to them.) The reading of al-Hasan is with the nominative (wa-yatuba), cutting it off from what precedes, meaning: Allah turns to them in forgiveness in every case.

(And Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful.) It is a predicate following a predicate for "kana" (was). It may also be an adjective for "Ghafur" (Forgiving), and it may also be a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun (implied in the verb). And Allah knows best what is correct.
