That is the meaning of His statement, blessed and exalted: "Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it..." — to the end of the verse.

Ma'mar narrated from al-Hasan that the trust was offered to the heavens, the earth and the mountains. They said: "And what is in it?" It was said to them: "If you do well, you will be rewarded, and if you do evil, you will be punished." They said: "No."

Mujahid said: When Allah created Adam, He offered it to him. He said: "And what is it?" He said: "If you do well, I will reward you, and if you do evil, I will punish you." He said: "Then I have taken it upon myself, O Lord."

Mujahid said: The time between his taking it upon himself and his being removed from Paradise was no more than the time between noon and the afternoon.

'Ali ibn Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His statement, the Exalted: "Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains," that he said: "The trust is the obligations. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, offered it to the heavens, the earth and the mountains. If they fulfilled it, He would reward them, and if they neglected it, He would punish them."

So they disliked that and feared it, without any disobedience, but out of glorification of the religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that they should not stand up to it.

Then He offered it to Adam, and he accepted it with what is in it.

Al-Nahhas said: This is the view upon which the people of tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis) rely.

It has also been said: When death approached Adam (peace be upon him), he was commanded to offer the trust to creation, so he offered it, and none accepted it except his children.

It has also been said: This trust is what Allah the Exalted deposited in the heavens, the earth, the mountains and creation, of the proofs of His lordship, that they should manifest it, and they manifested it, except for the human being, who concealed it and denied it. Some of the speakers (of kalam) said this.

The meaning of "offered" (ʿaradna) is "made manifest," as you say: "I displayed the slave girl for sale."

The meaning is: Indeed, We offered the trust and its loss to the people of the heavens and the people of the earth, from the angels, humans and jinn. "So they refused to bear it" — meaning, they refused to bear its burden, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens and burdens along with their burdens﴾ [Al-'Ankabut: 13]. [[See vol. 13, p. 330 onward.]]

"And man bore it." Al-Hasan said: The intended meaning is the disbeliever and the hypocrite.

"Indeed, he was a wrongdoer" to himself, "ignorant" of his Lord.

On this answer, it is then a metaphor (majaz), like: ﴿And ask the town﴾ [Yusuf: 82]. [[See vol. 9, p. 245 onward.]]

There is another answer in which it is taken in its literal sense (haqiqa): that He actually offered the trust and its loss to the heavens, the earth and the mountains, namely the reward and punishment. That is, He made this manifest to them, so they did not bear its burden, and they were fearful and said: "We do not seek reward or punishment." Each of them said: "This is a matter we cannot bear, but we are listeners to You and obedient in what we are commanded and subjected to." This was said by al-Hasan and others.

The scholars said: It is known that inanimate matter does not understand and does not answer, so on the last view it is necessary to assume life.

And this offering is an offering of choice, not of compulsion.

Offering to the human being, however, is compulsion.

Al-Qaffal and others said: The offering in this verse is a parable (darb mathal), meaning that the heavens and the earth, despite the greatness of their bodies, if they were such that they could be made responsible, the bearing of the laws would be too heavy for them because of the reward and punishment in it. That is, the obligation is a matter that the heavens, the earth and the mountains should be unable to bear, yet the human being has been charged with it, and he is a wrongdoer and ignorant, if he had understood.

This is like His statement: "Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain..." [Al-Hashr: 21] [[See vol. 18, p. 44.]] — then He said: ﴿And these parables We set forth for the people﴾ [Al-Hashr: 21].

Al-Qaffal said: Since it is established that He, the Exalted, sets forth parables, and there has come to us a report that cannot be understood except as a parable, it is obligatory to interpret it that way.

Some people said: The verse is figurative (majaz), meaning: When we compare the weight of the trust with the strength of the heavens, the earth and the mountains, we see that they cannot bear it, and that if they could speak, they would refuse and be fearful. So He expressed this meaning by His statement: "Indeed, We offered the trust..." — to the end of the verse.

This is like when you say: "I offered the load to the camel and it refused," while you mean: "I measured its strength against the weight of the load, and I saw that it fell short of it."

It has also been said: "We offered" means "We compared" the leadership (al-imamah) with the heavens, the earth and the mountains, so these things were too weak for the trust, and the trust outweighed them by its weight.

It has also been said: The offering of the trust to the heavens, the earth and the mountains was only from Adam (peace be upon him).

That is because when Allah, the Exalted, made him His successor over his descendants, and gave him power over all that is on the earth of livestock, birds and beasts, and made a covenant with him in which He commanded and forbade him, and made lawful and unlawful, he accepted it and never ceased to act upon it.

When death approached him, he asked Allah to inform him who would succeed him after him, and to entrust him with the trust that he himself had been entrusted with. So He commanded him to offer this to the heavens, on the condition that was taken from him: reward if he obeyed and punishment if he disobeyed. They refused to accept it out of fear [[Ash-shafaq and al-ishfaq: fear.]] of Allah's punishment.

Then He commanded him to offer it to the earth and all the mountains, and they refused it.

Then He commanded him to offer it to his children, and he offered it to them, and they accepted it on the condition. He did not take on what the heavens, the earth and the mountains had shrunk from.

"Indeed, he was a wrongdoer" to himself, "ignorant" of the consequence of what he had taken on for his Lord.

Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Ali said:

I am amazed at this speaker. From where did he bring this story?

If we look at the reports, we find them contrary to what he said. If we look at its outward meaning, we find it contrary to what he said. And if we look at its inward meaning, we find it far from what he said!

That is because he repeated the mention of the trust without mentioning what the trust is, except that in his statement he alludes to the fact that He gave him power over everything on the earth, and that Allah made a covenant with him in which was His command, His prohibition, His lawful and His unlawful. He claimed that He commanded him to offer this to the heavens, the earth and the mountains. So what do the heavens, the earth and the mountains do with the lawful and the unlawful?

And what is the power over the livestock, the birds and the beasts?

And how, when he offered it to his child and he accepted it, does it become a burden on the necks of his descendants after him?

In the beginning of the account in the revelation, He offered the trust to the heavens, the earth and the mountains until their refusal became manifest. Then He mentioned that the human being took it on, that is, of his own accord, not that it was imposed upon him. So He called him "wrongdoer," that is, to himself, "ignorant" of what it entailed.

As for the reports which contradict what has been mentioned, my father, may Allah have mercy on him, told me: al-Faydh ibn al-Fadl al-Kufi narrated to us: al-Sarri ibn Isma'il narrated to us from 'Amir al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said:

When Allah created the trust, He made a likeness of it as a rock. Then He placed it where He willed. Then He called upon the heavens, the earth and the mountains to carry it, and said to them: "Indeed, this is the 'trust,' and for it is reward, and against it is punishment." They said: "O Lord, we have no strength for it." Then the human being approached, before he was called, and said to the heavens, the earth and the mountains: "What is your standing?" They said: "Our Lord called us to carry this, and we feared it and could not bear it." He said: "Then he moved it with his hand and said: 'By Allah, if I willed to carry it, I would carry it.' So he carried it until he brought it up to his knees. Then he put it down and said: 'By Allah, if I willed to increase, I would have increased.' They said: 'It is yours!' So he carried it until he brought it up to his loins [[Al-hiqw (with a fatha or kasra on the ha'): the flank.]]. Then he put it down and said: 'By Allah, if I willed to increase, I would have increased.' They said: 'It is yours!' So he carried it until he placed it upon his shoulder. When he leaned to set it down, they said: 'Stay where you are! Indeed, this is the "trust," and for it is reward and against it is punishment. Our Lord commanded us to carry it and we feared it, but you carried it without being called to it. So it is upon your neck and upon the necks of your descendants until the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, you were a wrongdoer and ignorant.'"

He also mentioned reports from the Companions and the Successors (al-tabi'un), most of which have already been mentioned.

"And man bore it," that is, he undertook to carry out its right, and in doing so he was a wrongdoer to himself.

Qatada said: "[He was] a wrongdoer" to the trust; "ignorant" of the extent of what he entered into.

This is the interpretation of Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Jubayr.

Al-Hasan said: "Ignorant" of his Lord.

He said: The meaning of "bore it" is that he betrayed it.

Al-Zajjaj said: The verse concerns the disbeliever, the hypocrite and the disobedient, each according to his degree. This is on this interpretation.

Ibn 'Abbas and his companions, al-Dahhak and others said: "The human being" is Adam. He bore the trust, but not a single day passed for him before he committed the sin that expelled him from Paradise.

It is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas that Allah, the Exalted, said to him: "Will you bear this trust with what is in it?" He said: "And what is in it?" He said:

If you do good, you will be rewarded; and if you do evil, you will be punished.
He said:
"I will carry it with what is in it, between my ear and my shoulder."
So Allah the Exalted said to him:
"Indeed I will help you. I have made for your sight a veil, so shut it from what is not lawful for you, and for your private part a garment, so do not uncover it except for what I have made lawful for you."
And a people said:
"Al-insan" refers to the whole species.
This is good, along with the generality of the trust (amanah), as we mentioned at the beginning.
And al-Suddi said:
"Al-insan" is Qabil.
But Allah knows best.

(So that Allah may punish the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women.) The lam in "li-yu'adhdhiba" (so that He may punish) is connected to "hamala" (He bore it), meaning: He bore it so that He would punish the disobedient and reward the obedient. Thus it is the lam of causation (lam al-ta'lil), because punishment is the result of bearing the trust. It was also said that it is connected to "'aradna" (We offered), meaning: We offered the trust to all of them, then We entrusted it to the human being so that the polytheism of the polytheist and the hypocrisy of the hypocrite would become manifest, so that Allah would punish them, and the faith of the believer, so that Allah would reward him.

(And Allah turns in forgiveness to them.) The reading of al-Hasan is with the nominative (wa-yatuba), cutting it off from what precedes, meaning: Allah turns to them in forgiveness in every case.

(And Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful.) It is a predicate following a predicate for "kana" (was). It may also be an adjective for "Ghafur" (Forgiving), and it may also be a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun (implied in the verb). And Allah knows best what is correct.
